# Project Requirements: aTrainingTracker

This document tracks all functional and non-functional requirements of the project. Every code change must be traceable to a requirement defined here.

Tapping the action SHALL invoke `navigateToDrawerItem(R.id.drawer_my_sensors)`.<br>• Once displayed, the alert SHALL be cleared via `WorkoutNavigationEvents.consumeLowBatteryAlert()` to prevent duplicate popups upon recomposition.<br>4. *Persistent Android System Notification*:<br>• The system SHALL post an Android system notification on a dedicated notification channel `NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL__SENSOR_BATTERY` (`"NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL__SENSOR_BATTERY"`, importance `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT`).<br>• Notification ID: `NOTIFICATION_ID_SENSOR_BATTERY = 4300`.<br>• Title: Localized `R.string.sensor_battery_notification_title_1` or `R.string.sensor_battery_notification_title_many`.<br>• Text: Localized sensor name(s) and battery percentage.<br>• Tap Action: PendingIntent targeting `MainActivityWithNavigation` with extra `SELECTED_FRAGMENT = SelectedFragment.SENSORS.name` / `EXTRA_DRAWER_ITEM_ID = R.id.drawer_my_sensors` to launch directly into "Meine Sensoren" with `EXTRA_FILTER_CRITICAL_BATTERY = true`.<br>• Behavior: `setAutoCancel(true)`, persisting across screen sleep and lock screen until dismissed or tapped.<br>5. *Normal Battery Neutrality*:<br>• When all sensors active in the workout have battery $> 20\%$ (or if no remote sensors were connected), the system SHALL NOT post any system notification or in-app Snackbar.<br>6. *100% 9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• All notification channel names, descriptions, notification titles, notification text, snackbar messages, and action buttons SHALL maintain 100% parity across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, telemetry.batteryPercentage else knownDevice.batteryPercentage`, immediately propagating live battery levels into `mergedDevices` StateFlow.<br>• In `DeviceDataRepository.kt`, when stream is inactive or upon sensor disconnection.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-CON-007` (*Notify user about low battery ## 2. Sensor Data Processing & Filtering

|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **REQ-FIL-001** | Flexible filtering (Moving Avg, Exponential Smoothing). | Allow for smooth visualization of noisy sensor data. | `FilterManager.java` | `TST-UNT-004` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-002** | Configurable smoothing factors (α) for Power. | Balance responsiveness vs. stability. | `ExponentialSmoothingFilter.java` | `TST-UNT-005` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-003** | Calculate derived metrics (VAM, slope, pace). | Provide advanced metrics for climbing and analysis. | `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java` | `TST-UNT-002` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-004** | **Atomic Altitude Correction.** | The system SHALL apply altitude corrections from known locations atomically across all data structures. This MUST include shifting previous sample points, updating summary extrema (Min/Max), and recalculating total ascent/descent for the active workout to ensure 100% data consistency. | `TrackerService.java`, `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java` | `TST-FIL-003` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-005** | Implement "Proxy Sensors" and "Accumulator Sensors". | Extensible architecture for complex multi-sensor data. | `ProxySensor.java` | `TST-STR-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-006** | Geographical rolling averages for start altitude. | Filter out momentary GPS or barometric jitter. | `WorkoutSamplesDatabaseManager.java`| `TST-STR-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-012** | **Stabilized VAM (Vertical Speed) Metric, Location Accuracy Gating & Indoor Drift Suppression Architecture.** | The system SHALL calculate the vertical ascent/descent rate (VAM / Vertical Speed in m/h) in `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice` using linear regression slope smoothing over a sliding window, suppress indoor GPS wander and stationary drift, enforce location accuracy gating, maintain a noise deadband, and reject outlier anomalies (ATT-1621, ATT-1738):<br>1. *Sliding Window Linear Regression Derivative ($N = 15$ seconds)*:<br>• The system SHALL maintain an equidistant 1-second circular buffer of up to $N = 15$ recent altitude samples.<br>• For a full buffer of $N = 15$ samples, the ascent rate slope $\hat{\beta}$ (in m/s) SHALL be evaluated using least-squares linear regression: $\hat{\beta} = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} w_k \cdot a_k$ where $w_k = \frac{k - \frac{N-1}{2}}{\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} (j - \frac{N-1}{2})^2}$, minimizing total squared error across all samples in the window.<br>• For an initial buffer with $M$ samples ($2 \le M < 15$), the system SHALL evaluate the least-squares slope dynamically over the available $M$ points, enabling immediate responsiveness during warm-up without artificial startup delay.<br>• The unconstrained vertical speed in m/h SHALL be computed as $\text{raw\_vam} = \hat{\beta} \times 3600$.<br>2. *Location Accuracy Gating ($> 20.0\text{ m}$)*:<br>• The system SHALL query horizontal accuracy (`SensorType.ACCURACY`) via `cAccuracyFilter = new FilterData(null, SensorType.ACCURACY, FilterType.INSTANTANEOUS, 1)`.<br>• If GPS accuracy is degraded ($> 20.0\text{ m}$), the system SHALL suppress the calculated vertical speed to `0 m/h` to reject multipath altitude jitter in indoor, basement, or canyon environments.<br>3. *Stationary Gating & Low-Speed Drift Damping*:<br>• The system SHALL query horizontal speed `speed_mps` from `speedFilteredSensorData` and the dynamic minimum speed threshold `minSpeed = SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper.getSlopeMinSpeed(mContext)` (default `0.5` m/s).<br>• If the athlete is stationary (`speed_mps < minSpeed` or `speed_mps < 0.5` m/s):<br>  - If the calculated vertical ascent rate is within typical stationary sensor noise ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$, corresponding to $|\Delta h| < 0.2\text{ m}$ over 5s), the system SHALL clamp vertical speed to `0 m/h`.<br>  - If genuine vertical displacement occurs while stationary in the horizontal plane ($|\text{raw\_vam}| \ge 150\text{ m/h}$, such as an elevator, ski lift, or vertical climbing wall), the system SHALL broadcast the measured vertical speed.<br>• If the athlete is moving at low drift/walking speeds ($0.5\text{ m/s} \le \text{speed\_mps} < 1.2\text{ m/s}$):<br>  - The system SHALL enforce an elevated drift deadband ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$ clamped to `0 m/h`), preventing phantom GPS wander speeds from triggering false climbing rates.<br>4. *Flat Terrain Athletic Noise Deadband*:<br>• When the athlete is moving horizontally at athletic speed ($\text{speed\_mps} \ge 1.2\text{ m/s}$) with valid GPS accuracy ($\le 20.0\text{ m}$), if $|\text{raw\_vam}| < 35\text{ m/h}$, the system SHALL clamp vertical speed to `0 m/h` to eliminate barometric ripple on flat terrain.<br>5. *Outlier & Physical Boundary Clamping*:<br>• The calculated vertical speed SHALL be clamped to the range $[-3000, 3000]\text{ m/h}$ to prevent single-tick GPS multipath altitude jumps from corrupting downstream recording.<br>6. *Preservation of Invariants*:<br>• `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast integer values in m/h at 1-second intervals.<br>• Accumulator sensors `SensorType.ASCENT` and `SensorType.DESCENT` using `cAltitudeSuperFilter` SHALL remain completely unaffected.<br>• `SLOPE` calculation using `getSlopeMinSpeed(mContext)` SHALL remain completely unaffected.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-FIL-003` (*Calculate derived metrics: VAM, slope, pace*), implemented in `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.5 (ATT-1621), refined in Sprint 2026-40.6 (ATT-1738).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Stationary gating in ATT-1621 assumed horizontal speed drops below $0.5\text{ m/s}$ when stationary. However, in indoor/basement testing, GPS multipath wander was found to generate phantom horizontal speed ($0.6\text{–}1.5\text{ m/s}$) and large altitude jumps ($\pm 5\text{–}15\text{ m}$), bypassing the stationary check and amplifying noise into erratic $\pm 800\dots 2400\text{ m/h}$ swings.<br>4. *Refinement Reason*: Introducing location accuracy gating ($> 20.0\text{ m}$) and low-speed drift damping ($< 1.2\text{ m/s}$) to suppress indoor GNSS wander while preserving genuine outdoor athletic climbs and elevator/lift vertical movements.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: 1-second emission periodicity, integer m/h units, accumulator integration, and slope calculation invariants are 100% preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete stationary indoors or in a basement with degraded GPS accuracy ($> 20.0\text{ m}$),<br>• *When* GPS altitude fluctuates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast `0 m/h` without jumping to phantom positive or negative values.<br>• *Given* an athlete indoors with phantom GPS wander speed ($0.6\text{–}1.1\text{ m/s}$) but minor vertical jitter ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast `0 m/h`.<br>• *Given* an athlete climbing steadily at 800 m/h ($0.222\text{ m/s}$ vertical speed) with horizontal speed $> 1.2\text{ m/s}$ and accuracy $\le 20.0\text{ m}$,<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* calculated VAM SHALL smoothly converge to $800 \pm 15\text{ m/h}$ and maintain stability without erratic second-by-second swings exceeding $\pm 20\text{ m/h}$.<br>• *Given* an athlete in an elevator or ski lift moving vertically at $\ge 150\text{ m/h}$ while horizontal speed is $< 0.5\text{ m/s}$ and accuracy $\le 20.0\text{ m}$ (or indoor barometric fix),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* the vertical rate SHALL NOT be suppressed to 0, but accurately reflect the vertical movement.<br>• *Given* an athlete riding on a flat road where minor road vibration or barometric ripple produces $|\text{raw\_vam}| < 35\text{ m/h}$,<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL output `0 m/h`.<br>• *Given* a sudden isolated GPS altitude step anomaly (e.g. +30m jump in 1 second),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* the calculated VAM SHALL be safely clamped to $\le 3000\text{ m/h}$.<br><br>**Invariants**: 1-second emission periodicity, integer m/h units, accumulator integration, and slope calculation invariants MUST NOT be broken. | Stabilize VAM metric using 15-second least-squares linear regression slope, location accuracy gating, low-speed drift damping, flat terrain noise deadband, and outlier clamping in VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice. | `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java` | `TST-FIL-004` | Verified |

## 3. Tracking Logic & Session Management

| ID | Description | Rationale | Implementation File(s) | Verification ID | Status |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **REQ-TRK-001** | Support Start, Stop, Pause with Service persistence. | Ensure data integrity in the background. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-REG-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-002** | **Workout Lap Recording Lifecycle, Manual Splitting & Pause/Resume Neutrality.** | The system SHALL manage the lifecycle of workout laps deterministically during recording, tracking termination, and database retrieval, preventing the creation and presentation of zero-duration phantom laps:<br>1. *Pause and Resume Neutrality*: Transitioning active tracking into a paused state (`pauseTracking()`) or resuming tracking from paused (`resumeFromPaused()`) SHALL NOT broadcast `REQUEST_NEW_LAP` and SHALL NOT create, increment, or close workout laps. Active lap duration and distance accumulation SHALL pause and resume transparently with the session.<br>2. *Manual Lap Splitting Integrity*: Explicit lap requests initiated by the user (via `TrackingViewsRepository.requestNewLap()` in the tracking UI or `BUTTON_LAP` from a connected smartwatch) SHALL finalize the active lap, persist its split metrics to `Laps.db` (`saveLap(...)`), broadcast `BANALService.LAP_SUMMARY`, and initialize the subsequent sequential lap index ($N+1$).<br>3. *Workout Finalization & Termination Guards*: Upon tracking completion (`TrackerService.endWorkout()`), `createNewLap()` SHALL finalize and persist the active in-progress lap if and only if `lapTime_s > 0` or `lapDistance > 0.0`. If the active lap has zero duration and zero distance, the system SHALL discard it and MUST NOT persist it to `Laps.db`.<br>4. *Defensive Database & Receiver Validation*: `TrackerService.mLapSummaryReceiver` and `LapsDatabaseManager.saveLap(...)` SHALL reject any lap record where `timeTotal <= 0 && distanceTotal <= 0.0`, ensuring invalid or empty splits are never written to SQLite.<br>5. *Historical & Vectorized Query Sanitization*: In `LapsDatabaseManager.getLaps(workoutId)` and `getLapsForWorkouts(workoutIds)`, queries SHALL filter out legacy zero-duration records (`TIME_TOTAL_s > 0 OR DISTANCE_TOTAL_m > 0`), ensuring corrupted historical splits do not render in workout summaries (`WorkoutLaps.kt`) or export files (`TCXFileWriter.java`, `GPXFileWriter.java`).<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session with no manual lap presses,<br>• *When* the user pauses tracking, resumes tracking, pauses again, and ends the workout,<br>• *Then* `Laps.db` SHALL contain exactly 1 lap record whose duration and distance match the total active workout metrics, with zero 00:00:00 phantom laps.<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session where the user explicitly taps "New Lap" once at minute 10 and ends the workout at minute 25,<br>• *Then* `Laps.db` SHALL contain exactly 2 lap records (Lap 1 = 10 min, Lap 2 = 15 min), and zero zero-duration laps.<br>• *Given* an attempt to invoke `LapsDatabaseManager.saveLap()` with `lapTime = 0` and `lapDistance = 0.0`,<br>• *Then* the method SHALL discard the write and log a warning without inserting into `Laps.TABLE`.<br>• *Given* a database containing a historical zero-duration lap from prior app versions,<br>• *When* `LapsDatabaseManager.getLaps(workoutId)` is queried,<br>• *Then* the zero-duration lap SHALL be excluded from the returned list.<br><br>**Invariants**: Manual lap splitting (`TrackingViewsRepository`, `PebbleService`), total active time/distance calculation (`REQ-TRK-001`), live pause duration updates (`REQ-UI-038`), and TCX/GPX export schema compliance (`REQ-DAT-012`) MUST NOT be broken. | Eliminate confusing phantom zero-duration laps from workout summaries, preserve Rabbit/Hedgehog performance badge integrity, and ensure clean TCX exports by aligning pause/resume behavior with standard athletic tracking. | `TrainingApplication.java`, `TrackerService.java`, `LapsDatabaseManager.java` | `TST-TRK-002` | Verified |

| **REQ-TRK-011** | **Intelligent Workout Auto-Naming based on Recognized Start and Destination Lieblingsorte.** | The system SHALL automatically generate meaningful, localized workout names based on recognized favorite locations (*Lieblingsorte*) for recorded sessions that do not match an existing Route Cluster (ATT-1398):<br>1. *Start & Destination Location Resolution*:<br>• Upon workout finalization in `TrackerService.java`, when a session does not match an existing cluster (`suggestion == null`), the system SHALL resolve start and end coordinates (`startPosRaw`, `endPosRaw`) against `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.getMyLocation(...)`.<br>2. *Naming Heuristics*:<br>• *Round Trips (Start == Destination within geofence)*: When both start and end resolve to the same location (or $\le \text{geofence radius}$), the name SHALL format based on activity sport type:<br>  - Running (`BSportType.RUN`): Localized \"Run from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Lauf ab %1$s\").<br>  - Cycling (`BSportType.BIKE`): Localized \"Ride from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Fahrt ab %1$s\").<br>  - General / Other (`BSportType.UNKNOWN` / `CONFLICT`): Localized \"Loop from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Runde ab %1$s\").<br>• *Point-to-Point (Start != Destination, both recognized)*: When start and destination resolve to distinct locations:<br>  - Running: Localized \"Run from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Lauf von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>  - Cycling: Localized \"Ride from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Fahrt von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>  - Other: Localized \"Activity from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Aktivität von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>• *Start Only Recognized*: When only start resolves to a known location, format with single-location prefix (e.g. \"Run from %1$s\" / \"Lauf ab %1$s\").<br>• *Destination Only Recognized*: When only destination resolves, format as \"Run to %1$s\" / \"Lauf nach %1$s\".<br>• *Neither Recognized (Fallback)*: If neither start nor destination matches a known location, the system SHALL retain standard default naming (`mBaseFileName`).<br>3. *Cluster Proposal Seeding (`WorkoutClusterEngine.kt`)*:<br>• When suggesting or creating a new Route Cluster for an unclustered track that starts at a known location, the default cluster name SHALL be seeded with \"Loop from %1$s\" / \"Runde ab %1$s\" instead of generic \"Workout at YYYY-MM-DD\".<br>4. *User Sovereignty & | **REQ-TRK-013** | **GPS Speed Inactivity Watchdog, Gradual Speed Decay & Pace Nullification Architecture.** | The system SHALL monitor elapsed time since the last valid `Location` fix during active tracking and execute deterministic speed decay when location updates cease (ATT-2616):<br>1. *Location Inactivity Watchdog ($T_{\text{timeout}} = 5.0\text{ s}$)*:<br>• In `SpeedAndLocationDevice.java`, the system SHALL maintain an elapsed realtime timestamp (`mLastLocationTimestampMs`) tracking the most recent location update satisfying the GPS accuracy threshold.<br>• If elapsed time since the last valid location update reaches or exceeds 5.0 seconds ($5000\text{ ms}$), the system SHALL initiate periodic speed decay.<br>2. *Periodic Speed Decay ($1.0\text{ s}$ intervals)*:<br>• Every 1.0 second ($1000\text{ ms}$) following the 5-second timeout where location updates remain absent, the system SHALL decay active speed by 50% ($mSpeed = mSpeed \times 0.5$).<br>• When decayed speed drops below $0.1\text{ m/s}$ (or reaches 0.0), the system SHALL clamp active speed strictly to $0.0\text{ m/s}$ and publish $0.0$ to `mSpeedSensor`.<br>3. *Pace Resolution & Division-by-Zero Protection*:<br>• Whenever active speed is clamped to $0.0\text{ m/s}$ or is $< 0.1\text{ m/s}$, `mPaceSensor` SHALL emit `null` (rendering as `'--:--'` in cockpit tiles).<br>• Division-by-zero ($1.0 / 0.0$) SHALL NEVER be passed into `mPaceSensor`.<br>4. *Immediate Speed Recovery on Fresh Fix*:<br>• Upon receiving a valid new `Location` update, the watchdog timer SHALL reset, pending decay ticks SHALL be cancelled, and live speed evaluation ($mSpeed = (mSpeed + \text{speed}) / 2$) SHALL resume immediately.<br>5. *Lifecycle Cleanliness*:<br>• In `SpeedAndLocationDevice.shutDown()`, all scheduled watchdog timers/handlers SHALL be cleanly removed and released without memory leaks.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete tracking speed via GPS at 25 km/h who stops at a traffic light or enters GPS shadow,<br>• *When* 5.0 seconds elapse without receiving a valid location fix,<br>• *Then* speed SHALL begin halving every 1.0 second until clamped to 0.0 m/s.<br>• *Given* a decaying speed reaching 0.0 m/s,<br>• *When* inspected in `mSpeedSensor` and `mPaceSensor`,<br>• *Then* `mSpeedSensor` SHALL equal 0.0 m/s and `mPaceSensor` SHALL equal `null`.<br>• *Given* an inactive decaying speed state,<br>• *When* a new valid location fix is received,<br>• *Then* live speed evaluation SHALL immediately resume from the new fix without delay.<br><br>**Invariants**: Distance accumulator sensors (`mDistanceSensor`, `mLapDistanceSensor`) MUST NOT accumulate phantom distance during decay; start location and line distance MUST NOT be altered by decay ticks; broadcast intents (`NEW_LOCATION_INTENT`) MUST NOT be emitted by watchdog ticks. | Prevent frozen cockpit speed and pace metrics when athletes come to a complete stop or enter GPS shadow by decaying speed to zero after 5 seconds of location silence. | `SpeedAndLocationDevice.java` | `TST-TRK-005` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-014** | **Successive Geodesic Location Delta Fallback for Missing GPS Bearing and Speed in SpeedAndLocationDevice.** | The system SHALL calculate forward heading bearing and travel speed from the geodesic displacement and elapsed time interval between successive location fixes when incoming `Location` fixes lack explicit bearing or speed data (ATT-2467):<br>1. *Bearing Fallback Calculation (`SpeedAndLocationDevice.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL inspect `location.getBearing()`.<br>• If `location.getBearing() != 0.0f`, the reported bearing SHALL be used directly.<br>• If `location.getBearing() == 0.0f` (e.g. system test providers or hardware GNSS without heading lock):<br>  - If `mPrevLocation != null` and displacement `delta_distance > 0.5\text{ m}`, the system SHALL derive the forward initial azimuth bearing from `(mPrevLocation.bearingTo(location) + 360.0) % 360.0`.<br>  - If stationary or paused (`delta_distance \le 0.5\text{ m}`), the system SHALL retain the last valid non-null bearing (`mBearingSensor.getValue()`) to prevent the compass and map chevrons from snapping back to 0° (North).<br>  - If no previous fix exists, bearing defaults to `0.0`.<br>2. *Speed Fallback Calculation (`SpeedAndLocationDevice.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL inspect `location.getSpeed()`.<br>• If `location.getSpeed() > 0.0`, the reported speed SHALL be used directly.<br>• If `location.getSpeed() == 0.0` (e.g. mock locations without velocity attribute):<br>  - If `mPrevLocation != null` and `delta_distance > 0.1\text{ m}`, the system SHALL evaluate elapsed time `dt_ms = location.getTime() - mPrevLocation.getTime()`.<br>  - If `dt_ms > 0 && dt_ms < 30000`, the system SHALL calculate velocity as `delta_distance / (dt_ms / 1000.0)`.<br>  - Plausibility Clamping: If calculated speed $\le 70.0\text{ m/s}$ ($252\text{ km/h}$), it SHALL be accepted; teleportation or seek jumps $> 70.0\text{ m/s}$ SHALL be ignored.<br>  - Calculated speed SHALL feed into standard smoothing `mSpeed = (mSpeed + speed) / 2` and `mSpeedSensor`.<br>3. *Navigation & Route Auto-Detection Synergy (`TrackingTabsScreen.kt`)*:<br>• When dispatching location updates to `routeSelectorViewModel.onLocationChanged(location)`, the system SHALL populate `location.bearing = currentBearing.toFloat()` and `location.speed = currentSpeed.toFloat()`, ensuring `RouteAutoDetector` evaluates heading alignment without being suppressed by `!location.hasBearing()`.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Real hardware GNSS fixes providing valid bearing/speed MUST NOT be overridden.<br>• GPS watchdog inactivity decay (`REQ-TRK-013`) remains fully operational.<br>• 100% unit test pass rate across the full test suite.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-TRK-014`).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2467`, Sprint `Human_Review`. Arises because Android OS's native `cmd location providers set-test-provider-location` shell tool drops bearing and speed parameters (`IllegalArgumentException: Unknown option: --bearing`), preventing desk testing of navigation chevrons, turn cues, and fork alerts.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `SpeedAndLocationDevice` originally read `location.getBearing()` and `location.getSpeed()` directly from Android's `Location` object, assuming hardware GPS always provides them. Mock location testing revealed that without fallback delta math, heading is permanently frozen at North and speed remains at 0.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Hardware GPS fixes take absolute precedence if non-zero; watchdog timeout and decay invariants are untouched; 100% test pass rate preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active tracking session receiving location fixes with `bearing == 0.0f` and `speed == 0.0f` (e.g. from `fake_gps.py`),<br>• *When* successive fixes advance along an East-bound trajectory 7 meters apart at 1-second intervals,<br>• *Then* `SpeedAndLocationDevice` SHALL update `mBearingSensor` to `90.0°` and `mSpeedSensor` to `7.0 m/s` (smoothed: `3.5 m/s` on first move).<br>• *Given* a simulation that pauses or becomes stationary (`delta_distance \le 0.5\text{ m}`),<br>• *When* stationary fixes arrive,<br>• *Then* `mBearingSensor` SHALL retain its previous heading of `90.0°` rather than resetting to `0.0°`.<br>• *Given* a hardware GPS fix with non-zero bearing `180.0f`,<br>• *When* received,<br>• *Then* `SpeedAndLocationDevice` SHALL use the hardware bearing directly.<br><br>**Invariants**: Hardware non-zero metrics take precedence; watchdog decay preserved; 100% test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Successive geodesic location delta fallback for missing GPS bearing and speed in SpeedAndLocationDevice. | `SpeedAndLocationDevice.java`, `TrackingTabsScreen.kt` | `TST-TRK-006` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-015** | **Permission-Gated Foreground Service Types in TrackerService.** | The system SHALL dynamically evaluate held permissions before promoting `TrackerService` to an Android 14+ (API 34+) Foreground Service (ATT-2972):<br>1. *Permission Gating for FGS Types*:<br>• `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_LOCATION` SHALL always be included if `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` or `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` is granted.<br>• `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_CONNECTED_DEVICE` SHALL only be included if `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` (or `BLUETOOTH` on API < 31) is granted.<br>• `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_HEALTH` SHALL strictly be gated by verifying that the app holds `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_HEALTH` AND at least one health runtime permission (e.g. `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION`). `FINISHED = 1` guarantees that `hasUnfinishedWorkout()` evaluates to `false` on subsequent app launches, preventing false crash warning dialogs.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• export in `endWorkout()`,<br>• *When* the service tears down,<br>• *Then* `WorkoutSummaries.FINISHED = 1` SHALL still be committed and `TRACKING_FINISHED_INTENT` dispatched.<br>• *Given* a cleanly finished workout,<br>• *When* the athlete relaunches the application,<br>• *Then* `hasUnfinishedWorkout()` SHALL return `false` and `StartOrResumeDialog` SHALL NOT be shown.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite summary row integrity is strictly preserved; completion broadcasts reach MainActivityWithNavigation for automatic edit navigation. | Guarantee workout finalization and edit navigation when 0.10<br>(Sum of weights = 1.0).<br>4. *Graceful Fallback & Invariants*: If altitude position coordinates are absent on either the workout or the cluster candidate (e.g., flat routes, indoor sessions, | **REQ-LIV-005** | **Active and Approaching Live Segments Numeric Distance Prioritization.** | The system SHALL prioritize and sort active and approaching Strava Live Segments during live tracking (`TrackingViewModel.kt`) strictly by raw numeric distance values in meters (`Double`), eliminating unit-boundary sorting inversions and erratic active segment flipping caused by lexicographical string comparisons (ATT-3324, refining `REQ-LIV-003`):<br>1. *Raw Distance Representation in `LiveSegmentData` (`LiveSegmentsRepository.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL define `val remainingDistance_raw: Double = Double.MAX_VALUE` in `LiveSegmentData`.<br>• The system SHALL define `val distanceToStart_raw: Double = Double.MAX_VALUE` in `LiveSegmentData`.<br>• Default initialization SHALL be `Double.MAX_VALUE` so that uninitialized or inactive segment states naturally sort to the end.<br>2. *State-Aware Raw Distance Metric Population (`LiveSegmentsRepository.kt`)*:<br>• For `LiveSegmentStatus.APPROACHING`: `distanceToStart_raw` SHALL be populated with the athlete's along-track geodesic distance to the virtual start gate (`distanceToStart`), and `remainingDistance_raw` SHALL be populated with `liveSegment.staticData.summary.distance_raw + distanceToStart`.<br>• For `LiveSegmentStatus.ON_SEGMENT` and `LiveSegmentStatus.ON_SEGMENT_CLOSE_TO_FINISH`: `distanceToStart_raw` SHALL evaluate to `0.0`, and `remainingDistance_raw` SHALL be populated with the remaining along-track distance to the virtual finish gate (`remainingDistance`).<br>• For `LiveSegmentStatus.FINISHED`: `distanceToStart_raw` SHALL evaluate to `0.0`, `remainingDistance_raw` SHALL evaluate to `0.0`, and `segmentOffset_raw` SHALL be populated with the athlete's distance beyond the finish gate (`distanceToEnd`).<br>• For `LiveSegmentStatus.FAR_FAR_AWAY`: `distanceToStart_raw` and `remainingDistance_raw` SHALL default to `Double.MAX_VALUE`.<br>3. *Strict Numeric Sorting Comparator in `TrackingViewModel.kt`*:<br>• In `activeLiveSegments`, secondary tie-breaking SHALL evaluate strictly against raw numeric `Double` metrics:<br>  - For `LiveSegmentStatus.ON_SEGMENT` and `LiveSegmentStatus.ON_SEGMENT_CLOSE_TO_FINISH`: tie-break ascending by `it.liveData.remainingDistance_raw`.<br>  - For `LiveSegmentStatus.APPROACHING`: tie-break ascending by `it.liveData.distanceToStart_raw`.<br>  - For any other status: tie-break ascending by `it.liveData.segmentOffset_raw`.<br>• Formatted strings (`remainingDistance`, `distanceToStart`, `segmentOffset`) MUST NOT be used in the sorting comparator.<br>4. *System Invariants*:<br>• Segment progress calculation, gate crossing detection, orthogonal polyline projection (`REQ-GEO-001`), PR pacing comparison, and visual UI formatting via `DistanceFormatter` MUST NOT be altered.<br>• `LiveSegmentData` formatted string properties SHALL remain intact for Compose UI rendering.<br>• 100% full-suite unit test pass rate.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-LIV-003` (*Remaining distance/time vs PR*) and `TrackingViewModel.kt:161-175`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced during early Strava Live Segments implementation when `LiveSegmentData` was designed primarily as a presentation model for Compose UI cards.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In early development, `LiveSegmentData` was structured to bundle formatted strings (`distanceToStart`, `remainingDistance`) directly for UI rendering so composables wouldn't need formatting utilities. When writing `activeLiveSegments.sortedWith`, the author accessed `it.liveData.remainingDistance` for convenience, inadvertently triggering string ASCII comparison.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Formatted string presentation in UI cards (`SegmentHeader`, `LiveSegmentSheet`) remains 100% intact. `distanceToStart_raw` and `remainingDistance_raw` default to `Double.MAX_VALUE`, ensuring uninitialized segments sort cleanly to the end. Gate crossing, polyline orthogonal projection, PR delta math, and 100% clean-room test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* two active live segments on the same trajectory (Segment A with 995 m remaining formatted as `"995 m"`, and Segment B with 2,400 m remaining formatted as `"2.40 km"`),<br>• *When* `activeLiveSegments` comparator evaluates priority,<br>• *Then* Segment A SHALL be prioritized ahead of Segment B (995.0 < 2400.0), with zero UI card flipping.<br>• *Given* two approaching live segments (Segment A at 950 m to start gate formatted as `"950 m"`, and Segment B at 1,200 m to start gate formatted as `"1.20 km"`),<br>• *When* `activeLiveSegments` comparator evaluates priority,<br>• *Then* Segment A SHALL be prioritized ahead of Segment B (950.0 < 1200.0).<br>• *Given* any `LiveSegmentData` emitted across `APPROACHING`, `ON_SEGMENT`, `ON_SEGMENT_CLOSE_TO_FINISH`, and `FINISHED`,<br>• *When* inspecting `remainingDistance_raw` and `distanceToStart_raw`,<br>• *Then* both properties contain exact unrounded double-precision meter distances.<br>• *Given* Segment A in `ON_SEGMENT_CLOSE_TO_FINISH` and Segment B in `ON_SEGMENT`,<br>• *When* `activeLiveSegments` evaluates priority,<br>• *Then* Segment A SHALL outrank Segment B based on primary status weight (4 > 3).<br><br>**Invariants**: Gate crossing geometry, polyline projection, PR comparison, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | `LiveSegmentsRepository.kt`, `TrackingViewModel.kt` | `TST-LIV-001` | Verified |

| **REQ-EXP-008** | **Smart Asymmetric Workout Naming Strategy & Pre-Upload Duplicate Discovery for Strava.** | The system SHALL implement a smart asymmetric naming strategy and pre-upload duplicate discovery when synchronizing workouts to Strava (`StravaUploader.kt`), distinguishing fresh uploads from existing/duplicate activities:<br>1. *Pre-Upload Duplicate Discovery (Existing Activity Check)*:<br>• Before submitting a TCX file to Strava's upload endpoint (`POST /api/v3/uploads`), the system SHALL query Strava's athlete activities API (`GET /api/v3/athlete/activities?after={start - 300}&before={start + 300}`) using the workout's start timestamp (`TIME_START`).<br>• If an activity already exists on Strava within this temporal window (or if already recorded in `StravaUploadDbHelper`), the system SHALL bypass the TCX file upload entirely, preventing Strava from creating an unwanted duplicate activity in the athlete's feed. The system SHALL link the discovered Strava `activity_id` in `StravaUploadDbHelper` and immediately proceed with the duplicate reconciliation flow.<br>2. *Duplicate Reconciliation Flow (`isDuplicate == true` or existing Strava activity)*:<br>• *Strava Authority & Overwrite Protection*: When a workout already exists on Strava (via pre-upload query, local DB record, or upload duplicate error), the system SHALL NOT submit the workout name parameter (`NAME` / `"name"`) in the metadata update request (`doUpdate`). The activity title existing on Strava SHALL be preserved as authoritative and MUST NOT be overwritten by the app.<br>• *Local Database Enrichment & Strava Default Name Evaluation*: The system SHALL inspect the Strava activity name (`"name"`):<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- *Default Strava Name*: If the Strava name matches an auto-generated localized time-of-day default template (e.g., `"Radfahrt am Morgen"`, `"Lauf am Abend ⛅"`, `"Morning Ride"`, `"Afternoon Run"`), the app SHALL preserve the local name generated by the app (e.g. from route clustering or TCX tags) and SHALL NOT overwrite the local name in SQLite.<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- *Custom Strava Title*: If the Strava name is different from Strava default templates (e.g., `"Sunday Club Ride"`, `"Schwarzwald Tour"`, `"Berlin Marathon"`), the system SHALL | **REQ-EXP-022** | **GPX/TCX Export XML Well-Formedness, Garmin Schema Compliance, Downloads MIME Type & Privacy Protection.** | The system SHALL guarantee well-formed and schema-compliant XML exports for GPX and TCX formats across all workout configurations, ensure thread-safe UTC timestamp formatting, prevent public storage privacy leaks of internal upload files, and provide correct per-format MIME types and null-safe MediaStore handling (ATT-4013):<br>1. *GPX Segment State Machine & XML Well-Formedness (`GPXFileWriter.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL maintain an explicit boolean state flag `isSegmentOpen` (initially `false`).<br>• Upon encountering a new lap during sample iteration, if `isSegmentOpen` is `true`, the system SHALL emit the closing `</trkseg>` tag before opening a new track segment `<trkseg>`. If `isSegmentOpen` is `false`, the system SHALL emit `<trkseg>` directly without emitting a preceding closing tag.<br>• Setting `isSegmentOpen = true` SHALL strictly accompany the emission of `<trkseg>`.<br>• At the conclusion of cursor processing, the system SHALL emit the trailing `</trkseg>` if and only if `isSegmentOpen` is `true`. On zero-sample or empty workouts, zero closing `</trkseg>` tags SHALL be emitted.<br>• Output GPX files SHALL be 100% well-formed XML under all conditions, including cropped initial laps (`lap > 0`) and empty workouts.<br>2. *Garmin TCX v2 Schema Compliance (`TCXFileWriter.java`)*:<br>• In accordance with Garmin's official `TrainingCenterDatabasev2.xsd` schema, `<Creator xsi:type="Device_t">` SHALL be placed strictly inside `<Activity>`, positioned after `<Notes>` (if present) and before `<Extensions>`. `<Creator>` MUST NOT be rendered as a child of `<TrainingCenterDatabase>`.<br>• When `<Creator xsi:type="Device_t">` is serialized, it SHALL populate valid required schema child elements: `<Name>` (`aTrainingTracker`), `<UnitId>` (`0`), `<ProductID>` (`1`), and `<Version>` (`<VersionMajor>`, `<VersionMinor>`, `<BuildMajor>`, `<BuildMinor>` derived from `BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME` / `VERSION_CODE`).<br>• When `<Author xsi:type="Application_t">` is serialized under `<TrainingCenterDatabase>`, it SHALL populate valid required schema child elements: `<Name>` (`aTrainingTracker`), `<Build>` containing `<Version>`, `<LangID>` (`en`), and `<PartNumber>` (`000-00000-00`).<br>3. *Thread Safety & UTC Timezone (`GPXFileWriter.java`, `TCXFileWriter.java`)*:<br>• Static, mutable `SimpleDateFormat` instances (`msdfFromDb`, `msdfToXML`) SHALL be eliminated and replaced with immutable, thread-safe `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter` instances configured with explicit UTC timezone (`ZoneOffset.UTC`), preventing concurrent corruption during parallel background exports and eliminating local DST spring-forward timestamp distortions.<br>4. *Public Downloads Copying, MIME Types & Privacy Protection (`BaseExporter.java`, `BaseFileWriter.java`)*:<br>• *Preservation of User File Exports*: The system SHALL continue to copy exported workout files to the public `Downloads/` directory on Android 10+ (API 29+) for all user-initiated explicit file exports (`ExportType.FILE`: `CSV`, `TCX`, `GPX`, `FIT`, `GC`).<br>• *Internal Upload Privacy Protection*: The system SHALL NOT copy internal temporary files created solely for community uploads (`exportInfo.getFileFormat() == FileFormat.STRAVA` or `exportInfo.getExportType() == ExportType.COMMUNITY`) to the shared public `Downloads/` folder.<br>• *Per-Format MIME Types*: In `FileFormat.java`, the system SHALL define `getMimeType()` returning the standard MIME type: `GPX` -> `application/gpx+xml`, `TCX` / `STRAVA` -> `application/vnd.garmin.tcx+xml`, `FIT` -> `application/vnd.ant.fit`, `CSV` -> `text/csv`, `GC` -> `application/json`. `BaseExporter.copyFileToDownloads` SHALL query `exportInfo.getFileFormat().getMimeType()` rather than hardcoding `application/gpx+xml`.<br>• *MediaStore Insertion Null Guard*: In `copyFileToDownloads`, the system SHALL verify that `targetUri != null` before calling `resolver.openOutputStream(targetUri)`. If `targetUri` is null, it SHALL log a warning and return gracefully without throwing `NullPointerException`.<br>5. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Custom extension schemas (`att:ActivityExtension`) and naming conventions SHALL remain intact.<br>• 100% clean-room test suite pass rate (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-EXP-022`), amending `REQ-EXP-001` (*Export Interoperability*) and refining `BaseExporter.java`, `BaseFileWriter.java`, `GPXFileWriter.java`, and `TCXFileWriter.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Independent whole-app architecture review (2026-10-18, commit `0234bfc0`, ticket `ATT-4013`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: GPX track segment closing was originally implemented via a simple lap inequality check (`lap != BANALService.INIT_LAP_NR`) assuming workouts always start at lap 0. `copyFileToDownloads` was introduced in Android 10 scoped storage migration with a placeholder GPX MIME type and without format or upload-type distinctions. TCX creator block had been placed at document root during initial development.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Explicit file exports (`ExportType.FILE`) continue to be placed into `Downloads/` for athlete access, while community upload files stay private in app storage; XML tags and extensions remain compatible with third-party fitness platforms.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a workout whose initial lap 0 has been cropped so the first recorded sample has lap 1,<br>• *When* exported via `GPXFileWriter`,<br>• *Then* the resulting GPX file SHALL start the track with `<trkseg>` and SHALL NOT emit a preceding `</trkseg>` tag.<br>• *Given* a workout with zero track samples,<br>• *When* exported via `GPXFileWriter`,<br>• *Then* the output SHALL NOT contain orphan `</trkseg>` tags and SHALL parse as well-formed XML.<br>• *Given* an exported TCX file,<br>• *When* validated against Garmin's official `TrainingCenterDatabasev2.xsd`,<br>• *Then* `<Creator>` SHALL be a child of `<Activity>`, `<Author>` SHALL be a child of `<TrainingCenterDatabase>`, and the document SHALL validate with zero XSD errors.<br>• *Given* an export of a CSV, FIT, or TCX file to Downloads,<br>• *When* `copyFileToDownloads` executes,<br>• *Then* the MediaStore `MIME_TYPE` column SHALL be set to `text/csv`, `application/vnd.ant.fit`, or `application/vnd.garmin.tcx+xml` respectively.<br>• *Given* a workout export for Strava upload (`ExportType.COMMUNITY` / `FileFormat.STRAVA`),<br>• *When* export finishes,<br>• *Then* no copy SHALL be created in the public `Downloads/` directory.<br>• *Given* a MediaStore insert failure returning null `targetUri`,<br>• *When* `copyFileToDownloads` executes,<br>• *Then* no `NullPointerException` SHALL be thrown.<br><br>**Invariants**: Explicit file exports continue to appear in Downloads/; custom extension schemas preserved; 100% test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | GPX/TCX well-formedness, Garmin TCX v2 schema compliance, UTC thread-safe formatting, Downloads MIME types & privacy protection. | `GPXFileWriter.java`, `TCXFileWriter.java`, `BaseExporter.java`, `BaseFileWriter.java`, `FileFormat.java` | `TST-EXP-019` | Verified |

TTL eviction SHALL execute upon repository instantiation (`init`), during background sync worker execution (`StravaRoutesSyncWorker`, `StravaSegmentsSyncWorker`), and on demand. For expired segments, the eviction SHALL cascade-delete associated polyline stream coordinates from `SegmentStreamsTable`.<br>3. *Orphan & Tombstone Pruning*: During remote synchronization, the system SHALL compare local Strava records against the remote API response. Any local route with `source == RouteSource.STRAVA` whose external Strava ID is absent from the active remote route set SHALL be promptly pruned from `Routes.db`. Similarly, any local starred segment whose Strava ID is absent from the active remote starred segments set SHALL be pruned from `Segments.db` alongside its stream coordinates.<br>4. *Athlete Route Preservation (Local GPX Duplication)*: To allow athletes to retain desired navigation tracks permanently offline without violating Strava caching limits, the system SHALL provide a "Save as Local Route" / "Als lokale Route speichern" feature. Eviction operations MUST execute safely in background transactions without blocking UI threads or failing on offline devices. | Comply with Strava API Agreement Section 6.2 mandating a 7-day maximum cache retention and prompt orphan deletion, while safeguarding athlete-owned routes, native workout records, and sensor configurations. | `RoutesDatabaseManager.kt`, `RoutesRepository.kt`, `SegmentsDatabaseManager.java`, `SegmentsRepository.kt`, `StravaRoutesSyncWorker.kt`, `StravaSegmentsSyncWorker.kt` | `TST-EXT-007` | Verified |

It SHALL log an error and return `null` without deleting local data.<br>2. *Thread-Safe Reentrant Token Refresh & Double-Checked Locking (`REQ-EXT-011.2`)*:<br>• `StravaHelper` SHALL synchronize concurrent invocations of `getRefreshedAccessToken()` via a reentrant lock or monitor (`refreshLock`).<br>• Inside the synchronized block, `StravaHelper` SHALL re-verify token validity: if a preceding concurrent thread has already refreshed the token such that `now + 300 < expiresAt`, `getRefreshedAccessToken()` SHALL return `TrainingApplication.getStravaAccessToken()` immediately without sending a duplicate network request.<br>3. *5-Minute (300-Second) Token Expiry Margin (`REQ-EXT-011.3`)*:<br>• `StravaHelper` SHALL consider a cached access token valid if and only if `System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000 + 300 < TrainingApplication.getStravaTokenExpiresAt()`.<br>• If remaining token validity is less than or equal to 300 seconds (5 minutes), `StravaHelper` SHALL execute a preemptive token refresh.<br>4. *Singleton HTTP Client Reuse (`REQ-EXT-011.4`)*:<br>• `StravaHelper` SHALL reuse a shared singleton `OkHttpClient` instance configured with 15-second connect and read timeouts, eliminating per-call client allocations and thread pool leaks.<br>5. *Safe Authorization Header Construction (`REQ-EXT-011.5`)*:<br>• In `StravaUploader.kt`, methods `updateStravaActivity`, `getStravaJson`, and `getStravaJsonArray` SHALL resolve `val accessToken = StravaHelper.getRefreshedAccessToken()` prior to building HTTP requests.<br>• If `accessToken.isNullOrBlank()`, the method SHALL log an error/warning and return `null` immediately without creating or dispatching an HTTP request containing `"Authorization: Bearer null"`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-EXT-011`, extending `REQ-EXT-009` under Epic `ATT-597` (*Strava Support*). However, the implementation in `StravaHelper.kt` used a simplistic substring check `errorBody.contains("invalid")`, causing non-revocation errors (such as `client_secret: invalid`) and unsynchronized concurrent refresh collisions to wipe all local data.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Full compliance with Strava API Policy Section 7.4 is strictly preserved when the refresh token is truly revoked or invalid. Native workouts, local GPX routes, and hardware pairings in `Equipment.db` remain 100% protected.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* Strava API returns HTTP 400 with `field: client_secret, code: invalid` during token refresh,<br>• *When* `StravaHelper.getRefreshedAccessToken()` executes,<br>• *Then* it logs an error, returns `null`, and DOES NOT invoke `StravaDataPurgeManager.purgeAllStravaData()`.<br>• *Given* Strava API returns HTTP 400 with `field: refresh_token, code: invalid` or `invalid_grant`,<br>• *When* `StravaHelper.getRefreshedAccessToken()` executes,<br>• *Then* it invokes `StravaDataPurgeManager.purgeAllStravaData()` to fulfill Strava API Policy Section 7.4.<br>• *Given* an expired token and multiple concurrent threads requesting `getRefreshedAccessToken()`,<br>• *When* all threads invoke the method simultaneously,<br>• *Then* exactly one HTTP POST request is sent to Strava, and all threads receive the valid refreshed access token.<br>• *Given* a token whose `expires_at` is 200 seconds in the future,<br>• *When* `getRefreshedAccessToken()` is called,<br>• *Then* it triggers a refresh request because `now + 300 >= expires_at`.<br>• *Given* a failed token refresh (`getRefreshedAccessToken() == null`),<br>• *When* `StravaUploader` methods execute,<br>• *Then* no HTTP request with `Authorization: Bearer null` is dispatched.<br><br>**Invariants**: Strava API Policy Section 7.4 compliance preserved on actual user revocation; native athlete recordings and hardware pairings 100% protected; 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Protect local Strava data against accidental deletion during token refresh, synchronize concurrent refresh requests, enforce a 300-second expiry margin, reuse OkHttpClient, and eliminate Bearer null headers. | `StravaHelper.kt`, `StravaUploader.kt`, `StravaHelperTest.kt` | `TST-EXT-008` | Verified |

*Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4022`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, discovered during independent whole-app architecture review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`). `StravaOAuthCallbackActivity.kt` was introduced in commit `f3c3a0df` (ATT-597).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: The initial prototype omitted `state` verification and used `GlobalScope.launch` to avoid activity lifecycle binding on `finish()`. `BaseOAuthCallbackActivity.java` was left over as an unused prototype artifact.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Redirect URI `strava://rainerblind.github.io`, Custom Tabs integration, full OAuth scopes (`profile:read_all`, etc.), reactive state flow, and 100% test pass rate are strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete tapping "Connect with Strava",<br>• *When* the authorization URL is constructed,<br>• *Then* `state` query parameter is present with a 32-character cryptographic random token, and the token is saved in preferences with an epoch timestamp.<br>• *Given* a callback without `state` parameter or with a mismatched `state` value,<br>• *When* `StravaOAuthCallbackActivity` receives the intent,<br>• *Then* `StravaOAuthStateManager.validateAndConsumeState` returns `false`, no token exchange is initiated, and the activity finishes with an error state.<br>• *Given* a callback with matching `state` received within 10 minutes,<br>• *When* `StravaOAuthCallbackActivity` handles the intent,<br>• *Then* the state is consumed, `exchangeCodeForTokenAsync` is dispatched in repository scope, and tokens are stored upon successful network exchange.<br>• *Given* a callback arriving after 10 minutes from issuance,<br>• *When* validated,<br>• *Then* `validateAndConsumeState` returns `false` due to expiration.<br>• *Given* the codebase,<br>• *When* inspected,<br>• *Then* `BaseOAuthCallbackActivity.java` is absent and `GlobalScope` is not referenced in Strava OAuth code.<br><br>**Invariants**: Custom Tabs launch, canonical redirect URI, permission scopes, and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Protect Strava OAuth 2.0 flow against Login CSRF via cryptographic state parameter and 10-minute expiration, scope token exchange in repository CoroutineScope, and delete dead BaseOAuthCallbackActivity. | a truncated packet is received,<br>• *Then* the devices SHALL safely drop the invalid packet with zero crashes.<br>• *Given* valid, full-length BLE packets conforming to Bluetooth SIG formulas (power, cadence, speed, distance, wheel revolutions, power balance) and GATT connection lifecycle management (`REQ-CON-012`) MUST NOT be altered. | Eliminate fatal NullPointerExceptions | **REQ-CON-016** | **Smartphone Battery Remaining Duration Continuous Countdown & Discrete Transition Drain Rate Architecture.** | The system SHALL compute smartphone battery drain rate strictly across discrete percentage step-down transition events and provide a continuous, monotonic countdown during periods of constant battery level, eliminating sampling-induced upward drift and abrupt multi-hour estimate plunges (ATT-1631):<br>1. *Discrete Transition-Triggered Drain Rate Computation (`BatteryDevice.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL record discrete battery percentage transition points: `BatteryStep(int activeSeconds, int percent)`.<br>• Baseline initialization: At workout start or accumulator reset, record `(mActiveRecordingSeconds, mBatteryLevel)`.<br>• Step-down recording: A new `BatteryStep` SHALL be recorded strictly when `mBatteryLevel < lastRecordedStep.percent`.<br>• Drain rate evaluation: When evaluating drain rate, the system SHALL calculate the rate between the oldest step in the rolling window ($t_0, P_0$) and the latest step ($t_k, P_k$): $\Delta t = t_k - t_0$, $\Delta P = P_0 - P_k$, $\text{drainRatePerHour} = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t / 3600.0}$. When $\Delta t \ge \text{MIN\_STABILIZATION\_SECONDS}$ (300s) and $\Delta P \ge 1$, update `mEstablishedDrainRatePerHour = drainRatePerHour`, `mBaseRemainingSeconds = round((mBatteryLevel / drainRatePerHour) * 3600.0)`, and `mLastStepActiveSeconds = t_k`.<br>2. *Continuous Monotonic Countdown Between Step Transitions*:<br>• During active recording while the battery percentage remains constant ($t > mLastStepActiveSeconds$), remaining seconds SHALL count down: $\text{elapsedSinceStep} = mActiveRecordingSeconds - mLastStepActiveSeconds$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = mBaseRemainingSeconds - elapsedSinceStep$.<br>• *Monotonicity Invariant*: Remaining duration SHALL NEVER increase or drift upwards while battery percentage is constant.<br>• *Lower Bound Floor Clamping*: Remaining seconds SHALL be clamped to the floor of $(P - 1)$: $\text{floorSeconds} = \text{round}(((mBatteryLevel - 1) / mEstablishedDrainRatePerHour) * 3600.0)$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = \max(\text{floorSeconds}, \text{remainingSeconds})$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = \max(0, \text{remainingSeconds})$.<br>3. *Warmup & Stabilization*:<br>• The sensor SHALL emit `BatteryRemainingTimeFormatter.STABILIZING_STATUS_CODE` (`-2`, formatting as `--:--`) until active recording time reaches $\ge 300\text{s}$ AND a drop of $\ge 1\%$ is measured.<br>• If a 1% drop occurs prior to 300s, stabilization completes once total active recording reaches 300s using the effective elapsed time.<br>4. *Charging & Pause Invariants*:<br>• When connected to charger (`mIsCharging == true`), the sensor emits `CHARGING_STATUS_CODE` (`-1`).<br>• When tracking is paused, `mActiveRecordingSeconds` does not increment, preserving countdown state without drift.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-CON-015` (*Smartphone Battery Level and Estimated Remaining Duration Telemetry Sensors*), targeting `BatteryDevice.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `809bc479` (Ticket `ATT-1454`, Sprint `2026-40.4`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ATT-1454` added periodic 30s samples to estimate drain rate, not anticipating that discrete 1% quantization causes time $\Delta t$ to increase while $\Delta P$ is frozen at an integer, driving projected remaining time artificially upward.<br>4. *Refinement Reason*: On-road endurance testing demonstrated that constant battery levels caused remaining time to climb by several hours, followed by a violent downward jump upon the next 1% drop. Transition-based rate calculation combined with intra-step countdown restores accurate physical behavior.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: 1Hz sensor dispatch, zero wake-locks, zero disk I/O, `PHONE_BATTERY` accuracy, and charging detection remain 100% intact.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active workout tracking session where a battery drop has established a drain rate (e.g. 5.0%/h at 80%),<br>• *When* the battery level remains at 80% for several subsequent minutes,<br>• *Then* `BATTERY_REMAINING_TIME` SHALL count down steadily (decreasing second-by-second) and SHALL NEVER increase.<br>• *Given* an established drain rate and countdown at level $N$,<br>• *When* the battery level transitions from $N$ to $N - 1$,<br>• *Then* the new drain rate computed from the transition window SHALL smoothly adjust without erratic multi-hour jumps.<br>• *Given* active tracking in the first 300 seconds without confirmed drop,<br>• *When* `BATTERY_REMAINING_TIME` is queried,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `STABILIZING_STATUS_CODE` (`--:--`).<br>• *Given* an established drain rate of 10%/h (expected 360s per 1%),<br>• *When* active recording extends past 360s at the same percentage (e.g. 600s),<br>• *Then* remaining seconds SHALL NOT count down below the $(P - 1)$ threshold.<br><br>**Invariants**: PHONE_BATTERY reporting (0–100%), charging status detection, 1Hz telemetry dispatch, and zero wake-lock/disk-I/O invariants MUST NOT be broken. | Compute battery drain rate strictly across discrete percentage step-down events and provide a continuous monotonic countdown while percentage is constant, eliminating upward drift and abrupt jumps. | `BatteryDevice.java` | `TST-CON-007` | Verified |

(`KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL provide dedicated, atomic workout start tracking methods: `recordWorkoutStart(@NonNull LatLng pos)` and `recordWorkoutStart(@NonNull `hitCount = existing.hitCount + 1` in SQLite within an atomic transaction boundary.<br>• If `pos` does not match an existing location within $200\text{m}$, the system SHALL create a new location entry with `hitCount = 1`, resolve its human-readable name via `LocationNameResolver`, and store reference elevation (`altitude`).<br>3. *Single-Shot Workout Start Trigger (`TrackerService.java`)*:<br>• In `TrackerService`, the system SHALL track session state with a single-shot flag (`mWorkoutStartLocationRecorded = false`).<br>• When a new workout session starts (`mStartType == StartType.START_NORMAL`), upon acquiring the first valid GPS coordinate (`currentPos != null`) in `sampleAndWriteToDb()`, the system SHALL asynchronously dispatch `recordWorkoutStart(startPos, startAlt)` on the background database executor (`mDbExecutor`) and set `mWorkoutStartLocationRecorded = true`.<br>• Resumed workouts (`RESUME_BY_USER`, `RESUME_SERVICE_RECREATION`) SHALL initialize `mWorkoutStartLocationRecorded = true`, ensuring that pausing, resuming, or service recreation never increments start counts.<br>4. *Historical Data Preservation (Variante A)*:<br>• All existing `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced in ticket `ATT-1366` via commit `637eaefb` to track location usage frequency without corrupting established reference altitudes through running averages.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ATT-1366` placed `learnLocation(..., ExtremaType.START)` inside `initPressureSensor()` under the assumption launches the application, opens the cockpit, or reviews past workouts without starting a session,<br>• *Then* `AltitudeFromPressureDevice` SHALL apply reference altitude calibration (`setAltitudeCorrection`), and `hitCount` in `StartLocation2Altitude.db` SHALL remain strictly 5.<br>• *Given* an existing known location with `hitCount = 5`,<br>• *When* the user starts a new workout (`START_NORMAL`) and the first valid GPS position is acquired,<br>• *Then* `TrackerService` SHALL trigger `recordWorkoutStart()`, and `hitCount` in `StartLocation2Altitude.db` SHALL increment to 6.<br>• *Given* an active workout that is paused and subsequently resumed by the athlete or recreated after service interruption,<br>• *When* tracking resumes,<br>• *Then* `mWorkoutStartLocationRecorded` SHALL prevent redundant execution, and `hitCount` SHALL NOT increment.<br>• *Given* a workout started at a novel coordinate $>200\text{m}$ from any known location,<br>• *When* tracking starts,<br>• *Then* a new location record SHALL be created in SQLite with `hitCount = 1`, geocoded name, and reference altitude.<br><br>**Invariants**: Altimeter calibration calculations (`setAltitudeCorrection`), 200m geofence radius, SQLite schema V5, locked location altitude protection (`REQ-DAT-014`), and existing database records MUST NOT be modified or regressed. | If a fresh token is acquired, it SHALL automatically retry the HTTP request once with the new Authorization header.<br>• `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL record `lastHttpCode: Int?` and `lastErrorMessage: String?` from the response body to provide transparent failure diagnostics.<br>3. *Process-Wide Concurrency Synchronization & Global Folder Cache (`GoogleDriveClient.kt`)*:<br>• `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL maintain a static `globalFolderIdCache = ConcurrentHashMap<String, String>()` and `hierarchyLock = Any()` in its companion object.<br>• `ensureFolderHierarchy(folderNames: List<String>)` SHALL synchronize resolution with double-checked locking over `hierarchyLock`. When concurrent WorkManager workers (e.g. TCX and FIT exports) execute in parallel, the first worker creates and caches the folders; subsequent workers immediately reuse the cached or discovered folder ID, preventing duplicate folder creations in Google Drive.<br>• In `findFolderIdByName`, if multiple folders with the identical name exist under `parentId`, the client SHALL reuse the first returned ID and log a warning.<br>4. *Canonical Google Drive API v3 Folder Creation (`GoogleDriveClient.kt`)*:<br>• In `createFolder(folderName: String, parentId: String)`, when `parentId == "root"` or blank, the system SHALL omit the `parents` field from the request payload, adhering strictly to Google Drive API v3 canonical root placement.<br>• When creating a child folder under an existing folder ID, the system SHALL pass `parents: [parentId]`.<br>5. *Database Backup Automatic Token Refresh (`GoogleDriveBackupManager.kt`)*:<br>• In `GoogleDriveBackupManager`, `clientProvider: (Context) -> GoogleDriveClient` SHALL supply `tokenRefresher = { GoogleDriveAuthManager.refreshTokenSync(context).getOrNull() }`, guaranteeing database backup uploads also benefit from automatic 401 token renewal.<br>6. *User-Actionable Localized Error Reporting (`GoogleDriveUploader.kt`)*:<br>• In `GoogleDriveUploader.doExport()`, `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL be created with `tokenRefresher = { GoogleDriveAuthManager.refreshTokenSync(mContext).getOrNull() }`.<br>• If folder resolution fails due to unauthenticated state / token refresh failure (HTTP 401), the export SHALL return `ExportResult(false, false, mContext.getString(R.string.google_drive_error_auth_expired))`.<br>• If folder resolution fails due to Google Drive API disabled in Google Cloud Console (`HTTP 403` with `SERVICE_DISABLED` or `accessNotConfigured`), the export SHALL return `ExportResult(false, false, mContext.getString(R.string.google_drive_error_api_disabled))`.<br>• Other folder resolution failures SHALL return `mContext.getString(R.string.google_drive_error_folder_hierarchy)` with HTTP status code suffix.<br>7. *100% 9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-LOC-001`)*:<br>• String resources `google_drive_error_auth_expired`, `google_drive_error_api_disabled`, and `google_drive_error_folder_hierarchy` SHALL be defined across all 9 supported application locales (`values/`, `values-de/`, `values-es/`, `values-fr/`, `values-it/`, `values-ja/`, `values-nl/`, `values-pl/`, `values-pt/`).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines `REQ-DAT-020` (*Google Drive Integration for Automated Workout Export and Database Backup*), targeting `GoogleDriveClient.kt`, `GoogleDriveUploader.kt`, `GoogleDriveBackupManager.kt`, | **REQ-DAT-023** | **Workout Route Preview Map Simplification via Douglas-Peucker & Compact Scalar Streams.** | The system SHALL generate high-fidelity, compact workout route previews (`WorkoutSummaries.MAP_POLYLINE`) and scalar elevation/distance streams (`WorkoutSummaries.ALTITUDE_STREAM`, `WorkoutSummaries.DISTANCE_STREAM`) for both imported and live-tracked workouts (ATT-2667):<br>1. *Imported Workout Route Simplification (`LegacyImportEngine.kt`)*: In `recalculateStats()`, when generating `WorkoutSummaries.MAP_POLYLINE` from parsed trackpoints (`points: List<LatLng>`), the system SHALL apply the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplification algorithm via `PolyUtil.simplify(points, 10.0)` (10.0 meters tolerance) before encoding to polyline string. If `points` contains fewer than 3 coordinates, `PolyUtil.simplify` SHALL return `points` unchanged.<br>2. *Scalar Stream Downsampling (`LegacyImportEngine.kt`)*: In `recalculateStats()`, the system SHALL downsample parsed `altitudes` and `distances` using `WorkoutSummaries.ENCODING_STEP_SIZE` (20) intervals (`(index + 1) % 20 == 0`, with fallback to the last element if non-empty but fewer than 20 points) before encoding via `NumericalEncodingUtils.encodeDoubles`. The downsampled streams SHALL maintain identical sample counts and delta encoding.<br>3. *Live-Tracked Workout Raw Point Collection (`LiveWorkoutSession.java`)*: `LiveWorkoutSession` SHALL accumulate every valid 1 Hz GPS fix (`currentPos != null`) into an internal `rawLatLngs` collection across active session ticks. It SHALL expose `getRawLatLngs(): List<LatLng>` and `addRawLatLng(LatLng latLng)`. Incremental 20-second stream updates (`StreamIncrement`) during active tracking SHALL be preserved untouched to ensure real-time in-progress map and elevation preview compatibility.<br>4. *Live Session Finalization Simplification (`TrackerService.java`)*: In `finalizeLiveSession()`, the system SHALL simplify the full raw 1 Hz GPS track via `PolyUtil.simplify(mLiveSession.getRawLatLngs(), 10.0)` directly (falling back to `mLiveSession.getSampledLatLngs()` only if `rawLatLngs` is empty) and persist the resulting simplified polyline to `WorkoutSummaries.MAP_POLYLINE` in SQLite and `WorkoutRepository`.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Spatial bounding boxes (`BOUND_MIN_LAT`, `BOUND_MAX_LAT`, `BOUND_MIN_LNG`, `BOUND_MAX_LNG`) SHALL remain calculated from raw GPS coordinates to guarantee accurate zero-latency viewport framing. Raw 1 Hz telemetry samples in `WorkoutSamples` database tables MUST remain full-resolution and unaltered. Zero SQLite database schema upgrade or table rewrite is required (`DB_VERSION = 24` preserved).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-DAT-004` (*Encoded polylines and streams for storage/map*) in `docs/requirements.md`, targeting `LegacyImportEngine.kt`, `TrackerService.java`, and `LiveWorkoutSession.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2667` (Sprint `2026-41.4`), building on `REQ-DAT-004` (Sprint 2015-V15).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Prior import logic encoded 100% of raw 1 Hz points directly to preserve raw fidelity, but caused high memory consumption, visual noise, and scrolling jank in summary preview cards. Live tracking sampled points at 20-second intervals to save storage, but time-based downsampling retained redundant collinear points and cut corners.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Raw sample storage in `WorkoutSamples` database is 100% preserved; real-time incremental 20s stream updates during active tracking are preserved; bounding box accuracy is preserved; zero database migrations or table rewrites.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an imported workout file (TCX, GPX, or FIT) with 1 Hz trackpoints (~7,000 points),<br>• *When* the file is imported via `LegacyImportEngine`,<br>• *Then* `MAP_POLYLINE` is generated from `PolyUtil.simplify(points, 10.0)`, reducing point count to ~150–350 points without losing curve fidelity.<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session receiving 1 Hz GPS location fixes,<br>• *When* the athlete completes and finalizes the workout via `TrackerService.finalizeLiveSession()`,<br>• *Then* the stored `MAP_POLYLINE` is simplified from the full raw GPS points (`mLiveSession.getRawLatLngs()`) using `PolyUtil.simplify(..., 10.0)` rather than simplifying the 20-second sampled points.<br>• *Given* an imported workout with altitude and distance data,<br>• *When* `recalculateStats` writes `ALTITUDE_STREAM` and `DISTANCE_STREAM` to `WorkoutSummaries`,<br>• *Then* the streams are sampled at `ENCODING_STEP_SIZE = 20` intervals.<br>• *Given* existing workouts in `WorkoutSummaries.db`,<br>• *When* the app runs with the new simplification logic,<br>• *Then* zero database schema migration or background table rewrite is triggered.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite schema for `WorkoutSummaries.db` remains at `DB_VERSION = 24`; raw per-second samples in `WorkoutSamplesDatabaseManager` remain untouched; real-time 20s stream incremental updates remain unaltered. | Prevent memory bloat and UI scroll jank in workout summary cards by simplifying raw GPS polylines with Douglas-Peucker and downsampling scalar streams, while preserving full raw curve fidelity and zero database migrations. | `LegacyImportEngine.kt`, `LiveWorkoutSession.java`, `TrackerService.java` | `TST-DAT-018` | Verified |

(b) For `format == "tcx"`, candidate folders SHALL scan `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "TCX")`, followed by legacy fallback `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "Workouts")` and `listOf("aTrainingTracker")`. (d) For `format == "all"`, candidate folders SHALL scan `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "FIT")`, `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "TCX")`, `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "GPX")`, followed by legacy fallback `listOf("aTrainingTracker", "Workouts")` and `listOf("aTrainingTracker")`.<br>3. *Cross-Directory Base Filename Deduplication*: Discovered entries across format-specific and legacy directories SHALL be deduplicated by base filename (`removeSuffix("-TMP").removeSuffix("~").lowercase()`) per `REQ-MIG-031`, guaranteeing that an activity present in both `aTrainingTracker/<FORMAT>` and `aTrainingTracker/Workouts` is imported at most once.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*: Least-privilege OAuth scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` is strictly preserved; database backups remain strictly isolated in `aTrainingTracker/Backups/` (`GoogleDriveBackupManager.kt`); unlinked safety and 100% test pass rate are preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines `REQ-DAT-020` (*Google Drive Integration for Automated Workout Export and Database Backup*) and `REQ-MIG-034` (*Google Drive Historical Workout File Discovery & Bulk Recovery*), targeting `GoogleDriveUploader.kt` and `LegacyImportEngine.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-3168` (Sprint `2026-41.10`), building on `ATT-1306` (Sprint `2026-41.1`) and `ATT-2346` (Sprint `2026-41.9`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Google Drive was initially designed with a flat `Workouts/` folder for activity files. | **REQ-DAT-025** | **Authoritative Database Cursor Row and Batch Mappers for Route and Cluster Repositories.** | The system SHALL eliminate manual inline cursor column extractions and enforce Rule 20 (Database & DTO Mapping Symmetry) and Rule 36 (Single Source of Truth & DRY) across route and cluster persistence layers (ATT-3366):<br>1. *Cursor Lifecycle & Positioning Invariants*:<br>• Row-level mappers (`fromCursor(cursor: Cursor)`) SHALL expect a cursor already positioned at the target row. (`RoutesDatabaseManager.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL provide `fun mapCursorToRouteWaypoint(cursor: Cursor): RouteWaypoint`, `internal fun mapCursorToRouteWaypoint(cursor: Cursor, indices: WaypointIndices): RouteWaypoint`, and `fun mapCursorToRouteWaypoints(cursor: Cursor): List<RouteWaypoint>`.<br>• The system SHALL provide `fun mapCursorToPathPoint(cursor: Cursor): PathPoint`, `internal fun mapCursorToPathPoint(cursor: Cursor, indices: PathPointIndices): PathPoint`, and `fun mapCursorToPathPoints(cursor: Cursor): List<PathPoint>`.<br>• The system SHALL promote `mapCursorToRouteSummary(cursor: Cursor)` to `internal` and provide `fun mapCursorToRouteSummaries(cursor: Cursor): List<RouteSummary>`.<br>• `getWaypointsForRoute()` and `getRoutePath()` SHALL delegate strictly through these mappers with zero duplicated inline column resolutions.<br>3. *Index Caching Architecture*:<br>• Batch mappers SHALL resolve column indices exactly once per query via lightweight immutable index cache holders (`WaypointIndices`, `PathPointIndices`), passing them to indexed row mappers to eliminate $O(N \times K)$ JNI `getColumnIndexOrThrow` invocations inside row loops.<br>4. *Workout Cluster Database Manager & Repository (`WorkoutClusterDatabaseManager.kt`, `WorkoutClusterRepository.kt`)*:<br>• `WorkoutClusterDatabaseManager` SHALL expose `fromCursor(cursor: Cursor): WorkoutCluster` and `fromCursorBatch(cursor: Cursor): List<WorkoutCluster>`.<br>• `WorkoutClusterRepository.loadWorkoutsWithBatchMetadata` SHALL extract batch keys via `fromCursorBatchKeys(cursor: Cursor): WorkoutBatchKeys`, resolving column indices (`C_ID`, `FILE_BASE_NAME`, `CLUSTER_ID`) once and populating primitive/string collections directly without intermediate wrapper object allocation per row.<br>• `WorkoutBatchKey.fromCursor(cursor: Cursor)` SHALL be provided for single-row mapping symmetry.<br>5. *Preservation of Domain Invariants*:<br>• labels.<br>• *Given* any selected destination in the navigation drawer,<br>• *When* the drawer row is rendered,<br>• *Then* both the leading icon and text label SHALL render tinted with `color_primary`.<br>• *Given* the Online Communities drawer group,<br>• *When* Strava and Dropbox rows are rendered,<br>• *Then* their icons SHALL render with their authentic brand colors without monochrome tinting.<br>• *Given* the device configured in Light Mode,<br>• *When* the navigation drawer is opened,<br>• *Then* monochrome destination icons SHALL render with `color_on_surface` (dark navy `#000080`), maintaining high contrast against the white surface.<br>• *Given* an item in the navigation drawer with an invalid, corrupted, or unresolvable drawable resource ID (or a missing density asset),<br>• *When* the navigation drawer is composed,<br>• *Then* `DrawerItemView` SHALL catch the resource resolution exception, log a warning, and render a 24dp spacer without crashing the | **REQ-UI-139** | **Right-Aligned Edge FastScrollbar, Isolated Thumb Touch Target & Continuous Drag Accumulation.** | The system SHALL position the fast scrollbar (`FastScrollbar.kt`) flush against the right edge of the viewport, isolate drag gesture detection strictly to the draggable thumb, and maintain continuous drag displacement accumulation:<br>1. *Flush Edge Alignment*: In `WorkoutList.kt`, `FastScrollbar` SHALL be aligned flush to `Alignment.CenterEnd` with zero end padding (`padding(end = 0.dp)`), eliminating floating inward offsets.<br>2. *Right-Aligned Track & Ergonomic Thumb*: In `FastScrollbar.kt`, the track (`width = 4.dp`) SHALL be aligned to `Alignment.CenterEnd` flush against the viewport edge. The draggable thumb hit box SHALL be aligned to `Alignment.TopEnd` with an ergonomic touch target (`width = 28.dp`, `height = 48.dp`) containing an 8dp visual pill aligned to `Alignment.CenterEnd`, ensuring effortless grabbing while physically isolating the track from list cards (which end at `screenWidth - 8.dp`).<br>3. *Isolated Thumb Touch Target & Gesture Scoping*: Drag gesture detection (`detectDragGestures`) SHALL be scoped strictly to the draggable thumb composable, and MUST NOT be declared on the full-height outer container Box. The track area above and below the thumb SHALL NOT capture or consume pointer input, ensuring underlying list item action buttons (e.g. 3-dots export menu, edit button) receive click events without interference.<br>4. *Continuous Drag Accumulation & Zero-Latency Visual Tracking*: During drag gestures, the scrollbar SHALL maintain an active drag state (`isDragging: Boolean`, `dragProgress: Float`), continuously accumulating fractional displacement deltas without per-frame integer truncation loss ($\text{dragProgress} = (\text{dragProgress} + \text{dragAmount.y} / \text{maxOffsetPx}).\text{coerceIn}(0f, 1f)$). D_{\text{total}}$).<br>• *Given* the elevation profile is zoomed in,<br>• *When* the athlete scrubs along the visible curve,<br>• *Then* `onDistanceSelected` and the coordinate marker SHALL accurately reflect the absolute workout distance and elevation of the inspected point.<br><br>**Invariants**: Vertical elevation bounds, grade coloring thresholds, adaptive profile height, and absolute distance contract MUST NOT be altered. | Enable horizontal zoom and pan on the elevation profile chart with centroid scaling, double-tap reset, adaptive X-axis ticks, and synchronized coordinate scrubbing. | `ElevationProfile.kt` | `TST-UI-146` | Verified |
