| **REQ-UI-219** | **Aftermath/Graphs: Robust Running Pace Decoding, Stopped-Speed Clamping, and mm:ss Y-Axis Pace Formatting.** | The system SHALL enforce robust running pace decoding, stopped-speed clamping, and athletic mm:ss Y-axis label formatting across all Aftermath telemetry graphs and scrubbing cards (`ElevationProfile.kt`, `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`) (ATT-1818):<br>1. *ElevationProfile Scrubbing Pace Decoding & Stopped Clamping*:<br>• In `ElevationProfile.kt`, when `bSportType == BSportType.RUN`, the multi-metric scrubbing badge SHALL convert speed to seconds per meter ($s/m = 1.0 / point.speedMps$) and pass $s/m$ into `paceFormatter.format_with_units(1.0 / point.speedMps)`.<br>• When `point.speedMps == null || point.speedMps < 0.55` (speeds below 0.55 m/s / ~2.0 km/h, representing pauses or stops), the scrubbing badge SHALL invoke `paceFormatter.format_with_units(null)` to display `"-- min/km"` (or `"-- min/mile"` in Imperial), eliminating division-by-zero, infinity, and implausible walking paces.<br>• Non-running sports SHALL continue formatting speed via `speedFormatter.format_with_units(point.speedMps)` in `km/h` or `mph`.<br>2. *TelemetryMetricUtils Value Formatting (`TelemetryMetricUtils.formatValue`)*:<br>• For `TelemetryMetricType.PACE`, `formatValue` SHALL convert `value` (in minutes per unit) to seconds per meter ($s/m$): `spm = (value * 60.0) / metersPerUnit` (where `metersPerUnit` is 1000.0 for Metric and `BANALService.METER_PER_MILE` for Imperial) and pass $spm$ into `paceFormatter.format_with_units(spm)`. When `value == null`, it SHALL return `"--"`.<br>3. *Athletic Pace Y-Axis Formatting (`formatPaceMinutes` / `mm:ss`)*:<br>• `TelemetryMetricUtils` SHALL provide a public helper `formatPaceMinutes(paceMinutes: Double): String` returning `String.format(Locale.US, "%d:%02d", min, sec)`.<br>• In `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, when `metricType == TelemetryMetricType.PACE`, Y-axis maximum label (top / fastest, corresponding to `dataMin`) and minimum label (bottom / slowest, corresponding to `dataMax`) SHALL be rendered via `formatPaceMinutes(...)`. Raw decimal float formatting (`String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f", ...)`) SHALL NOT be used for Pace.<br>4. *Dynamic Range Bounding & Stopped Filtering (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• In `extractMetricValue` for `PACE`, speeds below $0.55 \text{ m/s}$ SHALL return `null` (treated as stopped/paused), and pace values SHALL be bounded within realistic athletic limits: coerced to `[1.5, 20.0]`.<br>• In `dataMin` and `dataMax` calculation for `PACE`, `dataMin` and `dataMax` SHALL be derived from active running points with a minimum spread of at least 1.0 min/km: `dataMin = (min * 0.95).coerceAtLeast(1.5)`, `dataMax = (max * 1.05).coerceAtMost(20.0)`, `dataMax = max(dataMax, dataMin + 1.0)`.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Pace inversion logic in `TelemetryMetricGraph` (faster pace near top, slower pace near bottom) remains strictly preserved.<br>• Synchronized multi-chart scrubbing via `selectedDistance` and global horizontal zoom alignment remain 100% intact.<br>• Non-running sports (cycling, hiking) remain unaffected and continue using `SpeedFormatter`.<br>• 100% 9-language localization parity is maintained.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-UI-219`), extending and refining `REQ-UI-206` under Epic `ATT-111` (*Compact Post-Workout Visual Analytics & Graphs*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `061a4b35` (`ATT-1740`) introduced `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` and initial pace conversion; ticket `ATT-1391` introduced multi-metric scrubbing.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ElevationProfile.kt` passed speed (m/s) to `PaceFormatter` (which expects s/m), producing 69:27 min/km for a 15 km/h runner. Decimal labels (1.0, 33.0) and unconstrained pause samples distorted the chart.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: `PaceFormatter` s/m contract, metric and imperial unit parity, synchronized scrubbing, and localization parity are 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete inspecting a running workout in `ElevationProfile`,<br>• *When* scrubbing at a point with speed 4.167 m/s (15 km/h),<br>• *Then* the scrubbing badge SHALL display `"4:00 min/km"` (Metric) or `"6:26 min/mile"` (Imperial), and SHALL NOT display `"69:27 min/km"`.<br>• *Given* an athlete scrubbing at a stopped point ($speedMps < 0.55\text{ m/s}$ or null),<br>• *When* rendered,<br>• *Then* the pace text SHALL render as `"-- min/km"` (or `"-- min/mile"`).<br>• *Given* `TelemetryMetricGraph` rendering a running workout (`metricType == PACE`),<br>• *When* inspecting Y-axis labels,<br>• *Then* top and bottom labels SHALL be formatted in athletic `mm:ss` format (e.g. `"4:00"`, `"6:00"`), and SHALL NOT display raw decimal numbers (`"1.0"`, `"33.0"`).<br>• *Given* a running workout with pause/stop points,<br>• *When* rendered in `TelemetryMetricGraph`,<br>• *Then* pause points SHALL NOT expand `dataMax` to 33.0, and the running curve SHALL utilize the vertical chart height effectively.<br><br>**Invariants**: Inverted pace plotting (faster higher), synchronized multi-chart scrubbing, SpeedFormatter usage for cycling/hiking, and 9-language localization parity MUST NOT be broken. | Enforce robust running pace decoding, stopped-speed clamping (<0.55 m/s to '-- min/km'), mm:ss Y-axis label formatting, and dynamic range bounding on Aftermath pace telemetry graphs and scrubbers. | `ElevationProfile.kt`, `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` | `TST-UI-173` | Verified |
| **REQ-UI-220** | **Aftermath/Graphs: Adaptive X-Axis Milestone Decimation, Collision Prevention, and Standardized Boundary Labeling.** | The system SHALL enforce adaptive X-axis milestone decimation, collision prevention, and boundary label parity across all Aftermath continuous telemetry graphs (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, `ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt`) (ATT-1819):<br>1. *Adaptive 2 km Step Progression (`ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt`)*:<br>• In `ElevationProfileZoomMath.calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep`, when `unit == MyUnits.METRIC`, the system SHALL provide an intermediate step for workouts with visible distance between 10 km and 20 km: `visibleDist > 10_000 -> 2_000f`. Workouts in `(10_000, 20_000]` meters SHALL generate 2,000m tick intervals rather than 1,000m intervals, reducing tick count to ~5–9 milestones.<br>2. *Standardized Milestone Label Formatting (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• In `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, intermediate milestone labels SHALL NOT repeat `" km"` or `" mi"` on every tick: (a) Metric: when `visibleSpan < 1500`, format as `"${currentDist.toInt()}m"`; when decimal (`currentDist % 1000.0 != 0.0`), format as `"%.1f"`; else format as `"${(currentDist / 1000.0).toInt()}"` (e.g. `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`); (b) Imperial: when decimal, format as `"%.1f"`; else format as `"${miles.toInt()}"` (e.g. `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`).<br>3. *Start and End Boundary Labels Parity (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• `TelemetryMetricGraph` SHALL instantiate `val distanceFormatter = remember(unit) { DistanceFormatter() }`.<br>• An explicit `endLabel` with units SHALL be rendered at `startPaddingPx + chartWidthPx - endLabelWidth`: `distanceFormatter.format_with_units(startDist + visibleSpan)` (e.g. `"17,82 km"`) in Distance domain, or `ElevationProfileZoomMath.formatTimeTick((startDist + visibleSpan).toLong())` in Time domain.<br>• When zoomed ($Z > 1.01$), an explicit `startLabel` with units SHALL be rendered at `startPaddingPx`: `distanceFormatter.format_with_units(startDist)` or `formatTimeTick(startDist.toLong())`.<br>4. *Dynamic Minimum Pixel Clearance & Decimation Algorithm (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• Intermediate milestone labels SHALL NOT render within 40 dp of the start padding (`tickX <= startPaddingPx + 40.dp.toPx()`) or within `endLabelWidth + 16.dp.toPx()` of the right chart edge (`startPaddingPx + chartWidthPx - tickX <= endLabelWidth + 16.dp.toPx()`).<br>• The renderer SHALL track `lastDrawnRightX`. An intermediate label SHALL only render if its left edge maintains at least 12 dp clearance: `labelLeft >= lastDrawnRightX + 12.dp.toPx()`, updating `lastDrawnRightX = labelLeft + labelWidth`. Colliding milestone labels SHALL be decimated (skipped) while underlying vertical grid lines continue to be rendered.<br>5. *Center-Aligned Milestone Positioning (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• Milestone labels SHALL be centered under the tick mark: `nativeCanvas.drawText(label, tickX - (labelWidth / 2f), size.height - 4.dp.toPx(), axisTextPaint)`.<br>6. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Horizontal padding geometry (50 dp start, 25 dp end), synchronized scrubbing cursor positioning, touch scrubbing coordinate mapping (`canvasXToDistance`), and 9-language localization parity remain 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-UI-220`), extending and refining `REQ-UI-206` under Epic `ATT-111` (*Compact Post-Workout Visual Analytics & Graphs*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `061a4b35` (`ATT-1740`) introduced `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` with an unconstrained X-axis loop; `ATT-1814` synchronized horizontal zoom.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Secondary continuous graphs lacked collision avoidance, drew redundant `" km"` units on every tick, and omitted boundary labels, causing solid text collisions on workouts $\ge 10\text{ km}$.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Shared horizontal paddings, synchronized scrubbing, and invertibility of `ElevationProfileZoomMath` remain 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a workout with total distance 17.82 km,<br>• *When* `calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep` is evaluated in Metric mode,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `2_000f` (2 km tick step).<br>• *Given* `TelemetryMetricGraph` rendering continuous telemetry curves for a 17.82 km workout,<br>• *When* inspecting intermediate milestone labels along the bottom axis,<br>• *Then* labels SHALL render as `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`, etc., without repeating `" km"`, and an explicit end label (`"17,82 km"`) SHALL be anchored at the right chart boundary.<br>• *Given* any combination of workout length, zoom level, or screen width,<br>• *When* X-axis milestone labels are rendered,<br>• *Then* zero labels SHALL collide, overlap, or obscure boundary labels.<br><br>**Invariants**: Shared 50.dp start / 25.dp end padding geometry, synchronized touch scrubbing, and full unit test regression suite pass MUST NOT be broken. | Enforce adaptive X-axis milestone decimation (2 km step for 10-20km), collision clearance, standardized milestone formatting, and boundary start/end labels across Aftermath telemetry graphs. | `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, `ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt` | `TST-UI-174` | Verified |

Trailing expandable chevron icon (`Icons.Default.ExpandMore`) with smooth animated rotation (`animateFloatAsState` from 0° collapsed to 180° expanded).<br>• Subsection contents SHALL expand and collapse via `AnimatedVisibility(visible = isExpanded, enter = expandVertically(), exit = shrinkVertically())`.<br>• Upon initial display of `AdvancedTuningDialog`, all 5 accordion subsections SHALL be initially collapsed (`expandedSections = emptySet<String>()`), presenting a compact, scannable overview of all 5 category headers and live summary subtitles on first launch without requiring vertical scrolling past the Cockpit Typography section (ATT-1957).<br>3. *Live Active-Value Subtitle Updating*:<br>• Each subsection header subtitle SHALL reactively update upon any parameter modification without requiring dialog save:<br>  - The table SHALL feature a dedicated sticky header and an independent horizontal scroll state (`shoeScrollState`).<br>• Horizontal scrolling in Table 1 SHALL NOT scroll or desynchronize Table 2, and vice-versa.<br>• Sticky First Column: The equipment name and icon column SHALL remain sticky on the left during horizontal scrolling across sensor columns in each table.<br>4. *1-Tap Checkbox Persistence (`EquipmentDbHelper.java` & `EquipmentViewModel.kt`)*:<br>• Each grid intersection cell SHALL display an interactive Material 3 `Checkbox`.<br>• The checkbox SHALL be checked if and only if `equipmentItem.linkedDeviceIds.contains(sensor.id)`.<br>• Tapping a checkbox SHALL trigger `EquipmentViewModel.setSensorLink(equipmentId, sensorId, !isCurrentlyLinked)`, updating SQLite table `LINKS` immediately within transactional helper `EquipmentDbHelper.setDeviceLink`, followed by a reactive reload of `bikes` and `shoes`.<br>• Changes made in the matrix SHALL immediately synchronize with the single-item configuration bottom sheet (`EditEquipmentDialog`) and sensor settings (`EditDeviceDialog`).<br>5. *Single-Item Dialog Linkage Restriction (`EditEquipmentDialog.kt` & `EditDeviceDialog.kt`)*:<br>• In `EditEquipmentDialog`, bikes SHALL only be offered bike-compatible and shared sensors; shoes SHALL only be offered run-compatible and shared sensors.<br>• In `EditDeviceDialog`, sensors SHALL only offer compatible equipment types matching `deviceType.sportType` (cycling sensors to bikes only, running sensors to shoes only, shared sensors to both).<br>6. *Empty States & Edge Case Resilience*:<br>• If zero remote sensors are paired across the fleet, an informative placeholder (`@string/equipment_matrix_no_sensors`) SHALL be displayed.<br>• If zero equipment items exist, an informative empty state SHALL be displayed.<br>• If a sport category has equipment but zero compatible sensors, an inline informational state SHALL indicate no compatible sensors are available.<br>7. *9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-LOC-001`)*:<br>• All newly introduced string resources SHALL be translated with 100% parity across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-UI-256` (*Equipment Management: Fleet-Wide Equipment-to-Sensor Mapping Matrix with Checkboxes for Bikes and Shoes*), targeting `EquipmentTabsScreen.kt`, `EquipmentSensorMatrixScreen.kt`, `EquipmentViewModel.kt`, and `DevicesDatabaseManager.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `fc10ad81` (Sprint `2026-40.16`), ticket `ATT-2126`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In ATT-2126, a monolithic table was created to establish the central matrix concept. However, practical usage revealed that displaying power meters on shoes and footpods on bikes created visual noise and nonsensical mapping options.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: 1-tap Checkbox persistence, bidirectional sync with single-item dialogs, sticky columns/headers, fast scrolling, and 9-language localization parity MUST be preserved. Bike sensors and shoe sensors are cleanly partitioned into two sport-specific tables, with shared sensors (HRM, Temperature) appearing in both.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* configured bikes and shoes, and paired remote sensors (e.g. Stages Power, Wahoo Speed, Stryd Footpod, Garmin HRM),<br>• *When* the athlete navigates to the "Sensor Matrix" tab in `EquipmentTabsScreen`,<br>• *Then* two separate tables SHALL be displayed: Table 1 (Fahrräder) containing Stages Power, Wahoo Speed, and Garmin HRM; and Table 2 (Schuhe) containing Stryd Footpod and Garmin HRM.<br>• *Given* Table 1 (Bikes) and Table 2 (Shoes),<br>• *When* the athlete scrolls Table 1 horizontally across bike sensors,<br>• *Then* Table 2 SHALL NOT scroll and SHALL maintain its own scroll position independently.<br>• *Given* a bike sensor row in Table 1,<br>• *When* the athlete taps an unlinked checkbox,<br>• *Then* the checkbox immediately toggles to checked, SQLite table `LINKS` is updated, and opening `EditEquipmentDialog` for that bike shows the sensor selected.<br>• *Given* `EditEquipmentDialog` opened for a running shoe,<br>• *When* viewing available sensors,<br>• *Then* only running-compatible and shared sensors SHALL appear, and cycling-exclusive power meters/cadence sensors SHALL NOT be selectable.<br>• *Given* zero paired remote sensors,<br>• *When* viewing the "Sensor Matrix" tab,<br>• *Then* an informative empty state placeholder is displayed.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite schema stable; bidirectional sync guaranteed; 100% clean-room test suite pass rate. | Centralized, interactive equipment-to-sensor mapping matrix partitioned into sport-specific tables for bikes and shoes with restricted incompatible linkage. | `EquipmentTabsScreen.kt`, `EquipmentSensorMatrixScreen.kt`, `EquipmentViewModel.kt`, `EquipmentDbHelper.java`, `DevicesDatabaseManager.java`, `EditEquipmentDialog.kt` | `TST-UI-230` | Verified |
| **REQ-CON-017** | **Barometric Altimeter Idempotent Calibration, Delta Shift Dispatch, Physical Sanity Limiting & Historical Workout Data Sanitization.** | The system SHALL eliminate barometric calibration oscillations, prevent runaway retroactive sample accumulation, enforce physical climb rate sanity limits, and strictly protect legitimate high-altitude workout data (ATT-1810, ATT-3990):<br>1. *Absolute Baseline Correction Formulation (`AltitudeFromPressureDevice.java`)*:<br>• In `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.setAltitudeCorrection(double correctAltitude)`, `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL be computed strictly relative to raw barometric pressure: $\text{newCorrection} = \text{correctAltitude} - \text{mLastRawAltitude}$.<br>• The method SHALL compute $\text{deltaOffset} = \text{newCorrection} - \text{mAltitudeCorrection}$, update $\text{mAltitudeCorrection} = \text{newCorrection}$, set $\text{mIsCalibrated} = \text{true}$, and publish $\text{mAltitudeSensor.newValue}(\text{mLastRawAltitude} + \text{mAltitudeCorrection})$.<br>• `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_INTENT` SHALL be broadcast containing `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_VALUE = deltaOffset` IF AND ONLY IF $|\text{deltaOffset}| \ge 0.1\text{ m}$. If $|\text{deltaOffset}| < 0.1\text{ m}$, the broadcast MUST be suppressed.<br>2. *Idempotent Altimeter Calibration Guard (`calibrate`)*:<br>• In `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.calibrate(double referenceAltitude)`, if `isCalibrated()` is true and current calibrated altitude is within $0.5\text{ m}$ of `referenceAltitude` ($|(\text{mLastRawAltitude} + \text{mAltitudeCorrection}) - \text{referenceAltitude}| < 0.5$), the method SHALL return `true` immediately without recomputing correction or broadcasting intents.<br>3. *Geofence Transition Calibration Gating (`TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`)*:<br>• In `TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`, altimeter calibration dispatch SHALL be gated on geofence transitions. The ViewModel SHALL maintain `lastCalibratedLocationId: Long?` and trigger `banalServiceRepository.calibrateAltimeter(closestItem.altitude)` IF AND ONLY IF `closestItem.id != lastCalibratedLocationId` or `!isCalibrated`.<br>• When exiting all geofences (`closestItem == null`), `lastCalibratedLocationId` SHALL be reset to `null`.<br>4. *Physical Climb/Descent Sanity Limiting & Atomic DB Transactions (`TrackerService.java`, `LiveWorkoutSession.java`)*:<br>• Retroactive sample shifting in `TrackerService.onReceive` SHALL be encapsulated within an explicit atomic SQLite transaction (`beginTransaction()` / `setTransactionSuccessful()` / `endTransaction()`).<br>• In `LiveWorkoutSession.applyAltitudeCorrection` and `TrackerService`, single retroactive shift offsets exceeding $|offset| > 500.0\text{ m}$ SHALL be rejected or clamped with an advisory warning.<br>• In `LiveWorkoutSession.recordStreamPoint` and `TrackerService`, altitude values outside human physical limits ($-500\text{ m} \dots +9000\text{ m}$) or vertical rate changes exceeding $|dh/dt| > 30\text{ m/s}$ ($108\text{ km/h}$) SHALL be clamped to the previous valid altitude sample.<br>5. *Prohibition of Automated Silent Sanitization & Thread Leak Elimination (`WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.java`, `GPXFileWriter.java`, `TCXFileWriter.java`, `ElevationProfile.kt`)*:<br>• Automated, silent background modification of historical workout streams is strictly PROHIBITED (ATT-3990).<br>• `WorkoutSummariesDbHelper.onOpen()` SHALL NOT execute `sanitizeCorruptedAltitudeWorkouts()` or spawn background threads via `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()`.<br>• The database open lifecycle SHALL remain purely passive, side-effect free, and zero-leak.<br>• Legitimate high-altitude climbs (e.g. 0m to 4200m) SHALL NEVER be truncated, flattened, or altered.<br>• `GPXFileWriter.java` and `TCXFileWriter.java` SHALL clamp non-physical altitude samples ($> 9000\text{ m}$ or vertical step spikes $> 100\text{ m}$) to the previous valid sample.<br>• In `ElevationProfile.kt` (`calculateElevationBounds`), non-physical start outliers SHALL be filtered from bounds computation, ensuring graph rendering auto-scales cleanly to real terrain (~480–530 m).<br>6. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Null safety on cold start (`REQ-CON-013`), DEM elevation caching (`REQ-DAT-014`), start location counting (`REQ-DAT-015`), cockpit calibration badge feedback (`REQ-UI-199`), and 9-language localization parity MUST NOT be broken.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-CON-017`), extending and refining `REQ-CON-013` and `REQ-UI-199` under Epic `ATT-111` / Altimeter Tracking.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `53502c7a` (`ATT-1353`), Sprint `2026-40.5` (`ATT-1617`), and Sprint `2026-42.10` (`ATT-3990`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `setAltitudeCorrection` evaluated `currentAltitude` from `mAltitudeSensor.getValue()` which was already corrected, causing feedback oscillation and retroactive runaway shifts. Under ATT-3990, an over-broad historical sanitizer in `onOpen()` was found to destroy legitimate high-altitude climbs (>2000m) and leak threads on every DB open.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Live barometric calibration safeguards are preserved, while automated silent modification of user workouts is eliminated, guaranteeing zero data loss for genuine climbs.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an `AltitudeFromPressureDevice` with `mLastRawAltitude = 450.0m` and default `mAltitudeCorrection = 0.0m`,<br>• *When* `setAltitudeCorrection(507.0)` is invoked,<br>• *Then* `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL be set to $+57.0\text{ m}$, `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_INTENT` SHALL be broadcast with extra value $57.0$, and the sensor value SHALL equal $507.0\text{ m}$.<br>• *Given* an `AltitudeFromPressureDevice` calibrated to 507.0m (`mAltitudeCorrection = 57.0m`),<br>• *When* `setAltitudeCorrection(507.0)` is invoked repeatedly interleaved with incoming pressure sensor measurements,<br>• *Then* `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL remain $+57.0\text{ m}$ (zero oscillation to 0.0), sensor reading SHALL remain locked at $507.0\text{ m}$, and zero additional broadcasts SHALL be emitted.<br>• *Given* `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.calibrate(507.0)` executed successfully,<br>• *When* `calibrate(507.0)` is invoked again while within the same geofence,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `true` immediately with zero broadcasts and zero DB shifts.<br>• *Given* an athlete inside a known location geofence emitting GPS updates every second,<br>• *When* `TrackingTabsViewModel.locationCalibrationStatus` evaluates sequential location emissions,<br>• *Then* `calibrateAltimeter` SHALL be invoked on initial geofence entry and SHALL NOT be dispatched repeatedly on continuous updates within the same location.<br>• *Given* incoming live tracking samples with an implausible vertical spike ($dh/dt > 30\text{ m/s}$) or single retroactive shift $> 500\text{ m}$,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL clamp the spike and reject runaway offsets.<br>• *Given* a stored workout with a legitimate mountain climb from 600m to 4200m,<br>• *When* the database is opened or accessed,<br>• *Then* its `ALTITUDE_STREAM`, `TABLE_EXTREMA_VALUES`, and raw samples SHALL remain 100% unchanged.<br>• *Given* repeated database open invocations,<br>• *Then* zero background executor threads SHALL be created or leaked.<br><br>**Invariants**: Cold-start null-safety, DEM caching, and cockpit badge feedback MUST NOT be broken. | Eliminate barometric calibration feedback oscillations, prevent runaway retroactive sample accumulation, enforce physical climb limits, eliminate thread leaks in DB open, and strictly preserve legitimate mountain climb data. | `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.java`, `TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`, `TrackerService.java`, `LiveWorkoutSession.java`, `WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.java`, `ElevationProfile.kt` | `TST-CON-008` | | **REQ-CON-018** | **Robust Bluetooth LE Sensor Discovery: GATT Queue Deadlock Prevention and State Reset in BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.** | The system SHALL guarantee robust, non-blocking GATT characteristic queue management and state reset in `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine` during peripheral discovery (ATT-2224):<br>1. *Defensive Queue Enqueueing*: In `onServicesDiscovered()`, only non-null `BluetoothGattCharacteristic` references returned by `service.getCharacteristic(...)` SHALL be appended to `mReadCharacteristicQueue`.<br>2. *Deadlock-Free Queue Progression*: In `readNextCharacteristic(String address)`:<br>• If the polled characteristic is `null`, the engine SHALL immediately advance by invoking `readNextCharacteristic(address)`.<br>• When dispatching `gatt.readCharacteristic(characteristic)`, the engine SHALL evaluate the boolean return value. If `readCharacteristic(...)` returns `false` (indicating failure to enqueue in the Bluetooth stack), the engine SHALL immediately advance by invoking `readNextCharacteristic(address)`.<br>3. *Resilient Device Notification (`newDeviceFound`)*: When all characteristics in the queue are read or skipped, the engine SHALL invoke `newDeviceFound(address)` to notify the listener, even if optional characteristics (Manufacturer Name, Battery Level) were omitted or failed to read.<br>4. *Comprehensive Lifecycle & State Reset*: In `stopAsyncSearch()` and `startAsyncSearch()`, the engine SHALL reset tracking state, clearing `mBTGatts`, `mReadCharacteristicQueue`, `mInformedDevices`, `mNameMap`, `mManufacturerMap`, and `mBatteryPercentage`. On `stopAsyncSearch()`, all active `BluetoothGatt` connections SHALL be disconnected and closed prior to clearing the map.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-CON-018`), extending GATT queue safety and connection lifecycle guarantees established in `REQ-CON-012` to `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java` under Epic `ATT-355` / Sensor Connectivity.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.15 (`ATT-2224`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine` added unchecked nulls to the read queue and lacked fail-forward handling, permanently deadlocking BLE device discovery on simulated or third-party sensors lacking optional descriptors.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Runtime telemetry parsing (`REQ-CON-012`, `REQ-CON-014`), BLE permissions (`BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`), and 100% test suite pass rate are strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a discovered BLE peripheral whose Device Information or Battery service returns null for requested characteristics,<br>• *When* `onServicesDiscovered` executes,<br>• *Then* zero null elements SHALL be added to `mReadCharacteristicQueue`.<br>• *Given* a characteristic queue containing a null entry or where `gatt.readCharacteristic()` returns `false`,<br>• *When* `readNextCharacteristic()` is executed,<br>• *Then* the engine SHALL skip to the next characteristic without stalling or terminating the discovery loop.<br>• *Given* a Bike Power or Heart Rate sensor lacking optional Device Information or Battery descriptors,<br>• *When* discovery finishes reading available characteristics,<br>• *Then* `newDeviceFound(address)` SHALL be invoked and the device SHALL be presented to the user.<br>• *Given* an active search where devices were detected and connected,<br>• *When* `stopAsyncSearch()` is called and a new search is started,<br>• *Then* previously connected devices SHALL be redisoverable and reconnectable.<br><br>**Invariants**: Runtime sensor operation in `MyBTLEDevice.java`, Bluetooth permissions, and clean-room test suite pass rate MUST NOT be altered. | Eliminate silent BLE discovery freezes caused by missing optional GATT characteristics and ensure connection state is cleared across searches. | `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java` | `TST-CON-009` | Verified |
| **REQ-CON-019** | **Robust Bluetooth LE Sensor Discovery & Direct LE Transport Connection Architecture.** | The system SHALL guarantee direct Low Energy physical transport connections, unsuppressed BLE scan result delivery, modern scan settings, robust runtime permission verification, and Android 14+ foreground service compliance across all Bluetooth LE discovery and communication workflows (ATT-2773):<br>1. *Direct Low Energy Transport Specification (`TRANSPORT_LE`)*:<br>• In `MyBTLEDevice.java` (`startSearching()`) and `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java` (`mScanCallback.onScanResult`), on Android 6.0+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.M`), the system SHALL invoke `device.connectGatt(mContext, false, mGattCallback, BluetoothDevice.TRANSPORT_LE)`.<br>• On legacy platforms (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.M`), the system SHALL fall back cleanly to `device.connectGatt(mContext, false, mGattCallback)`.<br>2. *Unsuppressed BLE Scan Result Delivery (`AndroidManifest.xml`)*:<br>• The system SHALL remove `android:usesPermissionFlags="neverForLocation"` from `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.BLUETOOTH_SCAN" />` in `AndroidManifest.xml`.<br>• The application SHALL utilize its already-granted `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` and `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` permissions to permit unrestricted reception of BLE advertisements across all filter configurations (including `DeviceType.ALL` where `ScanFilter` is null).<br>3. *Robust Runtime Permission Verification (`BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java`)*:<br>• In `startAsyncSearch()`: On Android 12+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S`), verify `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(mContext, Manifest.permission.BLUETOOTH_SCAN) == PERMISSION_GRANTED` before invoking `scanner.startScan()`. On Android < 12, verify `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`. | **REQ-MIG-036** | **Automated Background Backup WorkManager Scheduling, Monotonic Timer Preservation, and Bounded Local Storage.** | The system SHALL execute automated periodic database backups reliably in the background without timer resets on application cold starts, aligning default preference values, guaranteeing co-located atomic file creation with stale cleanup, and providing bounded local backup retention (ATT-3472, amending `REQ-MIG-003` and `REQ-MIG-004`):<br>1. *Monotonic WorkManager Periodic Scheduling (`BackupWorker.kt`)*:<br>• `BackupWorker.Companion.schedule(context)` SHALL enqueue the unique periodic work request using `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE` for `WORK_NAME = "automated_backup_work"` (replacing legacy `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.REPLACE`).<br>• The periodic timer and initial delay SHALL NOT be cancelled or reset to the full interval upon application cold starts in `TrainingApplication.onCreate()`, preserving monotonic countdown across daily app launches.<br>2. *Default Preference Value Parity (`BackupWorker.kt`)*:<br>• In `BackupWorker.doWork()`, the fallback default for `prefs.getBoolean("automated_backups", true)` SHALL evaluate to `true` (matching `schedule()`, `DropboxSettingsDialog.kt`, and `prefs_dropbox.xml`), guaranteeing that automated backups run on fresh installations without requiring explicit switch manipulation.<br>3. *Configuration Availability Before Worker Scheduling*:<br>• The system SHALL guarantee that application preferences (`SharedPreferences`) are fully initialized and accessible prior to invoking WorkManager background worker scheduling, ensuring background tasks read valid configuration parameters without encountering uninitialized state.<br>4. *Bounded Local Backup Creation, Co-Located Atomic Replacement & Stale Temp Cleanup (`BackupWorker.kt` & `BackupManager.kt`)*:<br>• When automated backups are enabled (`automated_backups == true`), `BackupWorker.doWork()` SHALL generate a valid local `.attbackup` archive using `BackupManager.createBackup(context)` regardless of whether cloud providers are connected.<br>• **Stale Temp Cleanup**: Prior to initiating a new backup bundling cycle, `BackupManager` SHALL delete any orphaned staging files (`aTrainingTracker_backup.tmp`) remaining from previous aborted attempts, preventing storage leakage.<br>• **Same-Directory Atomic File Replacement**: The staging file (`aTrainingTracker_backup.tmp`) SHALL reside in the exact same directory (`context.cacheDir`) as canonical `aTrainingTracker_backup.attbackup`, guaranteeing co-location on the same filesystem mount point. Replacement SHALL execute via `java.nio.file.Files.move` with `StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE` (falling back defensively to `StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING`), eliminating partial file corruption from process death during zipping.<br>• **Storage Boundedness**: Local backup generation SHALL be strictly bounded to $O(1)$ storage space by maintaining only the single canonical archive. No unbounded file accumulation is permitted on device disk.<br>5. *Concurrency Synchronization & Lock Contention Policy*:<br>• Backup bundling SHALL be synchronized via in-process mutex (`BackupManager.backupMutex`) and file lock (`aTrainingTracker_backup.lock`) to prevent race conditions with concurrent manual backups.<br>• If the lock is held by a concurrent manual backup, `BackupWorker` SHALL safely yield and return `Result.retry()` with exponential backoff.<br>6. *Decoupled Cloud Upload & Controlled Retry Policy*:<br>• If neither Dropbox nor Google Drive is connected, `BackupWorker` SHALL record `last_backup_timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis()`, update `last_backup_status = "LOCAL_SUCCESS"`, and return `Result.success()`.<br>• If cloud provider(s) are connected, `BackupWorker` SHALL attempt upload. If any connected upload succeeds, it SHALL update `last_backup_timestamp` and set `last_backup_status` to `"SUCCESS"` (or `"PARTIAL_SUCCESS"`). If all connected uploads fail, the atomic local backup remains safely preserved on device, `last_backup_status` is updated to `"Upload failed"`, and the worker returns `Result.retry()` with exponential backoff.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-MIG-003` (*Regular Cloud Backups via WorkManager*) and `REQ-MIG-004` (*Full Migration Mode*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.2 (initial `BackupWorker`), Sprint 2026-41.1 (`ATT-1306` Google Drive upload).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Under WorkManager 2.7, `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.REPLACE` was used because `UPDATE` did not exist. WorkManager 2.8+ introduced `UPDATE` to preserve monotonic elapsed time.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Unmetered Wi-Fi constraints, exponential backoff (1h), exception resilience in `schedule()`, single canonical file bounds, and `.attbackup` format remain 100% intact.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active periodic work request registered for `automated_backup_work` with remaining time $T_{rem} < T_{period}$,<br>• *When* `TrainingApplication.onCreate()` executes during app startup and calls `BackupWorker.schedule(context)`,<br>• *Then* `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork` uses `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE`, preserving the monotonic schedule without resetting the timer to $T_{period}$.<br>• *Given* a fresh installation where `"automated_backups"` is unset in SharedPreferences,<br>• *When* `BackupWorker.doWork()` executes,<br>• *Then* `prefs.getBoolean("automated_backups", true)` evaluates to `true` and proceeds with backup creation.<br>• *Given* an athlete with no cloud provider connected and automated backups enabled,<br>• *When* `BackupWorker.doWork()` executes,<br>• *Then* `BackupManager.createBackup(context)` creates a valid local archive bounded to $O(1)$ space via atomic same-mount move, `last_backup_timestamp` is updated, `last_backup_status` is set to `"LOCAL_SUCCESS"`, and the worker returns `Result.success()`.<br>• *Given* a previous crash leaving a `.tmp` file,<br>• *When* `BackupManager.createBackup(context)` executes,<br>• *Then* any stale `.tmp` file is purged prior to zipping, preventing storage leakage.<br>• *Given* an environment where WorkManager throws an exception during `schedule()`,<br>• *When* `BackupWorker.schedule(context)` executes,<br>• *Then* the exception is caught, logged, and the app does not crash.<br><br>**Invariants**: Network constraints, battery constraints, exponential backoff, storage boundedness, and exception resilience MUST NOT be broken. | Fix automated background backup WorkManager scheduling using ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE, align default preference values to true, and enable bounded local backups without cloud provider. | `BackupWorker.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java`, `prefs_dropbox.xml` | `TST-MIG-033` | Verified |

Instead, the system SHALL partition workouts into geographic activity regions, prioritize the primary activity region, and provide interactive region switching:<br>1. *Spatial Region Partitioning & Fast-Path*: In `SpatialRegionEngine.detectRegions(workouts)`, workouts with valid GPS coordinates SHALL be partitioned into connected component clusters using Great-Circle Haversine distance with configurable parameter `REGION_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_METERS` ($75\text{ km}$). If the global bounding box diagonal is $< \text{SINGLE\_REGION\_ENVELOPE\_METERS}$ ($60\text{ km}$) or total GPS workouts $\le 1$, the engine SHALL return a single region immediately ($O(1)$ fast-path).<br>2. *Dominant Region Identification*: When multiple regions are detected ($k > 1$), the engine SHALL rank regions deterministically: (a) Primary: Workout frequency/count (descending); (b) Secondary tie-breaker: Total active distance in meters (descending); (c) Tertiary tie-breaker: Timestamp of most recent workout (descending). The highest-ranked region SHALL be marked as primary (`isPrimary = true`, index 0).<br>3. *Initial Viewport & Thumbnail Framing*: In `PeriodSummaryCard.kt` (overview thumbnail) and `InteractivePeriodMap.kt` (detail map), the initial camera bounds SHALL focus tightly on the primary region's bounding box (`primaryRegion.bounds`), eliminating empty ocean tiles and rendering recognizable route polylines.<br>4. *Antimeridian & Polar Normalization*: When workouts within a cluster cross the $180^\circ$ meridian, `SpatialRegionEngine` SHALL construct wrapped `LatLngBounds(southwest, northeast)` with `southwest.longitude > northeast.longitude`, ensuring Google Maps fits the local $< 180^\circ$ span rather than a $350^\circ+$ world-spanning box. Polar coordinates SHALL be clamped to $[-85^\circ, 85^\circ]$.<br>5. *Interactive Region Navigation & Overflow Protection*: When `regions.size > 1`, `PeriodMapScreen.kt` SHALL render an interactive horizontally scrollable chip row (`Modifier.horizontalScroll(rememberScrollState())`) featuring `[ Primary: Region 1 (N) ]`, `[ Region 2 (N) ]`, ..., and `[ All Regions (Total) ]`. Tapping a chip SHALL update `selectedRegionId` and animate the camera to that region's bounds. Tapping \"All Regions\" SHALL fit the aggregate global bounds across all regions. When `regions.size <= 1`, the region switcher bar SHALL be completely hidden (`Visibility.GONE`).<br>6. *State Persistence & Threading*: `PeriodsViewModel` SHALL execute region detection exclusively on background worker threads (`Dispatchers.Default`) and SHALL persist `selectedRegionId` via `SavedStateHandle` across configuration changes and process recreation.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a period containing 100 workouts in Germany (~9°E) and 10 workouts in California (~-122°W),<br>• *When* the period overview card or detail map is displayed,<br>• *Then* the initial map camera SHALL focus tightly on the German training region, with zero centering over Greenland or the North Atlantic.<br>• *When* viewing `PeriodMapScreen` for this multi-region period,<br>• *Then* an interactive horizontal chip bar SHALL appear with chips for Region 1 (100), Region 2 (10), and All Regions (110).<br>• *When* the athlete taps the Region 2 chip,<br>• *Then* the map camera SHALL animate to the California workouts.<br>• *When* the athlete taps \"All Regions\",<br>• *Then* the camera SHALL zoom out to encompass both continents.<br>• *Given* a period where all workouts are within a 50 km perimeter,<br>• *When* the period map is displayed,<br>• *Then* the region chip bar SHALL be hidden and the camera bounds SHALL match legacy bounding behavior 100%.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite schema for `PeriodSummaries.db` MUST NOT be altered; (`TurnCueDetector.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL extract stored course points and waypoints with category `WaypointCategory.TURN_CUE` (`TURN_LEFT`, `TURN_RIGHT`, `TURN_STRAIGHT`) from `RoutesDatabaseManager.getWaypointsForRoute(routeId)` (`REQ-MAP-026`).<br>• For routes lacking embedded turn points, `TurnCueDetector` SHALL synthesize directional turn cues (`SLIGHT_LEFT`, `LEFT`, `SHARP_LEFT`, `SLIGHT_RIGHT`, `RIGHT`, `SHARP_RIGHT`, `U_TURN`) by pre-smoothing polyline bearings using a continuous distance-weighted spatial circular vector mean over a 5-meter envelope ($\pm 2.5\text{m}$ along cumulative distance) without coordinate decimation ($(\bar{x}, \bar{y}) = (\sum \Delta s_k \cos \theta_k, \sum \Delta s_k \sin \theta_k)$, falling back to chord bearing when total length $\le 10^{-4}\text{m}$), evaluating curvature across multi-scale forward sliding windows ($W_{\text{short}} = 12\text{--}15\text{m}$, $W_{\text{long}} = 35\text{--}50\text{m}$) in single-pass linear $O(N)$ execution with zero heap object allocation during internal processing (pre-allocated primitive arrays, index loops), anchoring cues at the true curvature apex $\max |\frac{d\theta}{ds}|$ with deterministic tie-breaking ($i_{\text{apex}} = i_{\text{start}} + \lfloor (K-1)/2 \rfloor$) and 5° hysteresis buffer, suppressing gentle road bends ($< 25^\circ$), clamping boundaries (10m from start/end, empty list for routes $< 20\text{m}$ or $< 3$ points), and consolidating $180^\circ$ hairpin switchbacks into a single `U_TURN` cue (ATT-3494).<br>2. *Real-Time Navigation Engine (`TurnByTurnNavigationEngine.kt`)*:<br>• When `RoutesRepository.activeNavigatedRouteId` is non-null, the engine SHALL project the athlete's current location onto the active route polyline, computing distance along the route ($D_{\text{current}}$) and cross-track orthogonal error ($D_{\text{cross}}$).<br>• The engine SHALL identify the next upcoming turn cue ahead ($D_{\text{cue}} > D_{\text{current}}$) and calculate remaining countdown distance $D_{\text{remain}} = D_{\text{cue}} - D_{\text{current}}$.<br>• State Lifecycle: `APPROACHING` when $D_{\text{remain}} \le \text{countdownThreshold}$ (default $150\text{ m}$); `TURN_NOW` when $D_{\text{remain}} \le 25\text{ m}$; `PASSED` when $D_{\text{current}} > D_{\text{cue}} + 20\text{ m}$, cleanly advancing to the next cue.<br>3. *Visual Cockpit HUD Banner (`TurnPromptBanner.kt`)*:<br>• Rendered as a prominent, glanceable overlay in `SensorGridScreen.kt` when a turn cue is approaching ($\le 150\text{ m}$) or when the athlete is off-route.<br>• Displays turn direction arrow icon, countdown distance in meters (e.g., "150 m", "50 m", or "JETZT" / "NOW" when $\le 25\text{ m}$), and way/street name if available.<br>• For off-route state, displays a high-visibility warning banner with "Off Route / Route verlassen" and distance back to the route corridor.<br>4. *Automated AMOLED Battery Saver Display Wake-Up*:<br>• Upon entering the `APPROACHING` threshold ($\le 150\text{m}$), the system SHALL invoke `BatterySaverController.onWakeupEvent()`, restoring 100% display brightness for the configured wake-up duration.<br>• Upon entering `OFF_ROUTE`, the system SHALL also invoke `BatterySaverController.onWakeupEvent()`.<br>5. *Auditory Chime Alerts (`NavigationAudioAlertManager.kt`)*:<br>• When audio cues are enabled, the system SHALL emit distinct audio chimes via Android `ToneGenerator` (`AudioManager.STREAM_NOTIFICATION` or `STREAM_MUSIC`): approach prompt double tone alert ($\le 150\text{ m}$), immediate turn ascending confirmation chime ($\le 25\text{ m}$), off-route descending warning chime, and rejoining route confirmation tone.<br>6. *Off-Route Corridor Monitoring & Recovery*:<br>• If cross-track distance $D_{\text{cross}} > \text{corridorThreshold}$ (default $50\text{ m}$) for $\ge 3$ consecutive GPS fixes, the system transitions to `OFF_ROUTE`.<br>• When returning to $D_{\text{cross}} \le 30\text{ m}$, the system transitions back to `ON_ROUTE`.<br>7. *Tuning Preferences & 100% 9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• `TuningPreferencesDataStore` provides Remaining path spans from current projection point to route end.<br>  - When "Return Home along route" is active, guidance follows the route polyline in reverse from current location back to route start ($D_{\text{remaining}} = D_{\text{current}}$, and climb $H_{\text{climb}}$ computed by summing positive elevations in reverse).<br>• *Unrouted Saved Route Snapping*: When no route is actively navigated:<br>  - The system SHALL evaluate saved routes in `RoutesRepository.allRoutes` to identify candidate routes that terminate near Home ($\le 500\,\text{m}$) and where the athlete is within corridor proximity ($\le 100\,\text{m}$).<br>• *Direct Geodesic Fallback*: If no matching route is available, the system projects a direct return vector to the Home destination.<br>3. *Elevation-Aware Dynamic ETA Engine (`ElevationAwareEtaCalculator.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL calculate remaining climb $H_{\text{climb}}$ by summing all positive vertical elevation gains along the remaining path segments: $H_{\text{climb}} = \sum_{k} \max(0.0, \text{altitude}_{k+1} - \text{altitude}_{k})$.<br>• The system SHALL calculate predicted travel duration $T_{\text{remaining}}$ using the athletic climbing model: $T_{\text{remaining}} = \frac{D_{\text{remaining}}}{V_{\text{flat}}} + \frac{H_{\text{climb}}}{\text{VAM}_{\text{climb}}}$.<br>• Where $V_{\text{flat}}$ is smoothed rolling speed when moving ($> 1.5\,\text{m/s}$), clamped to athletic limits; $400\,\text{m/h} \approx 0.1111\,\text{m/s}$ for running/walking).<br>• Clock ETA: $\text{ETA} = \text{System.currentTimeMillis()} + (T_{\text{remaining}} \times 1000)$.<br>• Formatting: Exposes formatted clock arrival time (e.g. `"18:42"`) and remaining duration (e.g. `"~34 min"`).<br>4. *Cockpit HUD Integration (`ReturnNavigationHud.kt` in `SensorGridScreen.kt`)*:<br>• In `SensorGridScreen.kt`, when Return Navigation is active or an active route has remaining progress, render a high-visibility HUD banner displaying: destination name & icon ("🏠 Zu Hause" or route name), remaining distance in kilometers (e.g. `"12.4 km"`), remaining vertical gain in meters (e.g. `"+180 m"`), and elevation-adjusted dynamic ETA (e.g. `"18:42 (~34 min)"`).<br>5. *1-Tap Entry Points*:<br>• In `RouteActionChipRow` (`SensorGridScreen.kt`), display remaining distance and ETA directly in the chip row when navigation is active.<br>• In `RouteSelectorSheet.kt`, provide a prominent "Take Me Home" ("Heimweg") card/button at the top to initiate return navigation immediately.<br>6. *100% 9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• All user-facing strings SHALL maintain 100% parity across all 9 supported application locales (EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement only (`REQ-MAP-029`). Agent 1 SHALL verify/set the `Lösungsversion` during Stage 5, and Agent 2 SHALL audit its presence during Gate 5 prior to human release approval and ticket closure.<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an assigned Jira ticket (Bug, Improvement, or Feature),<br>• *When* the ticket enters any lifecycle stage,<br>• *Then* Jira Automation SHALL automatically create the corresponding sub-task.<br>• *Given* Agent 1 finishes the stage deliverable and sets it as the sub-task Description,<br>• *When* the sub-task enters `In Überprüfung`,<br>• *Then* Agent 2 SHALL automatically audit the deliverable, post the review comment, and transition to `Freigabe (Human)`.<br>• *Given* Agent 2 audit PASS moving the sub-task to `Erledigt`,<br>• *When* transitioned,<br>• *Then* Jira Automation SHALL advance the parent ticket to the next stage and generate the next sub-task.<br>• *Given* a parent ticket entering Stage 5/6 release verification,<br>• *When* evaluated,<br>• *Then* the parent ticket's `Lösungsversion` SHALL be populated with the active release version, verified by Agent 2 in Gate 5.<br>**Invariants**: Moving parent tickets to `Erledigt` remains an inviolable human-only gate; sub-tasks transition directly to `Erledigt` upon automated Gate audit PASS; direct merges to `develop` without 100% sub-task completion remain strictly forbidden. | Ensure bidirectional ASPICE traceability, automated Jira lifecycle management, and independent AI quality audits without manual developer overhead. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/jira_util.py` | `TST-PRO-006`, `TST-PRO-008` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-015** | **Agent-Driven Git Branching, Conventional Commits, and Develop Merging Protocol.** | The development workflow SHALL mandate agent-driven git lifecycle management for all assigned Jira tickets:<br>1. *Branch Creation*: Upon starting work on any ticket, the agent SHALL verify or switch to `develop` and automatically create/checkout a dedicated branch adhering to naming standards (`feature/ATT-XXX` or `bugfix/ATT-XXX`).<br>2. *Conventional Commits*: The agent SHALL stage files (`git add`) and execute git commits (`git commit`) using the Conventional Commits format (`feat(...)`, `fix(...)`, `docs(...)`, etc.) with ticket reference and asterisk `*` bullet points.<br>3. *Develop Integration*: Upon completion and verification of all sub-tasks and human release approval, the agent SHALL switch to `develop` and merge the ticket branch into `develop` using a non-fast-forward merge (`git merge --no-ff <branch_name> -m "Merge branch '<branch_name>' into develop"`).<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an assigned Jira ticket (`ATT-XXX`),<br>• *When* the agent begins development,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL create and switch to branch `feature/ATT-XXX` or `bugfix/ATT-XXX` off `develop`.<br>• *Given* approved changes across implementation and documentation,<br>• *When* committing work,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL execute `git commit` with a Conventional Commit message using `*` bullet points and ticket reference.<br>• *Given* 100% of sub-tasks in `Erledigt` and human sign-off,<br>• *When* concluding the ticket,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL checkout `develop` and execute `git merge --no-ff <branch_name> -m "Merge branch '<branch_name>' into develop"`.<br>**Invariants**: Direct commits to `master` remain strictly forbidden; unreviewed code MUST NOT be merged into `develop`; sub-tasks complete autonomously via automated audit PASS while parent ticket release approval remains strictly reserved for the human user. | Ensure full git traceability, branch isolation, and non-fast-forward merge history without manual developer overhead. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules` | `TST-PRO-007` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-016** | **Inviolable ASPICE Human Decision Gates & Prevention of Premature Implementation Triggers.** | The development workflow SHALL strictly enforce human decision gate authority across all ASPICE stages, eliminating premature code execution caused by IDE test harness auto-approvals or synthetic prompts:<br>1. *Artifact Metadata Policy (`RequestFeedback: false`)*: Whenever an AI agent creates or updates plan, walkthrough, or analysis artifacts in the IDE, the agent SHALL ALWAYS specify `ArtifactMetadata: { RequestFeedback: false, UserFacing: true, ... }`. If the sub-task is in any status other than `Erledigt`, code modification is STRICTLY BLOCKED until Stage 3 is completed and passes Gate 3 audit.<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an AI agent generating an implementation plan or walkthrough artifact,<br>• *When* the artifact tool is invoked,<br>• *Then* `RequestFeedback` SHALL be set to `false`, preventing IDE review policy auto-approvals.<br>• *Given* an IDE environment emitting a synthetic auto-approval message,<br>• *When* received,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL discard the message and pause execution, refusing to touch code until Jira status is verified.<br>• *Given* an agent entering Stage 4,<br>• *When* preparing to modify production code,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL run `python3 tools/jira_util.py check-gate <Subtask>` and confirm exit code 0 before editing any file.<br>**Invariants**: The 5-stage ASPICE lifecycle, automated Jira sub-task generation, and dual-agent reviews MUST remain fully intact; moving parent tickets to `Erledigt` remains an inviolable human-only gate while sub-tasks complete autonomously via automated Gate audit PASS. | Prevent premature implementation triggers and guarantee absolute compliance with ASPICE Human Decision Gates across all AI tooling environments. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/jira_util.py`, `.agents/rules/aspice_governance.md` | `TST-PRO-009` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-017** | **Process Hardening: Sub-Task Self-Sufficiency, Transition Sequencing, Discovery-First, and Git Finalization.** | The development workflow SHALL enforce four operational process safeguards across all ASPICE lifecycle stages:<br>1. *Sub-Task Self-Sufficiency*: Every lifecycle sub-task MUST stand on its own as an independent audit record. | **REQ-PRO-018** | **Autonomous Multi-Model Independent Review Agent & Automated Gate Audits.** | The development workflow SHALL provide an autonomous, out-of-process review runner (`tools/review_agent.py`) capable of performing independent ASPICE quality gate audits (Gates 1 through 5) using external LLM providers (Google Gemini REST API via `.env.gemini` and Anthropic Claude Messages API via `.env.claude`):<br>1. *Architectural Independence & Memory Decoupling*: The review agent SHALL run in an independent Python process with zero shared conversational memory or prompt history with Agent 1, eliminating self-review confirmation bias.<br>2. *Gate Detection & Context Ingestion*: Given a sub-task key (`ATT-XXX`), the tool SHALL automatically determine the corresponding ASPICE stage and gate from the sub-task summary (`[Analysis]` -> Gate 1, `[Test-Spec]` -> Gate 2, `[Impl-Plan]` -> Gate 3, `[Implementation]` -> Gate 4, `[Test]` -> Gate 5). | **REQ-PRO-019** | **Multi-Account Jira Authentication, Atomic Resolution & Terminal Error Handling.** | The development workflow and CLI tooling (`tools/jira_util.py`, `tools/review_agent.py`) SHALL support role-specific Jira user credentials across three distinct agent roles: Agent 1 (Implementer), Agent 2 (Auditor), and Coordinator (Orchestrator):<br>1. *Role Credentials Configuration*: `.env.jira` SHALL support optional role-specific environment variables (`JIRA_AGENT1_USER`, `JIRA_AGENT1_TOKEN`, `JIRA_AGENT2_USER`, `JIRA_AGENT2_TOKEN`, `JIRA_COORDINATOR_USER`, `JIRA_COORDINATOR_TOKEN`) alongside base default credentials (`JIRA_USER`, `JIRA_TOKEN`).<br>2. *Atomic Resolution & Pair Fallback*: When resolving credentials for any role, if either the username or the API token for that role is missing, the system MUST NOT mix partial credentials; | **REQ-PRO-022** | **Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Modification Hurdle.** | The development workflow and governance tooling SHALL enforce an explicit, auditable archaeological investigation before any existing requirement in `docs/requirements.md` is modified, relaxed, or replaced:<br>1. *Mandatory Archaeological Investigation*: Prior to proposing or applying changes to an existing requirement, the agent/engineer SHALL inspect the requirement's historical git commits (`git log -S <REQ-ID> docs/requirements.md` with timeout and depth bounds), associated Jira tickets, and architectural rationale to understand why the requirement was originally formulated in its current form (Chesterton's Fence principle).<br>2. *Machine-Checkable Archaeology Audit Section*: Any deliverable (Stage 1 Analysis, Stage 2 Test Specification, and Pull Request / Implementation description) that modifies an existing requirement MUST include a dedicated section titled `### Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit` containing four mandatory structured fields:<br>• `Original Requirement ID & Target`: The exact requirement ID slated for alteration (e.g. `REQ-TRK-002`).<br>• `Historical Origin & Commit Trace`: Git commit hash(es), ticket key(s), and original defect/motivation.<br>• `Root Reason for Existing Formulation`: Explicit answer to *Why was this fence built?* (e.g. what bug, crash, regression, or schema constraint originally necessitated this exact phrasing).<br>• `Preservation of Core Invariants`: Explicit justification of *Why is it safe to modify now?*, proving that original system invariants remain protected or explaining why the historical constraint is obsolete.<br>3. *Independent Auditor Gate Enforcement (Gate 2)*: In `tools/review_agent.py`, the Gate 2 audit checklist SHALL explicitly inspect git diffs of `docs/requirements.md`. If existing requirement lines are modified (identified via diff hunk parsing), Gate 2 SHALL verify the presence, completeness, and validity of the archaeology section. Gate 2 SHALL issue `CHALLENGED` or `RECOMMEND REVISION` on any deliverable altering existing requirements without this complete archaeological justification.<br>4. *Dedicated Governance Verification Script (`tools/verify_requirement_governance.py`)*: A standalone verification utility implemented purely in Python 3 standard library SHALL analyze git diffs or deliverable text:<br>• Differentiates modified vs new requirements: detects whether existing requirement IDs were modified via diff analysis against `develop`.<br>• Validates section syntax: uses multiline regex parsing to verify that all four mandatory field labels exist with non-empty content.<br>• Deterministic exit codes: returns exit code `0` on compliance, exit code `1` with schema diagnostics on failure.<br>5. *Legacy Grandfathering*: Existing unmodified requirements remain valid as-is without requiring retroactive archaeology logs.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a branch with git diff modifications to an existing requirement line in `docs/requirements.md`,<br>• *When* `python3 tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` or `review_agent.py` Gate 2 evaluates the deliverable containing all 4 non-empty archaeology fields,<br>• *Then* the validation SHALL succeed with exit code 0.<br>• *Given* a branch modifying an existing requirement in `docs/requirements.md` where any of the 4 mandatory fields is missing or blank,<br>• *When* evaluated by `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` or `review_agent.py` Gate 2,<br>• *Then* the verification script SHALL return exit code 1 with itemized schema errors, and Agent 2 SHALL issue a `CHALLENGED` or `RECOMMEND REVISION` audit verdict.<br>• *Given* a deliverable introducing only net-new requirements (new row with a new ID not existing in base),<br>• *When* evaluated by `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py`,<br>• *Then* the script SHALL classify the change as net-new and exit with code 0 without demanding an archaeology section.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero external pip dependencies; APK runtime code and assets MUST NOT be modified; human decision gate authority remains inviolable. | Prevent regressions and accidental destruction of hard-won architectural protections by enforcing the Chesterton's Fence principle prior to modifying established requirements. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/review_agent.py`, `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` | `TST-PRO-015` | Verified |

transition `Freigabe` moves subtasks directly from `In Überprüfung` to `Erledigt` upon passing Agent 2 Gate audit.<br>• *Parent Tickets*: Standard Jira tickets (Bug, Feature, Improvement) mandate an explicit `Final Review (Human)` state following Stage 5 (`Test`). human decision gate on parent tickets remains inviolable; Gate 1 through Gate 5 quality checks remain mandatory. | Eliminate context window inflation and instruction drift, provide structured templates, enable rapid UI and backlog workflows, streamline subtask transitions, and formalize the 3-phase agile sprint lifecycle. | `.agents/skills/`, `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/jira_util.py` | `TST-PRO-017` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-025** | **Automated Test Execution Acceleration, Worker Parallelism, and Resource-Safe Caching.** | The build and test execution system SHALL accelerate automated unit test suite execution while guaranteeing host stability, bounded resource consumption, and zero cross-test state pollution:<br>1. *Multi-Worker Parallelism (`app/build.gradle`)*:<br>• The build system SHALL configure `testOptions.unitTests.all` with dynamic hardware-adaptive worker forking: `maxParallelForks = Math.max(1, Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2)`.<br>• On an 8-core CPU system, exactly 4 parallel test worker processes (`GradleWorkerMain`) SHALL execute test classes concurrently.<br>2. *Periodic Worker Recycling (`forkEvery`)*:<br>• The build system SHALL configure `forkEvery = 80`. Each test worker process SHALL be terminated and replaced with a fresh JVM after executing 80 test classes.<br>• Periodic recycling SHALL completely flush the JVM Metaspace and heap, permanently eliminating MockK/ByteBuddy classloader retention and stop-the-world Full GC pauses.<br>3. *Defensive Heap Allocation Capping (`minHeapSize` / `maxHeapSize`)*:<br>• To prevent host OOM or swap thrashing, each worker fork SHALL be constrained to `minHeapSize = "256m"` and `maxHeapSize = "768m"`.<br>• Total concurrent heap allocation across all 4 worker forks SHALL be strictly capped at $\le 3.072\text{ GB}$, leaving over 75% of physical memory available for the host OS and Gradle daemon.<br>4. *Optimized JIT Compiler Flags (`jvmArgs`)*:<br>• Test worker JVMs SHALL configure `-XX:+TieredCompilation`, `-XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1` (prioritizing fast C1 JIT compilation over heavyweight C2 optimizations, optimal for short-lived unit test forks), and `-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8`.<br>5. *Decoupled Task Execution & Local Build Caching (`gradle.properties`)*:<br>• `gradle.properties` SHALL declare `org.gradle.parallel=true` (enabling parallel execution of decoupled project tasks) and `org.gradle.caching=true` (enabling Gradle's local build cache for deterministically cacheable task outputs).<br>6. *Thread-Safe In-Memory Localization DOM Cache (`LocalizationTestCache.kt`)*:<br>• The test infrastructure SHALL provide a shared, thread-safe in-memory cache helper `LocalizationTestCache` backed by `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Map<String, String>>`.<br>• Strings for each locale SHALL be parsed from disk at most once per worker JVM via atomic `computeIfAbsent`, returning unmodifiable string maps (`Collections.unmodifiableMap`) to guarantee zero cross-test mutation.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-PRO-025`), establishing formal build and test infrastructure standards under Process Epic `ATT-232` (*Process & Engineering Workflow*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: `gradle.properties` historically had `# org.gradle.parallel=true` commented out due to early Gradle 2.x/3.x incubator instability. In modern Gradle and AGP, parallel task execution and the build cache are mature production-grade features. `testOptions` was never configured in `app/build.gradle`, defaulting to legacy single-worker execution.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Single-worker sequential execution was the zero-configuration default. As the test suite expanded from ~50 classes to 436 classes, cumulative execution time scaled linearly to 7–9 minutes.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Process-Level Test Isolation: Gradle's `maxParallelForks` creates separate operating system JVM processes (`GradleWorkerMain`), guaranteeing that static fields, global mocks (`mockkStatic`), and thread-locals remain 100% isolated between workers. In-memory Room/SQLite instances are worker-local. Zero Flakiness: All 436 test classes MUST pass cleanly with 100% determinism.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an 8-core CPU workstation,<br>• *When* `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is executed,<br>• *Then* Gradle SHALL spawn 4 parallel test worker processes (`maxParallelForks = 4`).<br>• *Given* the complete 436-class test suite,<br>• *When* `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` is executed,<br>• *Then* total execution duration SHALL decrease by at least 40% compared to baseline single-worker sequential execution (targeting $\le 4\text{ minutes}$).<br>• *Given* parallel multi-worker test execution,<br>• *When* running the complete test suite,<br>• *Then* 100% of test classes and test cases SHALL pass with zero race conditions, flakiness, or test cross-contamination.<br>• *Given* 4 concurrent test workers running simultaneously,<br>• *When* measuring worker JVM memory allocations,<br>• *Then* each worker SHALL NOT exceed 768 MB heap, capping aggregate worker memory at $\le 3.1\text{ GB}$.<br>• *Given* concurrent access to `LocalizationTestCache`,<br>• *When* multiple test classes request strings for the same locale,<br>• *Then* `strings.xml` SHALL be parsed from disk at most once per worker JVM, and returned maps SHALL be strictly immutable.<br><br>**Invariants**: Test isolation preserved; zero flaky tests; memory consumption bounded to safe host limits. | Dramatically reduce full test suite execution time from 7-9 minutes to under 3.5 minutes while bounding memory consumption, preventing MockK/ByteBuddy GC thrashing, and ensuring complete test isolation. | `app/build.gradle`, `gradle.properties`, `LocalizationTestCache.kt` | `TST-PRO-018` | Verified |

*Rule 36: Single Source of Truth & DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) — Shared Code Over Duplication*: Mandatory reuse of shared utilities and composables; canonical formatters (`DistanceFormatter`, `AltitudeFormatter`, `SpeedFormatter`, `PaceFormatter`, Compose `LocalMetricFormatter`) and unit math (`MyHelper.mps2userUnit()`, `UserUnit2mps()`) MUST be used for all metric presentation (inline string formatting like `String.format("%.1f km", ...)` and manual unit conversions are strictly forbidden); proactive elimination of divergent logic.<br>  - *Rule 20: Database & DTO Mapping Symmetry*: Symmetric single-item and batch `fromCursor` mappings.<br>  - *Rule 21: Specific Direct Platform Intents Over Generic App Settings*.<br>  - *Rule 29: Defensive Service Lifecycle Finalization & FGS Permission Gating*: Permission-gated FGS types and unconditional SQLite session finalization within guaranteed `try/finally` blocks.<br>  - *Rule 30: Developer Tool Host Pre-Flight Diagnostics*.<br>  - *Rule 34: Chesterton's Fence for Empty Callback Lambdas & Gesture Contract Tests*.<br>  - *Rule 35: Clean Hardware Teardown and Orphan Defense on Persistence Deletion*.<br>  - *Test Framework Invariants*: Strict prohibition of `returnDefaultValues = true`; phased execution distinguishing Stage 4 unit tests (5–15s) from Stage 5 clean-room regression (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`).<br>4. *Retrospective Routing Governance for Future Retros (Rule 11)*:<br>• Future retrospective improvements SHALL be routed systematically according to domain: process/gate/ceremony learnings to `.agents/rules/aspice_governance.md`, visual/UI/theme learnings to `docs/design_guidelines.md`, and technical/coding/architectural learnings to `docs/coding_standards.md`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-PRO-026`), establishing formal Document Triad architecture across `.agents/rules/aspice_governance.md`, `docs/design_guidelines.md`, and `docs/coding_standards.md`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-39.1 (`ATT-728`) established `.agents/rules/aspice_governance.md`. | **REQ-STB-002** | **Resilient TrackerService Foreground Service Lifecycle & Crash Protection.** | The system SHALL ensure the workout tracking service (`TrackerService`) operates with resilient lifecycle management and crash immunity across Android 14+ (API 34+) background launch restrictions:<br>1. *START_STICKY Preservation*: The system SHALL retain `Service.START_STICKY` as the return value of `TrackerService.onStartCommand` to allow automatic background recreation and continuous tracking when the process is killed during active workouts.<br>2. *Background Restart Precondition Guard*: When `onStartCommand` is invoked with `intent == null` (system recreation after kill):<br>• *If `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` is granted*: The service SHALL proceed to promote to a location foreground service (`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_LOCATION`) and continue tracking.<br>• *If `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` is NOT granted*: The service SHALL NOT attempt an illegal background promotion to location FGS; instead, it SHALL safely preserve workout metrics to SQLite, post a user-facing notification informing the user that tracking was paused, and call `stopSelf()`.<br>3. *Exception Shielding*: All invocations of `startForeground(...)` in `TrackerService` SHALL be encapsulated in a `try ... catch (SecurityException | IllegalStateException)` block, safely logging any unexpected platform launch restriction exceptions and calling `stopSelf()` rather than crashing the application process.<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an active workout on Android 14+ where the user has granted `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`,<br>• *When* the OS kills `TrackerService` and recreates it with `intent == null`,<br>• *Then* `TrackerService` SHALL successfully call `startForeground` with location type and continue tracking.<br>• *Given* an active workout on Android 14+ where the user has ONLY granted foreground location,<br>• *When* the OS kills `TrackerService` and recreates it with `intent == null`,<br>• *Then* `TrackerService` SHALL NOT crash with `SecurityException`, but SHALL safely stop itself, preserve workout data, and notify the user.<br>• *Given* any unexpected `SecurityException` during `startForeground`,<br>• *When* `startForeground` is executed,<br>• *Then* the exception SHALL be caught, logged, and handled cleanly without process death.<br>**Invariants**: `START_STICKY` MUST be retained; normal foreground workout tracking initiated by the user MUST continue to operate with location foreground service notification intact. | Ensure workout tracking resilience via START_STICKY while preventing fatal SecurityException crashes on Android 14+ when restarted in the background without background location permissions. | `TrackerService.java`, `AndroidManifest.xml` | `TST-STB-002` | Verified |

record in SQLite (`FINISHED == 0`),<br>• *When* the user launches the application normally,<br>• *Then* the application SHALL prompt the user with `StartOrResumeDialog` to resume or start fresh rather In `MapDetailLayout.kt`, zone thresholds SHALL be resolved and memoized at the top level via `remember(bSportType, context)` and `remember(context)`, passing resolved threshold models directly into dependent child composables (`ElevationProfile` and `TelemetryMetricGraph`).<br>3. *Optimized O(log N) Scrubbing Point Search (`TelemetryMetricUtils.kt`)*: Point selection along the workout scrubbing timeline SHALL utilize an allocation-free binary search algorithm `findNearestPoint(points: List<PathPoint>, targetValue: Double, isTimeDomain: Boolean = false): PathPoint?`. Exploiting the monotonic ordering of recorded `PathPoint` lists (sorted by `distance` or `timeSec`), the search SHALL identify the closest trackpoint in $O(\log N)$ comparisons with exact numerical parity to linear nearest-neighbor resolution, avoiding allocation of temporary closures or full list traversals on the UI thread during drag gestures.<br>4. *Scrubbing Point Search Replacement*: Ad-hoc linear scans `pathPoints.minByOrNull { abs(it.distance - selectedDistance) }` and `it.timeSec` in `MapDetailLayout.kt` and `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` SHALL be replaced with `TelemetryMetricUtils.findNearestPoint`.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete inspecting a workout in `MapDetailLayout`, `ElevationProfile`, or `TelemetryMetricGraph`,<br>• *When* HR or Power zone thresholds are configured in settings,<br>• *Then* `TelemetryZoneMath.loadHeartRateThresholds` and `loadPowerThresholds` SHALL load the exact thresholds corresponding to the workout's `BSportType` with 100% numerical parity.<br>• *Given* unconfigured or invalid ($\le 0$) zone settings,<br>• *Then* the threshold factory functions SHALL return `null` safely without runtime exceptions or partial zone initialization.<br>• *Given* a recorded `PathPoint` track containing $N \ge 1$ points monotonically sorted by distance and time,<br>• *When* scrubbing interactively to any distance or timestamp (including exact match, intermediate positions, boundary values, or out-of-range targets),<br>• *Then* `TelemetryMetricUtils.findNearestPoint` SHALL return the identical nearest `PathPoint` in $O(\log N)$ comparisons that `minByOrNull` would have selected.<br>• *Given* an empty `PathPoint` list,<br>• *When* `findNearestPoint` is invoked,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `null` safely.<br><br>**Invariants**: Telemetry data models, visual graph rendering styles, gesture detection contracts, and unit test pass rates MUST NOT regress. | Eliminate duplicate zone loading boilerplate across Aftermath visual analytics and eliminate UI thread frame stutters during timeline scrubbing by upgrading point lookup to O(log N). | `TelemetryZoneMath.kt`, `TelemetryMetricUtils.kt`, `MapDetailLayout.kt`, `ElevationProfile.kt`, `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` | `TST-UI-219` | Verified |

| **REQ-UI-266** | **Aftermath/Details: Immediate Collapsing Header Quick Return Expansion upon Downward Scrolling.** | The system SHALL restore immediate Quick Return downward header expansion in `CollapsingAppBarNestedScrollConnection.kt` and `MapDetailLayout.kt` (ATT-2304):<br>1. *Immediate Downward Expansion in `onPreScroll`*: When scrolling downward (`available.y > 0f`) and the header is currently in a collapsed or partially collapsed state (`rawOffset < 0f`), `CollapsingAppBarNestedScrollConnection.onPreScroll` SHALL consume available delta up to `0f`, immediately translating `appBarOffset` towards `0`. Once `rawOffset == -appBarMaxHeight.toFloat()`, `onPreScroll` SHALL return `Offset.Zero`, allowing child scroll containers to scroll their contents upward without locking.<br>3. *Sub-Pixel Precision Invariant*: The connection SHALL maintain high-precision floating-point delta accumulation in `rawOffset: Float`, eliminating integer truncation micro-stutters (`available.y.toInt()`), with `appBarOffset` exposed as `rawOffset.roundToInt()`.<br>4. *Child Scroll Coordination*: Child scroll containers (e.g. `lowerColumn` in `MapDetailLayout`, `LazyColumn` in `WorkoutTabsScreen`, `WorkoutSummariesListFragment`, `SegmentsTabsScreen`, etc.) SHALL receive full unconsumed scroll deltas once the header reaches its respective boundary (0 when expanding downward, `-appBarMaxHeight` when collapsing upward).<br>5. *Configurable Quick Return Mode*: `CollapsingAppBarNestedScrollConnection` SHALL provide a `quickReturn: Boolean = true` parameter (defaulting to `true`), allowing callers full control while restoring Quick Return globally by default.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines and supersedes Clause 1 of `REQ-UI-254` (*Aftermath/Details: Non-Blocking Nested Scroll Dispatch, Sub-Pixel Precision & Optimized High-Density Metadata Rendering in MapDetailLayout*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint `2026-40.14` (`ATT-2178`, commit `91fb65c1` and `083d1e04`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Clause 1 in `REQ-UI-254` deferred downward scroll consumption to `onPostScroll` based on a concern that downward gestures in lower analytics charts would squash the view.
