| **REQ-UI-272** | **Elevation Profile Adaptive X-Axis Tick Spacing and Dynamic Label Collision Prevention.** | The system SHALL eliminate overlapping distance and time tick labels on the X-axis of the elevation profile (`ElevationProfile.kt`) across all card previews (`RouteItem`, `SegmentItem`, `WorkoutSummary`) and detailed inspection views (`MapDetailLayout`, `TrackOnMapScreen`, `SensorGridScreen`) (ATT-2385):<br>1. *Adaptive Step Interval Calibration (`ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt`)*: `ElevationProfileZoomMath.calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep` SHALL provide balanced intermediate step increments for short and mid-range tracks. For metric units: `> 50_000` $\implies$ 10,000 m; `> 20_000` $\implies$ 5,000 m; `> 10_000` $\implies$ 2,000 m; `> 5_000` $\implies$ 1,000 m; `> 2_000` $\implies$ 500 m; `> 800` $\implies$ 250 m; `> 300` $\implies$ 100 m; `> 150` $\implies$ 50 m; else $\implies$ 25 m. For imperial units: `> 30` $\implies$ 5 mi; `> 10` $\implies$ 2 mi; `> 3` $\implies$ 1 mi; `> 1` $\implies$ 0.5 mi; `> 0.5` $\implies$ 0.25 mi; `> 0.2` $\implies$ 0.1 mi; else $\implies$ 0.05 mi. The step calculation MAY accept an optional canvas width parameter.<br>2. *Dynamic Clearance Invariant & Adjacent Label Collision Guard (`ElevationProfile.kt`)*: In both distance and time domain X-axis rendering loops, the system SHALL track the rightmost horizontal pixel coordinate of the previously rendered label (`lastDrawnRightX`). An intermediate candidate tick at canvas coordinate `x` with label text width $w_{\text{label}}$ SHALL be rendered if and only if: (a) Start clearance: $x - \frac{w_{\text{label}}}{2} \ge \text{startClearanceThreshold}$ (where $\text{startClearanceThreshold} = \text{startLabelWidth} + \text{minSpacingPx}$ when `startLabel` is drawn, or $\text{minSpacingPx}$ otherwise); (b) Preceding label clearance: $x - \frac{w_{\text{label}}}{2} \ge \text{lastDrawnRightX} + \text{minSpacingPx}$; (c) Terminal clearance: $x + \frac{w_{\text{label}}}{2} \le \text{width} - \text{endLabelWidth} - \text{minSpacingPx}$, where $\text{minSpacingPx} \ge 24.\text{dp.toPx()}$.<br>3. *Synchronized Tick Mark Suppression*: When an intermediate candidate tick label is suppressed due to insufficient clearance, the vertical tick mark line (`drawLine`) at position `x` SHALL likewise be suppressed, ensuring tick marks and labels remain 100% synchronized.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines Clause 5 of `REQ-UI-192` (*Interactive Elevation Profile Zoom, Pan & Centered Scaling Navigation*) and `REQ-UI-201` (*Synchronized Multi-Metric Scrubbing on Elevation Profile with Configurable X-Axis Domain Architecture*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: `ATT-527` (Sprint 2026-40.4) introduced initial `calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep`; `ATT-1391` (Sprint 2026-40.5) added time-domain ticks; `ATT-1819` / `REQ-UI-220` (Sprint 2026-40.7) introduced `shouldRenderMilestoneLabel` for telemetry charts.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ElevationProfile.kt` originally used a static `x > 60f` threshold and coarse step thresholds (jumping from 500m straight down to 100m at 1,500m), without dynamic label width collision checking.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Elevation bounds sanitization (`REQ-UI-126`), horizontal zooming/panning (`REQ-UI-192`), contextual zoom control suppression in preview cards (`REQ-UI-197`), and scrubbing accuracy remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an elevation profile for a segment or route of distance 1.47 km rendered on a standard preview card,<br>• *When* the X-axis is drawn,<br>• *Then* intermediate ticks SHALL render with a step of 250 m or 500 m, every label SHALL maintain at least 24 dp clearance from adjacent labels, and zero labels SHALL collide or overlap with each other or with the 1.47 km terminal label.<br>• *Given* any track distance from 50 m to 200 km rendered on any canvas width,<br>• *When* the elevation profile X-axis is rendered,<br>• *Then* all rendered distance or time labels SHALL satisfy the clearance invariants with zero overlapping text.<br>• *Given* `ElevationProfileZoomMathTest`,<br>• *When* executed,<br>• *Then* adaptive distance step tests and collision guard unit tests SHALL pass with 100% success rate.<br><br>**Invariants**: Grade color mapping, vertical profile height, multi-touch pinch zoom, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Eliminate overlapping distance and time tick labels on elevation profile X-axis via adaptive step intervals and dynamic clearance collision prevention. | `ElevationProfile.kt`, `ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt` | `TST-UI-232` | Verified |

| **REQ-MAP-036** | **Known Locations: Heim-Basis Redundant Badge Excision & Start-Count Home Resolution Alignment.** | The system SHALL excise the redundant "Heim-Basis" badge chip from `KnownLocationCard.kt`, unify home location resolution across domain repositories and navigation engines, and automatically display the Home icon on the effective home-base when no explicit designation exists (ATT-2629):<br>1. *Unified Home Location Resolution Engine (`HomeLocationResolver.kt`)*:<br>• `HomeLocationResolver` SHALL expose `fun resolveHomeLocationId(locations: List<MyLocation>): Long?`.<br>• It SHALL evaluate candidate locations according to a strict 3-tier priority hierarchy:<br>  - Tier 1 (Explicit User Designation): If any location has `isHome == true`, return its `id`.<br>  - Tier 2 (Workout Start Frequency Fallback): If no explicit designation exists, return the `id` of the location with the maximum `hitCount` among locations where `hitCount > 0`. If multiple locations share the identical maximum `hitCount > 0`, the first one encountered SHALL be returned.<br>  - Tier 3 (First Location Fallback): If no location has `hitCount > 0`, return the `id` of the first location in the list.<br>  - If the list is empty, return `null`.<br>• `HomeLocationResolver.resolveHomeLocation(knownLocationsManager: KnownLocationsDatabaseManager): HomeDestination?` SHALL delegate its candidate selection to `resolveHomeLocationId(rawLocations)`.<br>2. *Repository & Domain Model State Alignment (`KnownLocationsRepository.kt`, `KnownLocationItem`)*:<br>• In `KnownLocationsRepository.loadLocations()`, the system SHALL query `rawLocations = databaseManager.allLocations`.<br>• It SHALL evaluate `effectiveHomeId = HomeLocationResolver.resolveHomeLocationId(rawLocations)`.<br>• When mapping `rawLocations` to `KnownLocationItem`, `KnownLocationItem.isHome` SHALL evaluate to `(loc.id == effectiveHomeId)`.<br>• This ensures `locationsFlow` emits items where exactly one location has `isHome == true` whenever saved locations exist, perfectly matching the return navigation destination.<br>3. *Redundant Badge Excision in Presentation Layer (`KnownLocationsScreen.kt`)*:<br>• In `KnownLocationsScreen.kt` (`KnownLocationCard`), the redundant `Surface` badge chip displaying `R.string.known_locations_home_badge` with test tag `location_home_badge_${item.id}` inside the metadata `FlowRow` SHALL be completely excised.<br>• The primary title row Home icon (`Icons.Default.Home`) with test tag `location_home_icon_${item.id}`, tinted `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary`, and accessibility description `@string/known_locations_home_base` SHALL remain the single, elegant, and prominent indicator of home-base identity.<br>4. *Explicit User Designation & Transactional Exclusivity Preservation*:<br>• Setting a home location via `KnownLocationsViewModel.setHomeLocation(id)` or `EditKnownLocationDialog` SHALL atomically mark that location as `is_home = 1` in SQLite while clearing all other rows to `is_home = 0`.<br>• Clearing the home location via `clearHomeLocation()` SHALL reset all rows in SQLite to `is_home = 0`. Upon the subsequent repository refresh, the location with the highest start count (`hitCount > 0`, or first) SHALL automatically resume acting as the effective home-base, updating the UI reactively.<br>5. *100% 9-Language Localization & String Resource Integrity*:<br>• String resource `known_locations_home_base` SHALL be preserved for the Home icon's accessibility description across all 9 supported application locales (`values/`, `values-de/`, `values-es/`, `values-fr/`, `values-it/`, `values-ja/`, `values-nl/`, `values-pl/`, `values-pt/`).<br>• String resource `known_locations_home_badge` MAY be retained to prevent breaking legacy references or translations, but MUST NOT be rendered in `KnownLocationCard`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines Clause 3 of `REQ-MAP-034` (*Designated Home-Base Selection for Return Navigation & Substring Disambiguation*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2472`, Sprint `2026-41.1`, commit `0994f794`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In ATT-2472, both the title icon and a dedicated metadata badge chip were introduced to ensure maximum visual discoverability when home-base designation was first launched. At the time, `KnownLocationsRepository` mapped `isHome = loc.isHome` directly from the raw database query, omitting the fallback logic in `HomeLocationResolver` and leaving the UI without an active indicator when no explicit home was designated.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Single-home transactional exclusivity in SQLite (`StartLocation2Altitude.db`), explicit user designation strictly overriding start-count heuristics, context menu and edit dialog actions (`setHomeLocation`, `clearHomeLocation`), return navigation routing integrity, thread safety on `KnownLocationsDB-Thread`, and 100% full-suite clean-room unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a location item with `isHome == true`,<br>• *When* `KnownLocationCard` renders,<br>• *Then* the Home icon beside the title SHALL be displayed, and NO "Heim-Basis" badge chip SHALL be rendered in the metadata `FlowRow`.<br>• *Given* saved locations where Location A has `isHome = true` (hitCount = 2) and Location B has `isHome = false` (hitCount = 50),<br>• *When* `KnownLocationsRepository.loadLocations()` or `HomeLocationResolver.resolveHomeLocationId()` evaluates,<br>• *Then* Location A SHALL be resolved as the home location (`effectiveHomeId == Location A.id`).<br>• *Given* saved locations where all locations have `isHome = false`, Location A has `hitCount = 10`, and Location B has `hitCount = 25`,<br>• *When* `KnownLocationsRepository.loadLocations()` executes,<br>• *Then* Location B SHALL have `item.isHome == true` and Location A SHALL have `item.isHome == false`.<br>• *Given* saved locations where all locations have `isHome = false` and all `hitCount == 0`,<br>• *When* `KnownLocationsRepository.loadLocations()` executes,<br>• *Then* the first location in the list SHALL have `item.isHome == true`.<br>• *Given* an empty list of saved locations,<br>• *When* `HomeLocationResolver.resolveHomeLocationId(emptyList())` is called,<br>• *Then* it SHALL safely return `null` without throwing an exception.<br>• *Given* Location B resolved as default home due to highest start count,<br>• *When* the athlete explicitly designates Location A as home,<br>• *Then* Location A becomes `isHome == true`.<br>• *When* the athlete subsequently clears explicit home designation,<br>• *Then* Location B automatically resumes `isHome == true`.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite schema version 6 and column `is_home integer default 0` in `StartLocation2Altitude.db`, return navigation math, and 100% full-suite unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Excise redundant Heim-Basis badge chip from KnownLocationCard, unify home location resolution across domain repositories and navigation engines, and default to location with most starts when no home-base set. | `HomeLocationResolver.kt`, `KnownLocationsRepository.kt`, `KnownLocationsScreen.kt` | `TST-MAP-038` | Verified +| **REQ-MAP-037** | **Route Waypoint Marker Badge Diameter Optimization & Glanceability Proportional Scaling.** | The system SHALL optimize the default diameter of circular route waypoint badge markers to 22 dp, proportionally scale outer contrast and inner white halo stroke geometry with crisp hairline clamping, and configure composable map layers to prevent route polyline track occlusion while preserving sharp Maki glyph glanceability (ATT-2628):<br>1. *Default Marker Diameter Constant & Configuration (`MapUtils.kt`)*:<br>• `MapUtils.kt` SHALL define `const val DEFAULT_WAYPOINT_MARKER_SIZE_DP = 22`.<br>• `createWaypointBadgeMarker(context: Context, type: WaypointType, sizeDp: Int = DEFAULT_WAYPOINT_MARKER_SIZE_DP): BitmapDescriptor?` SHALL adopt `DEFAULT_WAYPOINT_MARKER_SIZE_DP` as its default parameter value, achieving a 52.7% reduction in visual surface area ($380.1\text{ dp}^2$ vs $804.2\text{ dp}^2$ at 32 dp).<br>2. *Proportional Double-Ring Stroke & Central Glyph Geometry Scaling*:<br>• The circular badge rendering pipeline SHALL scale stroke widths proportionally using scaling ratio `scale = sizeDp / 32f`.<br>• Outer dark contrast hairline / shadow stroke width SHALL evaluate to `(1f * density * scale).coerceAtLeast(0.75f * density)` with color `0x33000000`.<br>• Inner crisp white halo ring stroke width SHALL evaluate to `(2f * density * scale).coerceAtLeast(1.25f * density)` with color `Color.WHITE`.<br>• The category-filled disc SHALL occupy `fillRadius = haloRadius - (haloStrokeWidth / 2f)`.<br>• The centered white Maki glyph SHALL be rendered with `iconSizePx = (sizePx * 0.55f).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)` and tinted white (`Color.WHITE`).<br>3. *Composable Map Layer Integration (`MapLayers.kt`)*:<br>• `RouteWaypointsLayer` SHALL accept parameter `markerSizeDp: Int = DEFAULT_WAYPOINT_MARKER_SIZE_DP`.<br>• It SHALL invoke `createWaypointBadgeMarker(ctx, waypoint.type, markerSizeDp)` and key cached bitmap descriptors by `remember(waypoint.type, context, markerSizeDp)`.<br>4. *Visual Balance in Route Previews & Interactive Maps (`PathPreviewMap.kt`, `RouteOverlayLayer`)*:<br>• Waypoint markers rendered across both full-screen map views and route card preview thumbnails SHALL inherit the compact 22 dp badge size, eliminating polyline track occlusion and visual clutter while preserving sharp Maki glyph legibility.<br>5. *Category Color & Resource Invariants Preservation*:<br>• All 10 distinct waypoint category colors (`#E65100`, `#0288D1`, `#2E7D32`, `#00695C`, `#EF6C00`, `#6A1B9A`, `#D32F2F`, `#C62828`, `#1565C0`, `#546E7A`), Mapbox Maki CC0 glyph linkage, and 9-language localization parity SHALL remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines Clause 3 & Clause 4 of `REQ-MAP-033` (*High-Contrast Maki POI Waypoint Badges, Shelter Classification & Substring Disambiguation*), targeting `MapUtils.kt` and `MapLayers.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2461`, Sprint `2026-41.1`, commit `9b8fc6a9`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In ATT-2461, circular badge markers were introduced to replace bare unbacked vector icons, which suffered from poor contrast against varied satellite/terrain maps. A 32 dp diameter was initially chosen as a conservative reference to ensure glyph legibility. However, physical on-device evaluation during the Sprint 2026-41.1 review revealed that 32 dp markers are excessively large, creating polyline track occlusion and visual clutter on high-density screens.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: All 10 distinct waypoint category colors, white Maki vector glyphs centered at 55% of diameter, double-ring contrast geometry, InfoWindow tap interactions, route card thumbnail rendering, and 100% full-suite unit test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* `createWaypointBadgeMarker` called without an explicit `sizeDp` argument,<br>• *When* the marker bitmap is generated,<br>• *Then* the bitmap dimensions SHALL match `22 dp * density` (`DEFAULT_WAYPOINT_MARKER_SIZE_DP == 22`).<br>• *Given* `RouteWaypointsLayer` rendering on a full-screen interactive map or inside `PathPreviewMap`,<br>• *When* composing waypoint markers,<br>• *Then* markers SHALL render with 22 dp diameter, leaving underlying route tracks and map details unobscured.<br>• *Given* any supported screen density (mdpi to xxxhdpi),<br>• *When* generating 22 dp badge markers,<br>• *Then* outer dark hairline stroke SHALL be $\ge 0.75\text{ dp}$ and white halo ring SHALL be $\ge 1.25\text{ dp}$, preventing stroke drop-out or blurring.<br>• *Given* all 10 `WaypointType`s,<br>• *When* rendered at 22 dp,<br>• *Then* each marker SHALL present its distinct category color, crisp halo, and centered white Maki glyph.<br><br>**Invariants**: Category color mapping, Maki icon drawables, SQLite schema in `Routes.db`, and 100% full-suite unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Optimize route waypoint badge marker diameter from 32 dp to 22 dp with proportional stroke scaling and layer configurability to improve map glanceability and prevent polyline occlusion. | `MapUtils.kt`, `MapLayers.kt`, `PathPreviewMap.kt` | `TST-MAP-039` | Verified |

heading, ordered by proximity.<br>3. *Streamlined In-Ride Sheet & Redundant Prompt Excision (`RouteSelectorSheet.kt`)*:<br>• The separate `AutoDetectedRouteBanner` prompt widget inside `RouteSelectorSheet.kt` SHALL be excised. PT).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines Clause 2 & Clause 3 of `REQ-UI-279` (*Branded Route Selection Entry Point on Control Tracking Screen*) and Clause 3 of `REQ-UI-280` (*Streamlined Route Selector*), and integrates with `REQ-UI-282` (*Mid-Ride Route Selector Return Navigation Entry Point*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Tickets `ATT-2458` (commit `69dfa539`), `ATT-2459` (commit `cf4aafd8`), and `ATT-2462` (commit `2837bc39`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: RouteSelectorViewModel | **REQ-UI-297** | **Distance-Weighted Elevation Profile Gaussian Smoothing & Continuous Slope Grade Evaluation.** | The system SHALL smooth elevation profile coordinate streams and evaluate terrain slope gradient using a physically-grounded, distance-weighted Gaussian kernel filter with exact boundary renormalization, eliminating discrete sensor quantization staircase artifacts (ATT-2512, ATT-2746):<br>1. *Distance-Weighted Gaussian Kernel Engine (`ElevationSmoothingMath.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL encapsulate elevation profile smoothing in a dedicated pure mathematical engine `ElevationSmoothingMath`.<br>• For each point $i$ with monotonic cumulative distance $d_i$ and raw altitude $a_i$, neighboring points $j$ within a spatial cutoff radius $3\sigma = 63.0\text{ m}$ ($\sigma = 21.0\text{ m}$ default) SHALL be weighted by spatial distance: $w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{(d_j - d_i)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)$.<br>• Parameter `cutoff` in `smoothAltitudes` SHALL default dynamically to `3.0 * sigma`.<br>• The smoothed altitude $\hat{a}_i$ SHALL be strictly normalized by the sum of actual neighboring weights: $\hat{a}_i = \frac{\sum_{j} w_{ij} a_j}{\sum_{j} w_{ij}}$.<br>• Boundary conditions at track start ($d \approx 0$) and track end ($d \approx D_{total}$) SHALL apply dynamic renormalization over the truncated spatial window without zero-padding or artificial boundary sagging/peaking.<br>2. *Linear-Time Bounded Complexity ($O(N)$)*:<br>• Smoothing over monotonically ordered distance points SHALL utilize a sliding two-pointer window maintaining $[d_i - 3\sigma, d_i + 3\sigma]$, achieving strictly linear $O(N)$ computational complexity and sub-2ms latency on dense tracks ($N > 10,000$).<br>• Array operations SHALL execute via primitive `DoubleArray` with zero object allocations in the inner convolution loop.<br>3. *Continuous Slope Grade Evaluation (`ElevationProfile.kt`)*:<br>• Local terrain gradient between adjacent points SHALL evaluate from smoothed altitudes: $\text{grade}_i = \frac{\hat{a}_{i+1} - \hat{a}_i}{d_{i+1} - d_i} \times 100$.<br>• Continuous grade evaluation SHALL eliminate alternating 0% flat plateaus and 15%+ artificial step jumps on quantized sensor streams (e.g. 0.2m–0.4m steps), rendering natural, smooth grade zone coloration (`Zone1`..`Zone5`).<br>4. *Configurable Spatial Bandwidth in Tuning Preferences (`TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `AdvancedTuningDialog.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL declare `elevationSmoothingSigmaMeters` in `TuningPreferencesDataStore` with default `21.0f` and safety bounds $[10.0\text{f}, 50.0\text{f}]$.<br>• `AftermathAnalysisSection` inside `AdvancedTuningDialog` SHALL render an adjustable slider (`TuningSliderItem`) allowing the athlete to customize $\sigma$ between 10m and 50m in 1m step increments.<br>• Tapping "Reset to Factory Defaults" SHALL restore `elevationSmoothingSigmaMeters` to `21.0f`.<br>• All new string resources (`tuning_elevation_smoothing_sigma_title`, `tuning_elevation_smoothing_sigma_desc`) SHALL maintain 100% parity across all 9 supported locales.<br>5. *Dynamic Profile Reactivity (`ElevationProfile.kt`)*:<br>• `ElevationProfile` SHALL accept an optional parameter `smoothingSigma: Double? = null`. When null, it reactively observes `tuningConfig.elevationSmoothingSigmaMeters.toDouble()` and dynamically re-evaluates smoothed profile geometry whenever the preference changes.<br>6. *Preservation of Invariants*:<br>• True topographic summits, passes, and valleys SHALL be preserved without over-smoothing.<br>• Workout summary ascent/descent calculations, database persistence (`Segments.db`, `WorkoutSummaries.db`), Strava sync, and telemetry graphs MUST NOT be modified.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines `REQ-UI-297` (*Distance-Weighted Elevation Profile Gaussian Smoothing & Continuous Slope Grade Evaluation*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2512`, commit `7630148d`, sprint `2026-41.3`, refined in `ATT-2746`, sprint `2026-41.4`, Epic `ATT-2582` (*[Epic] Segments: Live Tracking, Exploration & Route Integration*).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Commit `7630148d` established $\sigma = 35.0\,\text{m}$ ($3\sigma = 105.0\,\text{m}$) to eliminate 0.2m–0.4m sensor quantization plateaus and derivative zebra artifacts. While mathematically robust, $\sigma = 35.0\,\text{m}$ acts slightly too aggressively on punchy climbs and short terrain features, damping authentic terrain inflections.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Reducing default bandwidth to $\sigma = 21.0\,\text{m}$ ($3\sigma = 63.0\,\text{m}$) continues to span multiple GPS/barometer points (1 Hz, 2–8 m spacing on climbs), reliably preventing quantization staircasing while sharpening short-pitch gradient response. Exposing $\sigma$ as an adjustable parameter (10.0m–50.0m) empowers the athlete to tune the filter to their terrain preference. System invariants, zero-allocation inner loops, and continuous grade evaluation are 100% preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an elevation stream with discrete vertical quantization (0.2m–0.4m steps),<br>• *When* `ElevationProfile` renders with default settings ($\sigma = 21.0\,\text{m}$),<br>• *Then* the elevation curve SHALL be smooth and continuous, sharpening short-pitch gradient response compared to $\sigma = 35.0\,\text{m}$ without staircasing.<br>• *Given* the athlete in `AdvancedTuningDialog` under Aftermath & Analysis,<br>• *When* adjusting the elevation smoothing slider,<br>• *Then* `elevationSmoothingSigmaMeters` SHALL update in preferences within $[10.0\text{m}, 50.0\text{m}]$, and `ElevationProfile` SHALL dynamically re-render using the updated $\sigma$.<br>• *Given* points at track boundaries ($d=0$ and $d=D_{total}$),<br>• *When* smoothing is applied,<br>• *Then* boundary altitudes SHALL renormalize cleanly without sagging or peaking.<br>• *Given* all 9 supported application locales,<br>• *When* running localization parity tests,<br>• *Then* all new tuning string resources SHALL exist and be non-empty.<br><br>**Invariants**: SQLite schemas, raw stream data, total ascent metrics, and 100% unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Distance-weighted Gaussian kernel elevation smoothing with default sigma 21m, dynamic cutoff, and configurable expert setting. | `ElevationSmoothingMath.kt`, `ElevationProfile.kt`, `TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `AftermathAnalysisSection.kt` | `TST-UI-257` | Verified |

`RouteSegmentsBreakdownSection`.<br>• If neither are present: `analyticsContent` SHALL cleanly evaluate to `null` without rendering empty cards or layout gaps.<br>4. *Map & Elevation Profile | **REQ-UI-317** | **Geodesic Polyline Orthogonal Projection & Interval Matching for Route-Segment Correlation.** | The system SHALL evaluate candidate route-segment spatial associations in `RouteSegmentMatcher.kt` using geodesic orthogonal projection onto polyline line segments and interval-based forward traversal tracking (ATT-2862, amending `REQ-UI-302` and `REQ-UI-305`):<br>1. *Orthogonal Polyline Segment Projection*:<br>• Rather than testing geodesic distance strictly against isolated route vertices, the system SHALL calculate the orthogonal projection of segment start, end, and sampled midpoint coordinates onto each line segment $(P_i, P_{i+1})$ of the candidate route polyline.<br>• For each projection, the system SHALL determine the projected coordinate $Q \in (P_i, P_{i+1})$, the orthogonal cross-track distance $d_{\text{cross-track}}$, and the exact interpolated cumulative route distance $D_{\text{along}} = D_i + t \cdot (D_{i+1} - D_i)$ where $t \in [0.0, 1.0]$.<br>2. *Corridor Distance Tolerance & Real-World GPS Adaptability*:<br>• A segment terminal point (start/end) SHALL be considered within corridor proximity if its cross-track distance to the route polyline is $\le 35.0\text{ m}$ (`CORRIDOR_TOLERANCE_METERS = 35.0`).<br>• For multi-point segments ($\ge 3$ points), the midpoint cross-track distance to the route polyline between start and finish projections SHALL be $\le 60.0\text{ m}$ (`MIDPOINT_TOLERANCE_METERS = 60.0`).<br>3. *Interval-Based Forward Traversal on Circuit, Loop & Out-and-Back Routes*:<br>• To prevent false rejections caused by independent global minimum selection on out-and-back tracks or figure-8 routes, the system SHALL evaluate localized forward candidate intervals $(proj_{\text{start}}, proj_{\text{end}})$ satisfying:<br>  a. $proj_{\text{end}}.distanceAlongRoute > proj_{\text{start}}.distanceAlongRoute$.<br>  b. Both start and end cross-track distances $\le 35.0\text{ m}$.<br>  c. Span distance consistency: $|(D_{\text{end}} - D_{\text{start}}) - \text{intrinsicDistance}| \le \max(100.0, \text{intrinsicDistance} \times 0.25)$.<br>4. *Directional Bearing Alignment on Projected Line Segments*:<br>• Forward bearing alignment SHALL be calculated using the travel bearing along the route's nearest polyline segment $(P_i, P_{i+1})$ containing the projection point, compared to the initial segment traversal bearing.<br>• The angular difference SHALL satisfy $\Delta \theta \le 45.0^\circ$ (`MAX_BEARING_DELTA_DEGREES = 45.0`) with positive vector dot product ($\cos(\Delta \theta) > 0$).<br>5. *Preservation of System Invariants & Zero Regression*:<br>• Genuine reverse traversals ($\Delta \theta > 90^\circ$), perpendicular crossing corridors, conflicting sport types, diverging finishes, and horseshoe midpoints MUST remain strictly rejected.<br>• Zero Android UI dependencies in `RouteSegmentMatcher.kt` (pure functional evaluation).<br>• 100% clean-room unit test pass rate across `RouteSegmentMatcherTest.kt` and the full test suite.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines and amends `REQ-UI-302` (*Route Starred Segments Spatial Overlap Matching, Chronological Route Breakdown & Map Synergy*, Clause 1) and `REQ-UI-305` (*Inverted Route-Segment Spatial Association*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-2583` (Sprint `2026-41.3`) and Ticket `ATT-2585` (Sprint `2026-41.4`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `RouteSegmentMatcher` was originally implemented with a simple discrete vertex search loop, validated against synthetic colinear test points with 0 m offset. ALERT_WINDOW_MAX_METERS`)..<br>3. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Spatial separation thresholds (`DIVERGENCE_INITIATION_THRESHOLD_METERS = 15.0m`, `DIVERGENCE_SEPARATION_THRESHOLD_METERS = 40.0m`, `LOOKAHEAD_METERS = 600.0m`), angular relative classification ranges (`[-20, 20]` for `STRAIGHT`), active route candidate matching restriction (`REQ-MAP-041` / `ATT-2942`), and 100% clean-room advertising objects via `org.bluez.LEAdvertisingManager1.RegisterAdvertisement` with standard 16-bit UUIDs (`['1818']` for `ATT-Pwr` and `['180d']` for `ATT-HRM`).<br>• The tool SHALL run the GLib Injection*:<br>• The tool SHALL inject simulated GPS fixes via ADB strictly adhering to Android 14+ `LocationShellCommand` syntax: `cmd location providers set-test-provider-location <p> --location be omitted from `cmd location` calls.<br>• Clean lifecycle guard: The tool SHALL remove test providers upon exit (`remove-test-provider`) via `atexit` and `signal` handlers.<br>• The tool SHALL provide a `--no-gps` flag to bypass ADB location injection when no device is attached.<br>5. *Rule 30 Host Pre-Flight Self-Diagnostics*:<br>• The tool SHALL execute pre-flight self-diagnostics at actionable diagnostics in both CLI terminal and GUI status indicators.<br>6. *Dual User Interface (PyQt6 Desktop GUI & Headless CLI)*:<br>• The tool SHALL offer a modern dark/obsidian PyQt6 desktop GUI dashboard with transport controls, interactive timeline slider, digital telemetry cards (Power, Cadence, HR, Speed, Distance, Altitude), status indicators, and file picker dialog.<br>• The tool SHALL offer a headless CLI mode (`--headless` / `--cli`) for CI environments with non-blocking keybindings.<br>7. *Desktop Process Lifecycle & Thread Isolation Architecture*:<br>• The tool SHALL | **REQ-MAP-046** | **Unified Viewport Anchor Authority for Follow-Me Map Tracking & Analytical Forward Lookahead Calculation.** | The system SHALL unify camera positioning, forward lookahead offset `followMeController`, forward lookahead SHALL be computed analytically by projecting the camera focal target coordinate ahead of the athlete along `filteredBearing` based on `tuningConfig.mapFollowMeLookaheadPaddingPercent`, viewport height, and map zoom level.<br>• Target projection math: $\text{offsetFraction} = (\text{lookaheadPaddingPercent} / 100\text{f}) \times 0.5\text{f}$, $\text{metersPerDp} = (156543.03392 \times \cos(\text{latRad})) / 2^{\text{targetZoom}}$, $\text{offsetMeters} = \text{viewportHeightDp} \times \text{offsetFraction} \times \text{metersPerDp}$, $\mathbf{x}_{\text{target}} = \text{SphericalUtil.computeOffset}(\text{currentLocation}, \text{offsetMeters}, \text{filteredBearing})$.<br>2. *Decoupling of GoogleMap Content Padding (`ATrainingTrackerMap.kt`)*:<br>• In `ATrainingTrackerMap.kt`, during `MapZoomFocus.FOLLOW_ME` mode, `GoogleMap` SHALL receive `contentPadding = PaddingValues(0.dp)`, completely eliminating competing layout recentering loops between Google Maps native padding and `cameraPositionState.animate(...)`.<br>• `BoxWithConstraints` SHALL pass `maxHeight.value` as `viewportHeightDp` and `tuningConfig.mapFollowMeLookaheadPaddingPercent` as `lookaheadPaddingPercent` to `followMeController`.<br>3. *Smooth Camera Animation & Zero-Jitter Invariant*:<br>• When a new GPS coordinate arrives, `followMeController` SHALL animate the camera to `CameraPosition.builder().target(target).bearing(filteredBearing).zoom(targetZoom).tilt(effectiveTilt).build()`.<br>• The camera SHALL stably anchor the athlete marker at the lower third (~35% from bottom / ~65% from top) without oscillating or jumping to the physical screen center (50% Y).<br>4. *Preservation of Non-Follow-Me Modes & System Invariants*:<br>• In non-Follow-Me modes (`EXPLICIT_BOUNDS`, `TRACK_AND_MARKERS`, `LOCAL_SEGMENTS`, `FIT_PRIMARY`), `followMeController` SHALL remain inactive and `contentPadding` SHALL remain `0.dp`.<br>• Speed zoom calibration ($0\text{ km/h} \to 20.0$, $20\text{ km/h} \to 18.0$), bearing smoothing ($\alpha = 0.15$), pitch angle ($0^\circ - 70^\circ$), DataStore preference persistence, and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate MUST be strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-MAP-044` (*Forward Lookahead Camera Top Content Padding Inversion*, Sprint 2026-41.7, ATT-3054) and `REQ-MAP-042` (*Calibratable Speed-Dependent Map Zoom Curve, Follow-Me Forward Lookahead Camera Padding & Pitch Tuning*, Sprint 2026-41.6, ATT-2946).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced in Sprint 2026-41.6 (`ATT-2946`, commit `d8177e06`) and modified in Sprint 2026-41.7 (`ATT-3054`, commit `8cdc39f0`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: ATT-3054 inverted bottom padding to top padding on `GoogleMap` to shift the camera center downward. However, `CameraPosition.builder().target(currentLocation)` in `followMeController` always centers the camera target at the unpadded physical screen center (50% Y), while Google Maps native padding shifts it downward (65% Y). This caused a continuous 1 Hz oscillation between center and lower third on every GPS update.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Stable rider positioning in lower third, speed-dependent zoom curve, tilt pitch, DataStore tuning preferences, and 100% test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active workout tracking session in `FOLLOW_ME` mode,<br>• *When* GPS telemetry updates are received at 1 Hz,<br>• *Then* `followMeController` animates the camera target to $\mathbf{x}_{\text{target}}$ ahead of the athlete along `filteredBearing`,<br>• *And* the athlete marker remains stably positioned at the lower third without oscillating to the viewport center.<br>• *Given* `GoogleMap` in `FOLLOW_ME` mode in `ATrainingTrackerMap.kt`,<br>• *When* inspecting `contentPadding`,<br>• *Then* `contentPadding` evaluates to `PaddingValues(0.dp)`.<br>• *Given* `tuningConfig.mapFollowMeLookaheadPaddingPercent` configured in Settings,<br>• *When* the athlete adjusts the slider,<br>• *Then* `followMeController` dynamically scales the forward lookahead ground offset accordingly.<br>• *Given* non-Follow-Me modes (`EXPLICIT_BOUNDS`, `TRACK_AND_MARKERS`),<br>• *When* rendered,<br>• *Then* `contentPadding` remains `0.dp` and `MapBoundsController` governs camera framing.<br><br>**Invariants**: Single spatial authority (Rule 33), speed zoom curve, bearing smoothing, pitch angle, DataStore settings, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Unified viewport anchor authority and analytical lookahead camera targeting in followMeController, eliminating GoogleMap content padding conflicts and camera oscillation jitter. | `MapBehaviors.kt`, `ATrainingTrackerMap.kt` | `TST-MAP-048` | Verified |

`0.5f`), preserving crisp visual separation without adding grey container backgrounds.<br>• Outer container border (`BorderStroke(1.dp, MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outlineVariant.copy(alpha = 0.8f))`) and inner group border (`BorderStroke(1.dp, MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outlineVariant.copy(alpha = 0.6f))`) SHALL be preserved.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Directional grouping (`decisionState.branches.groupBy { it.direction }`), route selection callback (`onRouteSelected`), dismiss callback (`onDismiss`), countdown distance, and 100% 9-language localization parity MUST be strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-UI-330` (*In-Ride Fork Route Decision Card HUD Layout & Selection Interactions*, Sprint 2026-41.6, ATT-2962) and complements `REQ-MAP-031` (*TurnPromptBanner Turn-by-Turn Navigation Prompts & Direction HUD*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.6 (`ATT-2962`, commit `0f24b2c0`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: During ATT-2962 construction, `tonalElevation = 1.dp` was assigned to `ForkDirectionGroup`, and `CardDefaults.cardElevation(defaultElevation = 6.dp)` was retained on the outer card. first().distance`).<br>• Latitude, longitude, altitude, and any associated telemetry or speed values SHALL remain strictly unmodified.<br>• If `pathPoints` is empty or already starts at `0.0`, the system SHALL return the points safely without mutation.<br>2. *Full-Width Elevation Profile Rendering (`ClimbOnMapScreen.kt`)*:<br>• `ClimbOnMapScreen` SHALL supply `climb.normalizedPathPoints` as the `activeScrubPath` to `MapDetailLayout`.<br>• The embedded `ElevationProfile` chart X-axis SHALL span exactly from base ($0.0\text{ m}$) to summit ($d_{\text{summit}}$), utilizing 100% of the horizontal chart width.<br>• The profile SHALL NOT be compressed into a sliver at the far right edge of the chart when the climb originated from a later section of a parent route.<br>3. *Interactive Scrubbing & Map Pin Synchronization*:<br>• When scrubbing the normalized elevation profile, `selectedDistance` ($0.0 \le s \le d_{\text{summit}}$) SHALL resolve to the corresponding geographical `PathPoint` via `TelemetryMetricUtils.findNearestPoint`.<br>• The active scrubbing pin on the map view SHALL accurately indicate the athlete's scrubbed location along the physical climb polyline.<br>4. *Preservation of Global Route Context in Header*:<br>• `ClimbHeader` SHALL continue to display the global route offset (e.g. "Start at 27.4 km") via `climb.pathPoints.firstOrNull()?.distance`, preserving the parent route orientation.<br>• Global route profiles rendered in `RouteOnMapScreen` SHALL remain unaffected.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Complements `REQ-UI-300` (*Climb Detail Sheet Visual Contract*), `REQ-UI-315` (*Harmonized Route & Climb Detail HUD*), and `REQ-UI-333` (*EntityDetailSheetScaffold Architecture*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.6 (`ATT-3053`). In ATT-3053, `ClimbOnMapScreen` and `ClimbDetailSheet` migrated to `MapDetailLayout` to harmonize with `SegmentOnMapScreen`. However, unlike segments (which are standalone tracks starting at 0m), climbs detected from routes carry route cumulative distances (e.g. 27.38 km to 28.10 km). `MapDetailLayout` assumes `activeScrubPath` starts at 0, resulting in the elevation profile being squished into the final 3% of the chart width.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Historical standalone canvas (`ClimbDetailElevationProfile`) explicitly normalized distances via `(p.distance - startDist) / totalDist`. standard top padding, allowing the map to retain primary flexible weight (`weight(1f)`).<br>• When `state.pathPoints.size < 2`, the elevation profile SHALL NOT be rendered, preventing empty stretched canvas artifacts.<br>3. *Decoupled Canvas Height Expansion (`ElevationProfile.kt`)*:<br>• `ElevationProfile` SHALL accept an explicit parameter `fillParentHeight: Boolean = false`.<br>• When ($\ge 120\text{dp}$).<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Ambient `NavigationHintsOverlay` positioning at `Alignment.TopCenter` when `showMap == false` (REQ-UI-335 / ATT-3100), map Target*: Complements `REQ-UI-197` (*Non-Overlapping Elevation Profile Vertical Layout*), `REQ-UI-225` (*Decoupled Telemetry Badge & Canvas Layout*), and `REQ-UI-326` (*TrackingMapContainer Recomposition Barrier*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.6 (`ATT-2944`). `TrackingMapContainer` was isolated with `weight(1f)`, but when `showMap == false`, no weight was was always visible when tracking. `liveSegment.liveData.segmentStatus` is `LiveSegmentStatus.APPROACHING` or `LiveSegmentStatus.FAR_FAR_AWAY`, it SHALL evaluate to `null`.<br>2. *Contract & Layout Integrity (`LiveSegmentSheetContractTest.kt`, `LiveSegmentSheetLayoutTest.kt`)*:<br>• Contract tests SHALL enforce `distance_raw` evaluation on `LiveSegmentStatus.FINISHED`.<br>• Unit tests SHALL verify that `externalScrubDistance` to `distance_raw`.<br>3. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Bottom sheet wrap-content height (`REQ-UI-270`), suppressed map and zoom controls (`REQ-UI-197`), unified Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends and supersedes the completion evaluation formula of `REQ-UI-331` (*Live Segment Elevation Profile Dynamic Position Marker & Scrub Distance Synchronization*, Sprint 2026-40.16, ATT-2967).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced in Sprint 2026-40.16 (`ATT-2967`, commit `54fb2b23`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In ATT-2967, `externalScrubDistance` was mapped to `summary.distance.toDouble()` under the mistaken assumption that `summary.distance` was numeric. Killed/Suppressed red).<br>5. *Headless CLI & Scripting Support*:<br>• The headless CLI runner (`run_headless_cli`) SHALL provide non-blocking hotkeys: `'h'` (HR toggle), `'p'` (Power toggle), `'g'` <sec>`, `--kill-power-at <sec>`, `--revive-power-at <sec>`, `--kill-gps-at <sec>`, `--revive-gps-at <sec>`.<br>6. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Production application code isolation: Zero mock or test code in `app/src/main`.<br>• Clean fallback: Seamless mock execution when BlueZ or PyQt6 is unavailable.<br>• 100% unit test pass rate across `tools/test_replay_workout.py` and `./gradlew Follows Sprint 2026-40.16 retro (`ATT-2389`), where testing sensor reconnection recovery and GPS tunnel behavior required physical sensor manipulation or manual script restarts.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Prior tool iterations focused on initial streaming synchronization; runtime dropout simulation was deferred.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Production code isolation, thread safety via isolated `GLib.MainContext`, and clean ADB test provider cleanup strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* `tools/replay_workout.py` running with BLE and GPS active,<br>• *When* `kill_hr()` is triggered in GUI or CLI,<br>• *Then* HR advertising ceases, HR GATT notifications are silenced, and connected clients receive disconnect notifications.<br>• *When* `revive_hr()` is triggered in GUI or CLI,<br>• *Then* HR advertising resumes, live HR GATT notifications resume matching the current TCX timestamp, and the client reconnects automatically.<br>• *Given* replay running with GPS active,<br>• *When* `kill()` is triggered on `AdbGpsInjector`,<br>• *Then* coordinate injection stops while test providers remain active.<br>• *When* `revive()` is triggered on `AdbGpsInjector`,<br>• *Then* coordinate injection resumes at the current TCX coordinates.<br>• *Given* automated CLI flags `--kill-hr-at 10 --revive-hr-at 20`,<br>• *When* playback reaches 10s and 20s,<br>• *Then* HR is automatically killed at 10s and revived at 20s.<br><br>**Invariants**: Production code isolation, thread safety via isolated GLib main context, and 100% unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | TCX replay per-device kill, disconnection, and reconnection simulation across BLE HRM, Power, and mock GPS. | `tools/replay_workout.py`, `tools/test_replay_workout.py` | `TST-TOOL-004` | Verified |
| **REQ-MAP-047** | **Continuous Linear Polyline Projection & Progress Metric Interpolation for Live Climbs.** | The system SHALL project the athlete's real-time GPS position orthogonally onto polyline segments of the active climb path and continuously interpolate distance, altitude, progress fraction, and instantaneous gradient to prevent UI stutter and eliminate false off-route cancellations between sparse trackpoints (ATT-3174, amending `REQ-MAP-027` and aligning with Design Guidelines §2.4):<br>1. *Continuous Orthogonal Segment Projection (`LiveClimbsRepository.kt`)*:<br>• For each consecutive polyline segment $[P_i, P_{i+1}]$ in `path` ($i = 0 \dots \text{path.size} - 2$):<br>  - Compute the segment vector $\vec{v} = (\Delta \text{lat}, \Delta \text{lng}) = (P_{i+1}.\text{lat} - P_i.\text{lat}, P_{i+1}.\text{lng} - P_i.\text{lng})$.<br>  - Compute segment squared Euclidean length $L^2 = \Delta \text{lat}^2 + \Delta \text{lng}^2$.<br>  - If $L^2 > 0.0$, compute the scalar projection parameter $t = \frac{(\text{location.lat} - P_i.\text{lat})\Delta \text{lat} + (\text{location.lng} - P_i.\text{lng})\Delta \text{lng}}{L^2}$ clamped to $[0.0, 1.0]$; otherwise $t = 0.0$.<br>  - Derive projected coordinate $P_{\text{proj}} = (\text{projLat}, \text{projLng}) = (P_i.\text{lat} + t \times \Delta \text{lat}, P_i.\text{lng} + t \times \Delta \text{lng})$.<br>  - Measure geodesic cross-track distance between athlete $(\text{location.lat}, \text{location.lng})$ and $P_{\text{proj}}$ using `Location.distanceBetween`.<br>  - Identify the optimal segment index $i$ and scalar $t$ that minimize cross-track distance across all segments.<br>2. *Cross-Track Off-Route Protection*:<br>• The off-route check SHALL evaluate the minimum cross-track distance to the projected polyline point against `CLIMB_OFF_ROUTE_THRESHOLD_METERS` (100.0m).<br>• If $\min(\text{crossTrackDist}) > \text{CLIMB\_OFF\_ROUTE\_THRESHOLD\_METERS}$, `processLocation()` SHALL return `null` (off climb).<br>• When riding along a straight road with sparse vertices (e.g. 180m apart), an athlete traveling on-segment SHALL NOT be falsely marked off-route.<br>3. *Continuous Telemetry & Progress Interpolation*:<br>• Using the optimal segment $[P_i, P_{i+1}]$ and scalar $t$, the system SHALL compute:<br>  - $\text{completedDist} = ((P_i.\text{distance} - \text{path.first().distance}) + t \times (P_{i+1}.\text{distance} - P_i.\text{distance})).\text{coerceAtLeast}(0.0)$<br>  - $\text{remainingDist} = (\text{climb.distanceMeters} - \text{completedDist}).\text{coerceAtLeast}(0.0)$<br>  - $\text{currentAlt} = P_i.\text{altitude} + t \times (P_{i+1}.\text{altitude} - P_i.\text{altitude})$<br>  - $\text{remainingGain} = (\text{summitAlt} - \text{currentAlt}).\text{coerceAtLeast}(0.0)$<br>  - $\text{progressFraction} = (\text{completedDist} / \text{climb.distanceMeters}).\text{coerceIn}(0.0, 1.0).\text{toFloat}()$<br>  - $\text{currentGradePercent} = \text{if } (P_{i+1}.\text{distance} - P_i.\text{distance} > 0.0) \frac{P_{i+1}.\text{altitude} - P_i.\text{altitude}}{P_{i+1}.\text{distance} - P_i.\text{distance}} \times 100.0 \text{ else } \text{climb.avgGradePercent}$<br>4. *Single-Point Geometry Fallback*:<br>• If `path.size < 2`, the system SHALL fall back to discrete vertex evaluation at $P_0$, using geodesic distance to $P_0$ for off-route check, $P_0.\text{altitude}$, and $\text{completedDist} = 0.0$.<br>5. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Summit gate detection (`CLIMB_SUMMIT_GATE_THRESHOLD_METERS = 35.0m`), start gate detection (`CLIMB_START_GATE_THRESHOLD_METERS = 30.0m`), approach detection (`CLIMB_APPROACH_THRESHOLD_METERS = 250.0m`), approach bearing tolerance ($\le 60^\circ$), and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate MUST be strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-MAP-027` (*ClimbPro Real-Time Live Climb Cockpit Sheet with Dynamically Colored Gradient Profile & Elevation Pacing*, Sprint 2026-40.14, ATT-1281) and aligns with `docs/design_guidelines.md` §2.4.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.14 (`ATT-1281`). The initial engine implementation adopted nearest-neighbor discrete vertex lookup for simplicity and minimum CPU overhead. Refined in Sprint 2026-41.7 (`ATT-2947`, `REQ-UI-328`) and Sprint 2026-41.8 (`ATT-3103`, `REQ-UI-341`), focusing on UI layout, typography, and `@Preview` tooling.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Nearest-neighbor discrete vertex snapping was implemented as a minimum viable progress tracking solution. Field testing on high-resolution displays (Google Pixel 10) demonstrated that on sparse tracks (50m–200m trackpoint spacing), telemetry metrics (remaining distance, elevation gain, current gradient) and the elevation profile rider indicator pin freeze and jump discontinuously, giving the impression of GPS lag or frozen UI. Furthermore, computing distance against discrete vertices rather than polyline segments left riders vulnerable to false 100m off-route cancellations between distant vertices.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Summit gate threshold (35m), start gate threshold (30m), approach bearing tolerance ($\le 60^\circ$), off-route threshold (100m cross-track), and full clean-room unit test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active live climb with sparse trackpoints 500m apart (vertex 0 at 0m, vertex 1 at 500m),<br>• *When* the athlete is located at the 250m midpoint (50% progress),<br>• *Then* `completedDist` evaluates to 250.0m (not 0.0m or 500.0m), `progressFraction` evaluates to 0.5f, and `currentAlt` is interpolated smoothly between base and summit.<br>• *Given* an athlete traveling along a road segment between two vertices spaced 180m apart,<br>• *When* the athlete is at the 90m midpoint 10m perpendicular to the segment (cross-track distance 10m, vertex distance 90.5m),<br>• *Then* `processLocation()` evaluates cross-track distance as 10m and retains the climb as active (does not trigger false off-route cancellation).<br>• *Given* an athlete who deviates > 100m perpendicular to all polyline segments of the climb,<br>• *When* `processLocation()` is called,<br>• *Then* `processLocation()` returns `null`, cleanly dismissing the off-route climb.<br>• *Given* a single-point climb path (`path.size == 1`),<br>• *When* `processLocation()` is evaluated,<br>• *Then* the engine falls back safely to $P_0$ without throwing an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.<br><br>**Invariants**: Gate thresholds, approach bearing checks, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Project athlete position orthogonally onto polyline segments of active climb and continuously interpolate telemetry metrics and rider pin position. | `LiveClimbsRepository.kt`, `LiveClimbsRepositoryTest.kt` | `TST-MAP-049` | Verified |

StartOrResumeInterface)?.showStartOrResumeDialog()` or instantiate `StartOrResumeDialog().show(...)` if not already visible.<br>3. *Database Query & Finalization Predicate Robustness (`WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.java` & `TrackerService.java`)*:<br>• In `WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.hasUnfinishedWorkout()`, the SQLite query SHALL filter rows matching `(finished IS NULL OR finished = 0)` and return `true` if any unfinalized workout exists.<br>• In `WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.discardOrFinishUnfinishedWorkout()`, the update SHALL match rows with `(finished IS NULL OR finished = 0)`.<br>• In `TrackerService.createNewWorkout()`, `ContentValues` SHALL explicitly insert `values.put(WorkoutSummaries.FINISHED, 0)`.<br>4. *Sticky Service Tracking State UI Synchronization (`TrainingApplication.java` & `BANALServiceRepository.kt`)*:<br>• In `TrainingApplication.setTracking()`, the method SHALL invoke `notifyTrackingStateChanged()`, dispatching the `TRACKING_STATE_CHANGED` broadcast intent and updating notification summary.<br>• In `BANALServiceRepository.init`, `_trackingMode` LiveData SHALL be initialized with `TrainingApplication.getTrackingMode()` rather than hardcoded `TrackingMode.READY`.<br>• When `TrackerService` resumes via `RESUME_SERVICE_RECREATION`, `ControlTrackingScreen` SHALL display the active tracking controls (e.g. Pause button) and `StartOrResumeDialog` SHALL NOT be shown.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-UI-329` (*Material 3 Jetpack Compose Workout Recovery Dialog Architecture*), `REQ-STB-003` (*Interrupted Workout Resumption & Unfinished Workout Recovery*), and `REQ-STB-012` (*Forensic Process Kill Diagnosis*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.9 (`ATT-3165`). Follows migration in `ATT-2948` (commit `fe4e24f1`), where `ComposeView` was hosted in floating `DialogFragment` without explicit window layout dimensions in `onStart()`, resulting in invisible dialog bounds on certain devices.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Historical `StartOrResumeDialog` relied on Android `AlertDialog.Builder`. | **REQ-MAP-048** | **Follow-Me Camera Target Forward Lookahead Projection Scaling, Tilt Foreshortening Compensation & Settings Scale Direction Transparency.** | The system SHALL scale and project the forward lookahead camera target coordinate in `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget` (`MapBehaviors.kt`) such that adjusting the "Vorausschau-Kameraabstand" (*Forward Lookahead Padding*) slider produces a proportional, visually distinct shift of the athlete marker between screen center and lower viewport across all camera tilt angles, compensating for 3D perspective tilt foreshortening and providing explanatory scale direction in user settings (ATT-3171, amending `REQ-MAP-046` and aligning with Design Guidelines §3.1 & §6.1):<br>1. *Analytical Forward Lookahead Projection Calibration (`MapBehaviors.kt`)*:<br>• `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget` SHALL accept `tiltAngle: Float = 0f`.<br>• The offset fraction calculation SHALL scale as: $\text{offsetFraction} = (\text{lookaheadPaddingPercent} / 100\text{f}) \times 0.6\text{f}$, mapping slider values from $10\% \dots 50\%$ to $6\% \dots 30\%$ of viewport height (anchoring the marker from $56\%$ Y just below center to $80\%$ Y in the lower cockpit, with the $30\%$ default anchoring at $68\%$ Y in the canonical lower third).<br>2. *Perspective Tilt Foreshortening Compensation (`MapBehaviors.kt`)*:<br>• The ground offset projection SHALL compensate for 3D perspective pitch tilt foreshortening: $\text{tiltFactor} = \cos(\text{Math.toRadians(tiltAngle.toDouble().coerceIn(0.0, 70.0))).toFloat().coerceAtLeast(0.34f)}$, $\text{offsetMeters} = (\text{viewportHeightDp} \times \text{offsetFraction} \times \text{metersPerDp}) / \text{tiltFactor}$.<br>• At $\text{tiltAngle} = 70^\circ$, $\text{tiltFactor} \approx 0.342$, scaling ground offset by $\approx 2.92\times$ so that when Google Maps renders the 3D perspective camera, the on-screen displacement matches the intended fraction of viewport height.<br>3. *Follow-Me Controller Delegation (`MapBehaviors.kt`)*:<br>• `followMeController` SHALL pass `tiltAngle = effectiveTilt` into `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget`.<br>4. *Settings Scale Direction Transparency (Design Guidelines §3.1)*:<br>• In accordance with Design Guidelines §3.1, `tuning_map_lookahead_padding_desc` SHALL explicitly state physical scale direction across all 9 supported locales ("higher value = rider further down / more road ahead" / "höherer Wert = Fahrer weiter unten / mehr Vorausschau").<br>5. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Single spatial authority (Rule 33 / Design Guidelines §6.1) without competing Google Maps content padding MUST be strictly preserved.<br>• Bearing low-pass filter smoothing ($\alpha = 0.15$), speed-dependent zoom curve, DataStore preference schema and defaults ($30\%$), and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate MUST be strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-MAP-046` (*Unified Viewport Anchor Authority for Follow-Me Map Tracking*, Sprint 2026-41.8, ATT-3102).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced in Sprint 2026-41.8 (`ATT-3102`, commit `611d3781`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In ATT-3102, forward lookahead was decoupled from Google Maps content padding to eliminate 1 Hz camera jitter. To approximate the old 15% midpoint shift, the developer used `* 0.5f`. However, `tiltAngle` was omitted from `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget`, and under default 70° tilt (`DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_TILT_ANGLE = 70.0f`), perspective foreshortening ($\cos(70^\circ) \approx 0.342$) squashed the displacement to ~6.8% of the screen across the entire 10%–50% slider range, making adjustments imperceptible.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Single spatial authority, smooth bearing filtering, speed-dependent zoom, and 100% clean-room test pass rate remain preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active workout tracking session in `FOLLOW_ME` mode with a 600dp viewport at zoom 18f,<br>• *When* `lookaheadPaddingPercent` is increased from 10% to 30% and to 50%,<br>• *Then* the calculated ground offset distance in meters SHALL scale strictly proportionally (5x from 10% to 50%, and 3x from 10% to 30%).<br>• *Given* a fixed `lookaheadPaddingPercent = 30f` and viewport height of 600dp,<br>• *When* `tiltAngle` is 70°,<br>• *Then* the calculated ground offset distance in meters SHALL be scaled up by approximately $2.92\times$ relative to `tiltAngle = 0°`, compensating for 3D perspective foreshortening.<br>• *Given* `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget` invoked with extreme tilt angles (e.g. 90° or negative angles),<br>• *When* evaluating the tilt compensation factor,<br>• *Then* `tiltAngle` SHALL be safely coerced to $[0^\circ, 70^\circ]$ and `tiltFactor` SHALL be clamped to $\ge 0.34\text{f}$.<br>• *Given* `followMeController` executing during workout tracking,<br>• *When* invoking `calculateFollowMeCameraTarget`,<br>• *Then* `followMeController` SHALL pass `tiltAngle = effectiveTilt`.<br>• *Given* all 9 supported application locales,<br>• *When* inspecting `tuning_map_lookahead_padding_desc`,<br>• *Then* each locale SHALL include the explicit scale direction indicator with zero missing entries.<br><br>**Invariants**: Single spatial authority, speed zoom curve, bearing smoothing, pitch angle, DataStore settings, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Follow-Me camera target forward lookahead projection scaling, tilt foreshortening compensation and settings scale direction transparency. | `MapBehaviors.kt`, `strings.xml` (all 9 locales) | `TST-MAP-050` | Verified |

| **REQ-GEO-001** | **Unified Polyline Progress Tracking Engine with Directional Virtual Gates and Orthogonal Segment Projection.** | The system SHALL extract and maintain a unified, reusable `PolylineProgressTracker` engine in `com.atrainingtracker.trainingtracker.geo` and delegate polyline tracking from both `LiveSegmentsRepository` and `LiveClimbsRepository` (ATT-3266, amending `REQ-LIV-001`, `REQ-LIV-002`, `REQ-LIV-004`, `REQ-MAP-027`, and `REQ-MAP-047`):<br>1. *Unified PolylineProgressTracker Engine Architecture*:<br>• The system SHALL define `PolylineProgressTracker` in package `com.atrainingtracker.trainingtracker.geo` as a pure-Kotlin utility decoupled from Android framework dependencies and database persistence.<br>• Core domain models SHALL include: `PolylineGate` (directional perpendicular virtual gate with endpoints $A, B$, reference forward point $N$, reference cross-product, and configurable gate distance threshold); `PolylineProjection` (projected point, optimal segment index, segment parameter $t \in [0, 1]$, along-track completed distance, cross-track error in meters, progress fraction $\in [0f, 1f]$, interpolated altitude, and instantaneous grade percentage); `PolylineTrackingState` (`FAR_FAR_AWAY`, `APPROACHING`, `ON_TRACK`, `FINISHED`).<br>2. *Directional Virtual Gate Crossing via 2D Vector Cross-Products*:<br>• For any polyline entry or exit, `PolylineProgressTracker` SHALL construct virtual gates perpendicular to the track entry vector ($[P_0, P_{\text{sample}}]$) and exit vector ($[P_{\text{last}-\text{sample}}, P_{\text{last}}]$).<br>• Gate crossing SHALL be evaluated via 2D vector cross-product: $\text{cross}(A, B, C) = (B_{\text{lat}} - A_{\text{lat}})(C_{\text{lng}} - A_{\text{lng}}) - (B_{\text{lng}} - A_{\text{lng}})(C_{\text{lat}} - A_{\text{lat}})$.<br>• A gate crossing event SHALL trigger if and only if: (a) Current location is within gate distance threshold ($D \le D_{\text{gate}}$); (b) Cross-product sign has flipped relative to the previous fix: $\text{sign}(\text{currCross}) \ne \text{sign}(\text{prevCross})$; (c) Cross-product sign matches the forward trajectory reference: $\text{sign}(\text{currCross}) == \text{sign}(\text{refCross})$ (for start gate) or $\text{sign}(\text{currCross}) \ne \text{sign}(\text{refCross})$ (for finish gate).<br>• Radial entry without cross-product sign flip (e.g. parallel pass or hairpin approach) SHALL NOT trigger gate crossing.<br>3. *Continuous Orthogonal Segment Projection & 3D Telemetry*:<br>• For an athlete at coordinate $L$, the engine SHALL project $L$ orthogonally onto each consecutive polyline segment $[P_i, P_{i+1}]$ using scalar parameter: $u = \frac{(L_{\text{lat}} - P_{i.\text{lat}})\Delta\text{lat} + (L_{\text{lng}} - P_{i.\text{lng}})\Delta\text{lng}}{\Delta\text{lat}^2 + \Delta\text{lng}^2}, \quad t = \text{coerceIn}(u, 0.0, 1.0)$.<br>• The engine SHALL select the segment index $i$ and scalar $t$ that minimize geodesic cross-track distance $D_{\text{cross}}$.<br>• Along-track completed distance SHALL evaluate to: $D_{\text{completed}} = (P_i.\text{distance} - P_{\text{first}}.\text{distance}) + t \times (P_{i+1}.\text{distance} - P_i.\text{distance})$.<br>• Altitude and grade SHALL interpolate continuously along the optimal segment: $\text{alt} = P_i.\text{altitude} + t \times (P_{i+1}.\text{altitude} - P_i.\text{altitude}), \quad \text{grade} = \frac{\Delta\text{altitude}}{\Delta\text{distance}} \times 100\%$.<br>4. *Smooth Finish Remaining Distance Blending*:<br>• When within finish proximity threshold ($D_{\text{end}} \le D_{\text{finishThreshold}}$), the engine SHALL blend along-track remaining distance with direct geodesic line distance to the finish gate using linear $\lambda$-interpolation: $\lambda = \min\left(1.0, \frac{D_{\text{end}}}{D_{\text{finishThreshold}}}\right), \quad D_{\text{rem}} = (D_{\text{total}} - D_{\text{completed}}) \times \lambda + (1.0 - \lambda) \times D_{\text{end}}$.<br>• This guarantees remaining distance continuously and monotonically reaches exactly $0.0\text{m}$ at the finish line without discrete sampling jumps.<br>5. *Approach Filtering, Heading Alignment & Off-Track Detection*:<br>• Approaching state SHALL activate when athlete distance to start gate $D_{\text{start}} \le D_{\text{approach}}$ (default $250\text{m}$) AND bearing difference $|\Delta\theta| \le \theta_{\text{tol}}$ (default $45^\circ$).<br>• Off-track deviation SHALL trigger when minimum cross-track error $D_{\text{cross}} > D_{\text{offTrack}}$ (default $50\text{m}$ for segments, $100\text{m}$ for climbs), resetting state to `FAR_FAR_AWAY`.<br>6. *Repository Delegation & Migration*:<br>• `LiveSegmentsRepository.kt` SHALL delegate gate creation, gate crossing, and polyline projection to `PolylineProgressTracker`, replacing raw odometer subtraction ($D_{\text{current}} - D_{\text{start}}$) with orthogonal along-track distance.<br>• `LiveClimbsRepository.kt` SHALL delegate start/summit gate detection and orthogonal projection to `PolylineProgressTracker`, replacing radial circles with directional virtual gates.<br>7. *Preservation of Domain Models & Invariants*:<br>• Segment-specific telemetry (PR comparison, time delta, elapsed time) and Climb-specific telemetry (remaining ascent, climb category, route sequencing) MUST remain intact.<br>• Multi-track candidate concurrency in `LiveSegmentsRepository` and active route vs free-riding climb detection in `LiveClimbsRepository` MUST NOT be altered.<br>• 100% clean-room unit regression test suite pass rate.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-LIV-001` (*Detect segments using "Gates" and cross-products*), `REQ-LIV-002` (*Real-time progress on starred Strava segments*), `REQ-LIV-004` (*Filter segments by bearing alignment*), `REQ-MAP-027` (*ClimbPro Real-Time Live Climb Cockpit Sheet*), and `REQ-MAP-047` (*Continuous Linear Polyline Projection for Live Climbs*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.14 (`ATT-1281`), Sprint 2026-41.9 (`ATT-3174`), Sprint 2026-41.10 (`ATT-3266`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Climbs and Segments were delivered under separate feature epics with divergent math (odometer subtraction vs orthogonal projection, radial circles vs virtual gates).<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Starred segment PR pacing, ClimbPro elevation profile, rider marker progress fraction, and 100% clean-room test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete approaching a virtual start or finish gate,<br>• *When* crossing the gate line in the correct track heading direction,<br>• *Then* `PolylineProgressTracker` detects the crossing via cross-product sign flip and transitions state cleanly.<br>• *Given* an athlete riding on a parallel switchback near the gate,<br>• *When* location updates are evaluated,<br>• *Then* the gate is NOT triggered unless the perpendicular line is physically crossed in the designated direction.<br>• *Given* an athlete traveling along a live segment or climb,<br>• *When* GPS fixes arrive,<br>• *Then* progress is projected orthogonally onto the polyline, providing accurate along-track distance and cross-track error independent of odometer drift.<br>• *Given* an athlete approaching the finish or summit gate within finish threshold,<br>• *When* remaining distance is computed,<br>• *Then* $\lambda$-blending produces a smooth, continuous decrease reaching exactly $0.0\text{m}$ at the finish line.<br>• *Given* an athlete on a segment or climb who turns away onto another road ($D_{\text{cross}} > D_{\text{offTrack}}$),<br>• *When* tracking updates,<br>• *Then* the tracker immediately disengages and reverts state to `FAR_FAR_AWAY`.<br>• *Given* the automated test suite,<br>• *When* `LiveClimbsRepositoryTest`, `LiveSegmentsRepositoryTest`, `PolylineProgressTrackerTest`, and full application regression tests execute,<br>• *Then* 100% of tests pass with 0 failures.<br><br>**Invariants**: Starred segment PR comparison, ClimbPro live profile, rider pin tracking, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be | **REQ-UI-358** | **Dynamic Cockpit Viewport Allocation, Asymmetric Map Weight Expansion & Bounded Sensor Grid Containment.** | The system SHALL ensure that when a tracking tab displays both a sensor grid and an embedded map view (`showMap == true`), the map expands flexibly to consume 100% of all vertical space remaining between the sensor grid and the elevation profile (or bottom cockpit boundary), eliminating dead white space, while bounding multi-row sensor grids to at most 50% of available viewport height with internal vertical scrolling (ATT-3343, amending `REQ-UI-346` and `REQ-UI-339`, complementing `REQ-UI-355`):<br>1. *Available Viewport Measurement (`SensorGridScreen.kt`)*:<br>• The main tracking cockpit container in `SensorGridScreen.kt` SHALL be hosted within `BoxWithConstraints(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(top = paddingValues.calculateTopPadding()))`.<br>• The available height `val availableHeight = maxHeight` SHALL constrain child elements proportionally.<br>2. *Asymmetric Weight Allocation for Sensor Grid & Map*:<br>• When `state.mapState.showMap == true`:<br>  - The sensor grid `Column` SHALL NOT declare `Modifier.weight(...)`.<br>  - The sensor grid `Column` SHALL declare `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(max = availableHeight * 0.5f).verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())`.<br>  - For 1–2 rows, the sensor grid measures at its exact intrinsic content height; for 4–6 rows, it is capped at 50% of `availableHeight` and scrolls internally.<br>  - The map `Box` SHALL declare `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().weight(1f, fill = true)`.<br>  - Because the map is the sole weighted child in the Column, it expands flexibly to occupy 100% of all vertical space remaining after measuring the sensor grid and elevation profile.<br>• When `state.mapState.showMap == false`:<br>  - The sensor grid `Column` SHALL declare `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()).weight(1f, fill = false)`, preserving the exact canonical behavior of `REQ-UI-346`.<br>3. *Elevation Profile Anchoring & Adaptive Height Preservation*:<br>• The elevation profile `Surface` SHALL remain non-weighted with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(top = 8.dp)`.<br>• The elevation profile SHALL continue to calculate its height adaptively between $70\text{dp}$ and $200\text{dp}$ via `calculateElevationProfileHeight(range)` per `REQ-UI-346`.<br>• When the elevation profile is toggled off or contains fewer than 2 points, the map expands seamlessly down to the bottom screen boundary.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Zero regression to `TrackingMapContainer` recomposition barrier isolation (`REQ-UI-326`).<br>• Ambient navigation overlays, live climb sheets, and configuration mode controls remain fully functional.<br>• 100% clean-room unit test pass rate across the full test suite.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-UI-346` (*Canonical Adaptive Height & Weight Decoupling for Sole Elevation Profile on Tracking Screen*, Sprint 2026-41.9, ATT-3173) and `REQ-UI-339` (*Dynamic Cockpit Weight Allocation & Flexible Vertical Expansion for Elevation Profile when Map is Disabled*, Sprint 2026-41.8, ATT-3107), and complements `REQ-UI-355` (*Active Route Full Elevation Profile with Map-Matched Position Marker, Categorized Climbs & Per-Tab Rolling Window Scoping During Tracking*, Sprint 2026-41.10 / Sprint 2026-42.1, ATT-3199 & ATT-3317). Targets `SensorGridScreen.kt` and `SensorGridScreenLayoutTest.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.8 (`ATT-3107`, commit `8d6ef4e1`) introduced `Modifier.weight(1f, fill = false)` on the sensor grid. Sprint 2026-41.9 (`ATT-3173`, commit `ad0c2020`) removed weight from the elevation profile.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In `ATT-3107`, `weight(1f, fill = false)` was placed on the sensor grid so it wraps 1–2 rows and scrolls for many rows. However, when `showMap == true`, the map was also given `weight(1f)`. In Compose Column, weighted children divide available space proportionally. With `fill = false`, the sensor grid only consumes intrinsic height, but Compose does not donate unused quota to the other weighted child (the map). The map remains capped at 50%, leaving the remaining space blank as dead white space.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Sensor grid scrolling, canonical adaptive height ($70\text{dp} \dots 200\text{dp}$), non-weighted wrapping elevation profile Surface, map recomposition barrier isolation, ambient overlays, and 100% full-suite test pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a tracking view configured with 1 row of sensor fields, a map, and an elevation profile,<br>• *When* viewing the tracking screen,<br>• *Then* the map expands to fill all remaining vertical space between the sensor row and the elevation profile, with zero dead white space below the elevation profile.<br>• *Given* a tracking view configured with 5 rows of sensor fields and a map,<br>• *When* viewing the screen,<br>• *Then* the sensor grid is capped at 50% of the available height and scrolls smoothly without pushing the map or elevation profile off screen.<br>• *Given* a tracking view with the map toggled off (`showMap == false`) and elevation profile enabled,<br>• *When* viewing the tracking screen,<br>• *Then* the sensor grid wraps content without stretching and the elevation profile renders at its canonical adaptive height directly below it.<br>• *Given* an active tracking view with map and elevation profile,<br>• *When* the athlete toggles the elevation profile off in configuration mode,<br>• *Then* the map dynamically expands to fill the entire vertical space below the sensor grid down to the screen edge.<br><br>**Invariants**: Sensor grid scrollability, canonical adaptive height, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Dynamic cockpit viewport allocation, asymmetric map weight expansion, and bounded sensor grid containment. | `SensorGridScreen.kt` | `TST-UI-319` | Verified |
