| **REQ-UI-373** | **Automatic Training Zone Boundary Calculation from FTP and Heart Rate Baselines.** | The system SHALL provide automated, deterministic training zone boundary calculation directly within the zones settings workflow (`ZonesSettingsActivity.kt`) from physiological benchmarks (Functional Threshold Power for cycling power, and Maximum Heart Rate / Resting Heart Rate for heart rate), while strictly preserving manual customization, guaranteeing single-transaction ACID atomicity in DataStore, enforcing two-layer boundary inversion protection with strict integer increments ($Z_n \ge Z_{n-1} + 1$), guaranteeing historical analytics immutability, and maintaining full 9-language localization parity (ATT-3188, amending `REQ-UI-370` and complementing `REQ-PRO-022`):<br>1. *Cycling Power Coggan 7-Zone Calculation & Zone 7 Ceiling (`REQ-UI-373.1`)*:<br>• The system SHALL compute cycling power zone upper boundaries from Functional Threshold Power (FTP, in Watts) using the canonical Coggan percentages: Z1 (55%), Z2 (75%), Z3 (90%), Z4 (105%), Z5 (120%), Z6 (150%).<br>• The system SHALL apply deterministic half-up rounding (`Math.round(percent * ftp).toInt()`) with boundary rationalization guaranteeing strictly monotonic ascending boundaries ($Z_{n\text{max}} \ge Z_{n-1\text{max}} + 1$).<br>• Zone 7 upper bound SHALL be capped at physical maximum $2500\text{ Watts}$ (finite storage invariant; zero `Infinity` values stored in DataStore). Zone 7 lower bound is $Z_{6\text{max}} + 1\text{ W}$.<br>• Allowed FTP input range SHALL be constrained to $[50, 600]\text{ Watts}$. For maximum FTP = $600\text{ W}$, Zone 6 cutoff evaluates to $900\text{ W}$, leaving a valid Zone 7 interval $[901\text{ W}, 2500\text{ W}]$. If any input sets $Z_{6\text{max}} \ge 2500\text{ W}$, `ZoneCalculationMath` and `ZoneValidator` MUST throw `IllegalArgumentException`.<br>2. *Heart Rate Zone Calculation (% of HRmax and Karvonen HRR) & Explicit Error Messages (`REQ-UI-373.2`)*:<br>• Model A (% of HRmax): Z1 (59%), Z2 (69%), Z3 (79%), Z4 (89%), Z5 ($HR_{\max}$).<br>• Model B (Karvonen HRR): Target HR = $\text{round}(HR_{\text{rest}} + (HR_{\max} - HR_{\text{rest}}) \times \text{intensity}\%)$. Z1 (59% HRR), Z2 (69% HRR), Z3 (79% HRR), Z4 (89% HRR), Z5 ($HR_{\max}$).<br>• Allowed baseline ranges: $HR_{\text{rest}} \in [30, 120]\text{ bpm}$, $HR_{\max} \in [80, 240]\text{ bpm}$.<br>• Primary Karvonen Invariant Check: Enforces $HR_{\max} > HR_{\text{rest}}$ and $HR_{\max} - HR_{\text{rest}} \ge 20\text{ bpm}$. If $HR_{\max} \le HR_{\text{rest}}$, the UI displays `zone_calc_error_hr_max_greater_rest` (*"HFmax muss größer als HFruhe sein"*) and disables calculation. If $HR_{\max} - HR_{\text{rest}} < 20\text{ bpm}$, the UI displays `zone_calc_error_karvonen_delta` (*"HFmax muss mindestens 20 bpm über HFruhe liegen"*) and disables calculation. `ZoneCalculationMath` throws `IllegalArgumentException` on violation.<br>3. *Two-Layer Monotonicity Validation & Strict Step Increment (`REQ-UI-373.3` & `REQ-UI-373.4`)*:<br>• Layer 1 (UI Reactive Barrier): Evaluated synchronously on every keystroke (`onValueChange`). Verifies $Z_{n\text{max}} \ge Z_{n-1\text{max}} + 1$ and $Z_{n\text{max}} \le Z_{n+1\text{max}} - 1$. Minimum integer delta $\Delta = 1$ is mandatory (adjacent zones cannot share identical cutoffs). If violated, sets `isError = true`, displays error message (\"Wert muss zwischen %d und %d liegen\"), and disables Save/Apply buttons.<br>• Layer 2 (Domain Blocking Guard): `ZoneValidator.validatePowerZoneStack()` and `validateHeartRateZoneStack()` throw `IllegalArgumentException` on any inversion ($Z_i \ge Z_{i+1}$) or out-of-bounds cutoff.<br>4. *Single-Transaction ACID Atomicity & UI Mutation Lock (`REQ-UI-373.5`, `REQ-UI-373.6` & `REQ-UI-373.10`)*:<br>• Baseline mutation, customization flag (`pwr_bike_zones_customized`, `hr_zones_customized`), and all cutoffs persist atomically in a single `dataStore.edit { }` block via file-level atomic swap.<br>• UI maintains `isSaving: Boolean` state; while writing to DataStore, action buttons are disabled with loading indicators, preventing concurrent or re-entrant mutations.<br>• UI observes state via UDF `collectAsState()` directly from DataStore, eliminating disconnected local state.<br>5. *Formal Data Integrity Policy & Historical Analytics Immutability (`REQ-UI-373.7`)*:<br>• Prospective-Only Baseline Mutation: Past completed workouts in SQLite (`WorkoutSummaries.db`, `Extrema.db`) are immutable and NEVER retroactively recalculated.<br>• Intra-Session Historical Fidelity: Mid-workout baseline changes apply strictly to subsequent telemetry ticks ($t \ge t_{\text{change}}$).<br>6. *Customization Lifecycle & Destructive Overwrite Warning (`REQ-UI-373.8`)*:<br>• Profiles transition to `CUSTOMIZED` upon any manual edit of an individual cutoff field.<br>• Recalculating over customized zones triggers a modal confirmation dialog warning that manual zones will be overwritten. Cancel preserves custom zones with 0 changes.<br>7. *Locale-Aware Number Parsing & 9-Language Localization Token Parity (`REQ-UI-373.9`)*:<br>• `ZoneNumberParser.parseIntOrNull()` handles `,` vs `.` and non-breaking space grouping.<br>• All UI strings maintain 100% translation parity and format specifier token parity (exact count, order, and argument types of `%d`, `%s`, `%1$d`) across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-UI-373`. Amends `REQ-UI-370` (*Decoupled Training Zone Architecture & 7-Zone Coggan Cycling Power Model*, Sprint 2026-42.4, ATT-3184) and complements `REQ-PRO-022`. Targets `ZoneCalculationMath.kt`, `ZoneValidator.kt`, `ZoneNumberParser.kt`, `ZoneCalculatorDialog.kt`, `ZonesSettingsActivity.kt`, `SettingsDataStore.kt`, `SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper.kt`, and `strings.xml`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.5 (`ATT-1390`, commit `e3966ebf`) introduced manual zone configuration; Sprint 2026-42.4 (`ATT-3184`, commit `0da639ba`) expanded power to 7 zones. Active ticket `ATT-3188`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Zones were previously entered manually because athlete baselines (FTP, HRmax) were not stored in DataStore, treating cutoffs as raw arbitrary thresholds.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Manual cutoff customization preserved, proportional migration fallback preserved, SQLite historical workout immutability preserved, and 100% clean-room test pass rate strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete entering FTP = 250W in the calculator dialog,<br>• *When* tapping "Berechnen",<br>• *Then* calculated preview displays: Z1 <= 138W, Z2 <= 188W, Z3 <= 225W, Z4 <= 263W, Z5 <= 300W, Z6 <= 375W, Z7 is [376W, 2500W] capped at 2500W.<br>• *Given* HRmax = 190 and HRrest = 50,<br>• *When* calculating Karvonen zones,<br>• *Then* cutoffs resolve to: Z1 <= 133, Z2 <= 147, Z3 <= 161, Z4 <= 175, Z5 <= 190 bpm.<br>• *Given* HRmax - HRrest < 20 bpm,<br>• *When* inputting in the dialog,<br>• *Then* calculation is disabled and the explicit localized error message `zone_calc_error_karvonen_delta` is displayed.<br>• *Given* HRmax <= HRrest,<br>• *When* inputting in the dialog,<br>• *Then* calculation is disabled and the explicit localized error message `zone_calc_error_hr_max_greater_rest` is displayed.<br>• *Given* manual editing of adjacent zone cutoffs with zero delta ($Z_3 = 200, Z_4 = 200$),<br>• *When* validated,<br>• *Then* validation fails because $Z_4$ must be >= $Z_3 + 1$.<br>• *Given* calculated zones applied from the dialog,<br>• *When* persisted to DataStore,<br>• *Then* baseline, timestamp, customization flag, and all cutoffs save atomically in a single transaction while disabling action buttons with a loading state.<br>• *Given* customized zones and user tapping recalculate,<br>• *When* modal confirmation appears and user taps cancel,<br>• *Then* existing custom zones remain completely untouched.<br><br>**Invariants**: Historical workout immutability in SQLite, finite Zone 7 bound (2500W ceiling), strict integer monotonicity ($Z_n \ge Z_{n-1} + 1$), canonical SI storage, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Automatic training zone boundary calculation from FTP and Heart Rate baselines with single-transaction ACID atomicity, two-layer monotonicity, and historical immutability. | `ZoneCalculationMath.kt`, `ZoneValidator.kt`, `ZoneNumberParser.kt`, `ZoneCalculatorDialog.kt`, `ZonesSettingsActivity.kt`, `SettingsDataStore.kt` | `TST-UI-336` | Verified |

| **REQ-TRK-018** | **Sport-Specific Auto-Pause Engine with Anti-Chatter Hysteresis, Mutex Precedence, Sensor Dropout Guard, Synchronous Ingestion Gating, and Sport-Decoupled Thresholds.** | The system SHALL provide an automated, sport-specific Auto-Pause Engine (`AutoPauseManager.kt`) that suspends active recording when an athlete becomes stationary and seamlessly resumes recording upon departure, maintaining strict metric integrity, crash resilience, and manual user sovereignty (ATT-45, ATT-3677, extending `REQ-TRK-001` and `REQ-TRK-002`, complementing `REQ-FIL-012`, `REQ-FIL-013`, and `REQ-UI-262`):<br>1. *Sport-Specific Default Activation*:<br>• The system SHALL enable Auto-Pause by default for Cycling (`BSportType.BIKE`).<br>• The system SHALL disable Auto-Pause by default for Running (`BSportType.RUN`) and Other sports (`BSportType.UNKNOWN`), ensuring interval workouts and track drills are never inadvertently paused.<br>• Sports-specific activation SHALL be independently configurable via `TuningPreferencesDataStore`.<br>2. *Sport-Decoupled Thresholds, Integer Configuration, Anti-Chatter Hysteresis Deadband & Hard Ceilings (`ATT-3677`)*:<br>• The system SHALL provide independent Speed Thresholds and Debounce Windows per sport (`Bike`, `Run`, `Other`), configured strictly as integer (`Int`) values in `TuningPreferencesDataStore`:<br>  - **Cycling (`BSportType.BIKE`)**: Speed threshold $1 \dots 5$ in user speed unit ($1 \dots 5\text{ km/h}$ Metric, $1 \dots 5\text{ mph}$ Imperial), step $1$, default $3\text{ km/h}$ / $2\text{ mph}$; Debounce window $1 \dots 10\text{ s}$, step $1\text{ s}$, default $2\text{ s}$.<br>  - **Running (`BSportType.RUN`)**: Speed threshold $1 \dots 5$ in user speed unit ($1 \dots 5\text{ km/h}$ Metric, $1 \dots 5\text{ mph}$ Imperial), step $1$, default $2\text{ km/h}$ / $1\text{ mph}$; Debounce window $1 \dots 20\text{ s}$, step $1\text{ s}$, default $5\text{ s}$.<br>  - **Other (`BSportType.UNKNOWN`)**: Speed threshold $1 \dots 5$ in user speed unit ($1 \dots 5\text{ km/h}$ Metric, $1 \dots 5\text{ mph}$ Imperial), step $1$, default $1\text{ km/h}$ / $1\text{ mph}$; Debounce window $1 \dots 60\text{ s}$, step $1\text{ s}$, default $10\text{ s}$.<br>• Sliders in `SensorsGpsFilterSection.kt` SHALL be rendered conditionally directly below each sport's auto-pause toggle (collapsible when enabled) and formatted using dynamic speed units ($v\text{ km/h}$ or $v\text{ mph}$) via `R.string.units_speed` / `MyHelper.getUnitsId(SensorType.SPEED_mps)`.<br>• **Hysteresis Deadband & Ceiling**: Resumption strictly requires $v_{\text{resume}} \ge \min(v_{\text{pause}} + 0.5\text{ [user unit]}, v_{\text{ceiling}})$ sustained for a confirmation tick ($1\text{ second}$). The upper ceiling is clamped to $6.0\text{ km/h}$ in Metric ($1.667\text{ m/s}$) or $4.0\text{ mph}$ in Imperial, ensuring a deterministic and reachable threshold even at maximum threshold, while suppressing chattering near the pause threshold.<br>• **Numerical Sanitization**: Any non-finite speed values (`Double.NaN`, `Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY`, `Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY`) SHALL be sanitized and rejected prior to evaluation.<br>3. *Speed Hierarchy, 5-Second Stale Packet TTL, SENSOR_LOST State & Audit Trail*:<br>• Speed Hierarchy: The engine consumes `BANALService.getBestSensorData(SensorType.SPEED_mps)`. High-precision hardware wheel sensors (ANT+/BLE) take primary precedence. If no hardware sensor is connected, the engine seamlessly falls back to GPS speed (`GPS_SPEED` / Location provider).<br>• Stale Packet Rejection: The engine rejects sensor packets where `System.currentTimeMillis() - packet.timestamp > 5000ms`. If the newest speed packet is older than 5 seconds, the engine treats the feed as stale/disconnected and transitions to `SENSOR_LOST` rather than falsely assuming stationary 0 km/h.<br>• Stationary vs Signal Loss: Periodic location/sensor updates arriving with low speed ($v < v_{\text{pause}}$) and valid accuracy ($\le 30\text{ m}$) evaluate as stationary and trigger auto-pause. Total signal outage ($> 5\text{ s}$) transitions to `SENSOR_LOST`, suspends auto-pause, and maintains recording state.<br>• State Change Audit Logging: When transitioning between `TRACKING`, `AUTO_PAUSED`, and `SENSOR_LOST`, the system SHALL persist a state-transition event record in SQLite session metadata for full auditability, while keeping the continuous `WorkoutSamples` trackpoint stream free of synthetic coordinate/speed spikes to preserve clean FIT/GPX exports.<br>• Recovery Contract: When valid speed readings resume and remain stable for $\ge 2$ consecutive seconds, `AutoPauseManager` transitions from `SENSOR_LOST` back to `TRACKING` and re-engages regular stationary speed evaluation.<br>4. *Synchronous Hierarchical Gating & Elevation Drift Protection*:<br>• In `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice`, `MyAccumulatorSensor<Double>` (for `SensorType.DISTANCE`), and `LocationManager` callbacks, gating executes sequentially in the sensor ingestion thread: first `if (TrainingApplication.isPaused()) return;` (enforcing manual pause priority), then `if (AutoPauseManager.isAutoPaused()) return;` (enforcing auto-pause gating).<br>• Gating is 100% synchronous in memory, preventing any elevation drift or ghost trackpoints before the database persistence completes.<br>• Horizontal distance accumulation and vertical elevation gain/loss (`mAscentSensor`, `mDescentSensor`) immediately halt. `ElevationProfile` path-point logging and `WorkoutSamples` database writes are suspended during `AUTO_PAUSED`.<br>• Authoritative average speed in `WorkoutSummaries` strictly evaluates $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{TimeActive}}$ (moving time), completely uncorrupted by stationary pause duration.<br>5. *Strict Mutex Enforcement (TrackingLock), Persistence & Race-Free Reset*:<br>• An explicit manual pause sets `mManualPauseLock = true` in `TrainingApplication`. While `mManualPauseLock` is active, `AutoPauseManager` is strictly blocked from issuing auto-resume events.<br>• Lock Persistence: `mManualPauseLock` is immediately persisted to `DataStore`, surviving process death or background OS killing.<br>• Centralized Lock Reset: `mManualPauseLock` is cleared (`mManualPauseLock = false`) and persisted whenever ANY explicit user resume action is dispatched (in-app Cockpit button, "Resume Now" badge button, or background notification action). All actions funnel through `TrainingApplication.resumeFromPaused()`.<br>6. *Strictly Ordered FIFO Asynchronous Flush & Crash Invariants*:<br>• Single-Threaded FIFO Queue: `mDbExecutor` in `TrackerService` enqueues the final stationary `WorkoutSample` and accumulator snapshots immediately followed by the summary paused-state update, guaranteeing strict in-order persistence.<br>• Crash Recovery during Debounce: The `debounceCounter` is transient in-memory. If process death occurs while in `PAUSE_DEBOUNCE_PENDING`, the counter is reset to 0 and the restored session strictly defaults to `TRACKING` (active recording).<br>7. *Deterministic Startup State-Recovery Hierarchy*:<br>• Upon application restart or crash recovery in `TrackerService`:<br>  - Tier 1 (User Sovereignty): If `mManualPauseLock == true` in DataStore, the session MUST restore in `MANUAL_PAUSED` state regardless of the last `WorkoutSample` velocity. The user's explicit manual intent strictly overrides telemetry samples.<br>  - Tier 2 (Auto-Paused): If `mManualPauseLock == false` and `isAutoPaused == true`, the session restores in `AUTO_PAUSED`. Sensor evaluation is re-engaged. If immediate fresh speed readings arrive exceeding $v_{\text{resume}}$, the engine smoothly transitions to `TRACKING`.<br>  - Tier 3 (Active Tracking): If both flags are false, the session restores to `TRACKING`.<br>• In-memory sensor accumulators are re-initialized with the last persisted totals from `WorkoutSummaries` to avoid value jumping/spikes upon resume.<br>8. *Cockpit UI & Audio/Haptic Feedback*:<br>• When in `AUTO_PAUSED` state, `SensorGridScreen.kt` renders an amber pill badge displaying "Auto-Pause" along with an immediate "Resume Now" button.<br>• When in `SENSOR_LOST` state, `SensorGridScreen.kt` renders an amber pill badge displaying "Speed Sensor Lost".<br>• Tapping "Resume Now" clears `mManualPauseLock`, sets `isAutoPaused = false`, and immediately forces the session back to `TRACKING`. Audio tones are emitted on pause/resume.<br>9. *Localization (9 Languages)*:<br>• Full copy parity across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT for all settings sliders, toggles, badge text, and manual override controls.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Extends and refines `REQ-TRK-001` (*Support Start, Stop, Pause with Service persistence*) and `REQ-TRK-002` (*Workout Lap Recording Lifecycle, Manual Splitting & Pause/Resume Neutrality*). Targets `AutoPauseManager.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java`, `TrackerService.java`, `TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `SensorsGpsFilterSection.kt`, and `SensorGridScreen.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `3c09e3e7` (Initial baseline import, 2011), `ATT-166` Epic (*Filtering to improve sensor values*), `ATT-45` (Sprint 2026-42.4, commit `53c20db4`), and `ATT-3677` (Sprint 2026-42.5). `TrainingApplication.pauseTracking()` and `resumeFromPaused()` historically supported manual user pause only; ATT-45 added auto-pause with global thresholds; ATT-3677 decouples thresholds and debounces per sport with integer-only sliders.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Manual pause was designed as an absolute binary state to suspend recording active time, trackpoints, and lap splitting per `REQ-TRK-002` when an athlete took a break. When introducing automated speed-drop pausing, naive auto-resume would violate user intent if an athlete deliberately paused at a cafe and walked with their bike. Furthermore, different sports (cycling vs running vs other) operate at vastly different low-speed dynamics, necessitating independent thresholds and debounce windows per sport without fractional float jitter. Therefore, Chesterton's Fence mandates that manual pause semantics must remain sovereign via `mManualPauseLock`, and per-sport thresholds must maintain integer cleanliness while preserving lap neutrality and continuous `TIME_TOTAL_s` accumulation.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Manual user pause sovereignty via persisted `mManualPauseLock`, zero lap increments or split disruptions on auto-pause/resume (`REQ-TRK-002`), continuous `TIME_TOTAL_s` elapsed tracking during pause (`REQ-TRK-009`), strict moving-time average speed calculation ($v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{TimeActive}}$), backward compatibility bridges for legacy global properties, and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* active cycling tracking with default settings (threshold 3 km/h, debounce 2s),<br>• *When* speed drops below 3 km/h for 2 seconds,<br>• *Then* `AutoPauseManager` transitions to `AUTO_PAUSED`, halts distance and elevation accumulation, flushes final sample asynchronously, and renders amber badge in Cockpit.<br>• *Given* active running tracking with default settings (threshold 2 km/h, debounce 5s),<br>• *When* speed drops below 2 km/h for 4 seconds,<br>• *Then* engine remains in `PAUSE_DEBOUNCE_PENDING`; when 5th second elapses at $\le 2\text{ km/h}$, transitions to `AUTO_PAUSED`.<br>• *Given* a session in `AUTO_PAUSED`,<br>• *When* speed fluctuates below $v_{\text{pause}} + 0.5$,<br>• *Then* session remains paused due to 0.5 hysteresis deadband.<br>• *Given* a session in `AUTO_PAUSED`,<br>• *When* speed exceeds $v_{\text{resume}}$ for 1s,<br>• *Then* recording resumes automatically.<br>• *Given* Imperial units active,<br>• *When* configuring auto-pause sliders,<br>• *Then* speed thresholds step in whole mph integers (1..5 mph) with defaults Bike=2, Run=1, Other=1.<br>• *Given* a user manual pause,<br>• *When* athlete speeds up,<br>• *Then* auto-resume is strictly blocked by `mManualPauseLock`.<br>• *Given* an athlete in `AUTO_PAUSED` tapping "Resume Now",<br>• *Then* `mManualPauseLock` clears and session immediately resumes active tracking.<br>• *Given* total speed signal dropout exceeding 5 seconds,<br>• *Then* engine enters `SENSOR_LOST`, logs transition in session metadata, suspends auto-pause, and trackpoint logging remains clean.<br><br>**Invariants**: Moving average speed calculation, manual pause precedence, zero elevation drift during pause, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Sport-specific auto-pause engine with sport-decoupled integer thresholds and debounce windows, anti-chatter hysteresis, mutex precedence, and synchronous ingestion gating. | `AutoPauseManager.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java`, `TrackerService.java`, `TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `SensorsGpsFilterSection.kt`, `SensorGridScreen.kt` | `TST-TRK-010` | Verified |

| **REQ-TRK-020** | **Live Normalized Power (NP) and Intensity Factor (IF) Calculations & Cockpit Integration.** | The system SHALL calculate Dr. Andrew Coggan's Normalized Power (NP) and Intensity Factor (IF) in real time during cycling workouts, integrating these metrics into the telemetry engine, filter presets, and tracking cockpit (ATT-1290, complementing `REQ-TRK-019`, `REQ-UI-370`, `REQ-UI-373`, and `REQ-UI-374`):<br>1. *First-Class Sensor & Metric Definitions*:<br>• `SensorType.NORMALIZED_POWER`: fullNameId `R.string.normalized_power`, shortNameId `R.string.normalized_power_short` ("NP"), unitId `R.string.units_power` ("W"), `SensorValueType.DOUBLE`, `IntegerFormatter`.<br>• `SensorType.INTENSITY_FACTOR`: fullNameId `R.string.intensity_factor`, shortNameId `R.string.intensity_factor_short` ("IF"), unitId `R.string.units_intensity_factor` (""), `SensorValueType.DOUBLE`, `IntensityFactorFormatter` (2 decimal places `#0.00`).<br>• Icon mapping: `case POWER, POWER_TO_WEIGHT, NORMALIZED_POWER, INTENSITY_FACTOR -> R.drawable.ic_power;`.<br>2. *Decoupled 1Hz Computed Engine Architecture (`CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL maintain a 30-sample rolling FIFO window of 1-second power samples (t) \ge 0.0\text{ W}$.<br>• Active Pause Gating: Calculation and window updates SHALL be strictly gated by `TrainingApplication.isRecordingSuspended()`. When paused or auto-paused, the state of the 30-sample queue and cumulative sums MUST NOT advance.<br>• Coasting Policy: 0 W power samples are genuine physiological recovery points and MUST be ingested into the 30-sample rolling window.<br>• Warm-Up Window ( < 30\text{ s}$): While the queue contains fewer than 30 samples, Normalized Power and Intensity Factor are undefined; `newValue(null)` SHALL be published and formatted as `"--"`.<br>• Calculation ( \ge 30\text{ s}$):<br>  a. Compute rolling 30s average power: {30s} = \frac{1}{30}\sum_{i=0}^{29} P(t-i)$.<br>  b. Raise to 4th power: (t) = (P_{30s})^4$.<br>  c. Accumulate cumulative 4th power sum  = \sum y(t)$ and valid tick counter $.<br>  d. Take 4th root of cumulative 4th power average: $\text{NP} = \sqrt[4]{\frac{S_4}{N}}$.<br>  e. Publish $\text{NP}$ via `mNormalizedPowerSensor.newValue(np)`.<br>• Intensity Factor:<br>  a. Retrieve athlete FTP via `mFtpProvider.getFtp(context)`.<br>  b. If $\text{FTP} > 0$ and $\text{NP} \ge 0$, compute $\text{IF} = \frac{\text{NP}}{\text{FTP}}$ and publish via `mIntensityFactorSensor.newValue(ifVal)`.<br>  c. If FTP is unconfigured ($\le 0$ or null), publish `null` to `mIntensityFactorSensor.newValue(null)`.<br>3. *Thread Safety & Lifecycle Invariants*:<br>• All calculation, queue mutation, and sensor emission logic SHALL be synchronized within `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` monitors.<br>• Scheduled executor service SHALL be explicitly terminated via `shutdownNow()` during service destruction.<br>4. *Sensor Filter Defaults*:<br>• `NORMALIZED_POWER` and `INTENSITY_FACTOR` SHALL default to `FilterType.INSTANTANEOUS` (1.0s direct).<br>5. *Activity Types*:<br>• `SensorType.NORMALIZED_POWER` and `SensorType.INTENSITY_FACTOR` SHALL be registered in `ActivityType.BIKE_POWER`.<br>6. *Cockpit Grid & Guidance UI*:<br>• Cockpit tiles for NP and IF SHALL render `"--"` when undefined or unconfigured.<br>• In `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt`, selecting `INTENSITY_FACTOR` when FTP is unconfigured SHALL display a guidance prompt with direct access to Zone Settings.<br>7. *9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• All string resources SHALL be defined across all 9 application locales: EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TRK-020`. Complements `REQ-TRK-019` (*Power-to-weight ratio*), `REQ-UI-370` (*7-Zone Coggan Cycling Power Model*), `REQ-UI-373` (*Automated Training Zone Calculation*), and `REQ-UI-374` (*Contextual Zone Settings Navigation*). Targets `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SensorType.java`, `IntensityFactorFormatter.java`, `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt`, and `strings.xml`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Cycling power support introduced originally in `BANALService`. Modernized to Compose 7-zone Coggan model in Sprint `2026-42.4` (`ATT-3184`, commit `6ae4625b`), automatic zone calculation from FTP (`ATT-3188`), contextual pairing navigation (`ATT-3189`), and real-time power-to-weight ratio (`ATT-1289`, commit `5eee662f`). Active ticket `ATT-1290`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Previous power telemetry handled raw and smoothed instantaneous metrics. NP requires cumulative session state across 30s rolling buffers and 4th power summation.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Pause gating invariant strictly preserved, FTP preference integrity preserved, SQLite schema integrity preserved, and 100% test pass rate preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active cycling workout with power data,<br>• *When* fewer than 30 seconds have elapsed,<br>• *Then* NP and IF emit null, displaying "-- W" and "--".<br>• *Given* constant 200 Watts for 60 seconds,<br>• *When* 30 seconds elapse,<br>• *Then* NP displays exactly 200 W.<br>• *Given* alternating intervals of 100 W and 300 W (mean 200 W),<br>• *When* evaluated,<br>• *Then* NP strictly exceeds 200 W.<br>• *Given* FTP of 300 W and NP of 240 W,<br>• *When* observing IF,<br>• *Then* it displays "0.80".<br>• *Given* unconfigured FTP,<br>• *When* observing IF,<br>• *Then* it displays "--", and selecting the tile in edit mode prompts the user to configure FTP.<br><br>**Invariants**: Pause gating, FTP DataStore integrity, SQLite column schema, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Real-time Normalized Power (NP) and Intensity Factor (IF) calculations, 30s rolling buffer, 4th power weighting, pause gating, and cockpit integration. | `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SensorType.java`, `IntensityFactorFormatter.java`, `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt` | `TST-TRK-012` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-021** | **Real-Time Mechanical Work (kJ) and Training Stress Score (TSS) Telemetry.** | The system SHALL integrate Mechanical Work (kJ) and Dr. Andrew Coggan's Training Stress Score (TSS) in real time during cycling workouts, integrating these cumulative load metrics into the telemetry engine, filter presets, and tracking cockpit (ATT-1291, complementing `REQ-TRK-019`, `REQ-TRK-020`, `REQ-UI-370`, `REQ-UI-373`, and `REQ-UI-374`):<br>1. *First-Class Sensor & Metric Definitions*:<br>• `SensorType.WORK_KJ`: fullNameId `R.string.work_kj`, shortNameId `R.string.work_kj_short` ("kJ"), unitId `R.string.units_work_kj` ("kJ"), `SensorValueType.DOUBLE`, `IntegerFormatter`, `isInstantaneous = false`.<br>• `SensorType.TSS`: fullNameId `R.string.tss`, shortNameId `R.string.tss_short` ("TSS"), unitId `R.string.units_none`, `SensorValueType.DOUBLE`, `IntegerFormatter`, `isInstantaneous = false`.<br>• Icon mapping: `case POWER, POWER_TO_WEIGHT, NORMALIZED_POWER, INTENSITY_FACTOR, WORK_KJ, TSS -> R.drawable.ic_power;`.<br>2. *Decoupled 1Hz Computed Engine Architecture (`CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`)*:<br>• Mechanical Work Integration: For every active 1-second tick when recording is not suspended and power $P(t) \ge 0.0\text{ W}$, the system SHALL integrate mechanical energy: $W_{\text{joules}} \leftarrow W_{\text{joules}} + (P(t) \times 1.0\text{ s})$, and publish $\text{Work (kJ)} = \frac{W_{\text{joules}}}{1000.0}$ via `mWorkKjSensor.newValue(workKj)`. Coasting ($0\text{ W}$) adds $0\text{ J}$.<br>• Active Duration Tracking: Active power duration $t$ (seconds) advances by 1 second on each valid non-suspended tick.<br>• Warm-Up Window ($t < 30\text{ s}$): While $t < 30\text{ s}$, Normalized Power and Intensity Factor are undefined (`null`); TSS publishes `null` (formatted as `"--"`).<br>• TSS Calculation ($t \ge 30\text{ s}$): If athlete Functional Threshold Power is configured ($\text{FTP} > 0$) and $\text{NP} \ge 0.0$ and $\text{IF} \ge 0.0$, the system SHALL compute live TSS: $\text{TSS} = \frac{t \times \text{NP} \times \text{IF}}{\text{FTP} \times 3600.0} \times 100.0$, and publish via `mTssSensor.newValue(tss)`. If FTP is unconfigured ($\le 0$ or null), TSS publishes `null`.<br>• Active Pause Gating: When paused or auto-paused (`isRecordingSuspended() == true`), $W_{\text{joules}}$, $t$, and TSS MUST NOT advance.<br>• Session Reset: `resetSession()` SHALL reset $W_{\text{joules}} = 0.0$, $t = 0\text{ s}$, and publish `null` to both sensors.<br>3. *Thread Safety & Lifecycle Invariants*:<br>• All calculation, queue mutation, and sensor emission logic SHALL be synchronized within `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` monitors.<br>4. *Sensor Filter Defaults*:<br>• `WORK_KJ` and `TSS` SHALL default to `FilterType.INSTANTANEOUS` (1.0s direct).<br>5. *Activity Types*:<br>• `SensorType.WORK_KJ` and `SensorType.TSS` SHALL be registered in `ActivityType.BIKE_POWER`.<br>6. *Cockpit Grid & Guidance UI*:<br>• Cockpit tiles for WORK_KJ and TSS SHALL render `"--"` when undefined or unconfigured.<br>• In `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt`, selecting `TSS` when FTP is unconfigured SHALL display the guidance prompt with direct access to Zone Settings.<br>7. *9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• All string resources (`work_kj`, `work_kj_short`, `units_work_kj`, `tss`, `tss_short`) SHALL be defined across all 9 application locales: EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TRK-021`. Complements `REQ-TRK-019` (*Power-to-weight ratio*) and `REQ-TRK-020` (*Normalized Power & Intensity Factor*). Targets `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SensorType.java`, `ActivityType.java`, `SensorFilterDefaults.kt`, `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt`, and `strings.xml`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Cycling power support introduced originally in `BANALService`. `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` created in Sprint `2026-42.4` (`ATT-1289`, commit `5eee662f`) and extended for NP/IF (`ATT-1290`, commit `4fe4996c`). Active ticket `ATT-1291`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Athletes require external mechanical work (kJ) for fueling/caloric tracking and live TSS for endurance pacing.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Pause gating invariant strictly preserved, FTP preference integrity preserved, SQLite schema integrity preserved, and 100% test pass rate preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active cycling workout with power data,<br>• *When* riding at constant 200 Watts for 10 seconds,<br>• *Then* Work (kJ) accumulates to 2.0 kJ.<br>• *Given* constant 250 Watts for 3600 seconds (1 hour) with FTP = 250 W,<br>• *When* evaluating TSS at 1 hour,<br>• *Then* TSS displays exactly 100.<br>• *Given* an athlete in the first 29 seconds of a ride ($t < 30\text{ s}$),<br>• *When* observing TSS,<br>• *Then* TSS displays "--", while Work (kJ) accumulates normally from second 1.<br>• *Given* an athlete with unconfigured FTP,<br>• *When* observing TSS,<br>• *Then* TSS displays "--", and selecting the tile in edit mode prompts the user to configure FTP.<br>• *Given* active recording suspended (paused),<br>• *When* 1Hz ticks occur,<br>• *Then* neither Work (kJ) nor TSS advance.<br><br>**Invariants**: Pause gating, FTP DataStore integrity, SQLite column schema, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Real-time Mechanical Work (kJ) and Training Stress Score (TSS) telemetry. | `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SensorType.java`, `EditSensorFieldDialog.kt` | `TST-TRK-013` | Verified |

For Heart Rate (`HR_RUN`, `HR_BIKE`): Exactly $K = 5$ segments using `TTColor.Zone1..Zone5`.<br>  - For Cycling Power (`PWR_BIKE`): Exactly $K = 7$ segments using `TTColor.Zone1..Zone7`.<br>• Equal visual width per zone ($\frac{1}{K}$ width each) guarantees that narrow high-intensity target zones (e.g. Z4 Sweetspot, Z5 VO2max) remain clear, readable, and trackable without shrinking to unreadable slivers.<br>3. *Intra-Zone Needle Interpolation & Clamping Math (`ZoneGaugeMath.kt`) (`REQ-UI-376.3`)*:<br>• For interior closed zones $i \in \{1 \dots K-1\}$ with bounds $[L_i, U_i]$:<br>  $$\text{fraction}_i = \frac{v - L_i}{U_i - L_i} \in [0.0, 1.0]$$<br>  $$x_{\text{needle}} = \frac{(i - 1) + \text{fraction}_i}{K} \in [0.0, 1.0]$$<br>• Baseline lower bounds: $L_1 = 0.0\text{ W}$ for Power; $L_1 = 30.0\text{ bpm}$ for Heart Rate.<br>• For readings below baseline ($v \le L_1$): Needle clamps cleanly to $x_{\text{needle}} = 0.0$ (left edge of Zone 1).<br>• Open-Ended Top Zone Dynamic Ceiling:<br>  - L_{\text{top}}}{U_{\text{top}} - L_{\text{top}}}\right)$$<br>    $$x_{\text{needle}} = \frac{(K - 1) + \text{fraction}_{\text{top}}}{K}$$<br>  - Peak sprints ($v \ge U_{\text{top}}$) clamp cleanly to $x_{\text{needle}} = 1.0$ without overflow.<br>4. *Telemetry Stale / Disconnected / Null State Handling (`REQ-UI-376.4`)*:<br>• When telemetry is absent, disconnected, unconfigured, or stale (`v == null`, `v.isNaN()`, `!v.isFinite()`, or stale packet age $> 5\text{ s}$):<br>  - The needle SHALL be completely hidden (needle alpha 0.0).<br>  - The segmented zone track SHALL remain rendered with dimmed opacity (alpha 0.35), preserving full visual context of the zone boundaries.<br>5. *Cockpit UI & AMOLED Contrast Compliance (`REQ-UI-376.5`)*:<br>• `ZoneGaugeBar.kt` SHALL render a compact horizontal track (`height = 6.dp`, `shape = RoundedCornerShape(3.dp)`).<br>• Segments SHALL be separated by thin vertical dividers (`1.dp`).<br>• The outer track and segment dividers SHALL be stroked with `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outlineVariant` (`#2B3342`), ensuring non-text contrast $\ge 3:1$ against True-Black AMOLED backgrounds (`#000000`) for dark zones (`TTColor.Zone6` and `TTColor.Zone7`).<br>• The indicator needle SHALL be rendered with a high-contrast inverted marker (Pure White `#FFFFFF` with a 1dp dark shadow/border) with minimum height of `10.dp` centered vertically over the track, achieving $> 12:1$ contrast against any zone segment color.<br>• When configured, a compact active zone badge (`Z1`..`Z7`) rendered in the active zone color SHALL appear adjacent to the gauge.<br>6. *60 FPS Performance & Recomposition Decoupling (`REQ-UI-376.6`)*:<br>• The gauge needle position SHALL be calculated via pure $O(1)$ math.<br>• Needle rendering in Compose SHALL execute via canvas drawing or drawWithContent without triggering full tile recompositions on high-frequency power packets (2Hz–4Hz).<br>7. *9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-UI-376.7`)*:<br>• Add string token `zone_display_gauge` across all 9 application locales: EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-UI-376`. outside `LifecycleUtils`.<br>• Standalone CLI linter `tools/lint_lifecycle_safety.py` SHALL verify zero violations.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Legacy code relied on symmetric lifecycle callbacks and unconstrained pre-Oreo background service start rules.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Android API 26+ background execution limits and lifecycle race conditions throw `IllegalStateException` on service starts and `IllegalArgumentException` on unregistering unregistered receivers.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Bounded service operations via `bindService(..., BIND_AUTO_CREATE)` remain fully functional; receiver unregistration postcondition (receiver is unregistered) is preserved; zero crashes.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an application in the background when `BANALService` or Pebble services are requested,<br>• *When* `safeStartService` executes,<br>• *Then* `null` is returned, a warning is logged, and no `IllegalStateException` is thrown.<br>• *Given* an Activity or Service being destroyed where a `BroadcastReceiver` was not registered,<br>• *When* `safeUnregisterReceiver` executes,<br>• *Then* `false` is returned, a warning is logged, and no `IllegalArgumentException` crashes the process.<br>• *Given* the automated test suite,<br>• *When* `LifecycleServiceReceiverSafetyAuditTest` runs,<br>• *Then* zero unshielded calls exist in `app/src/main`.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero unhandled lifecycle exceptions, idempotent receiver unregistration, 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Guarded service launches and idempotent BroadcastReceiver teardown across lifecycle boundaries. | `LifecycleUtils.kt`, `MainActivityWithNavigation.kt`, `BANALServiceRepository.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java`, `TrackerService.java`, `DeviceManager.java` | `TST-STB-016` | Verified |
| **REQ-DAT-001** | **Deterministic Resource Management via Try-With-Resources and Bounds Checking on SQLite Cursors Across Legacy Database Managers.** | The system SHALL guarantee deterministic resource cleanup and zero cursor leaks by enclosing all internally-consumed `Cursor` instances in `try-with-resources` (`AutoCloseable`) blocks across all Java database managers, database helpers, and file exporters, AND SHALL guarantee crash immunity against `CursorIndexOutOfBoundsException` by validating cursor navigation before accessing column data (ATT-3550, parent epic ATT-431):<br>1. *Try-With-Resources Allocation (`REQ-DAT-001.1`)*:<br>• All local queries (`db.query(...)`, `db.rawQuery(...)`) in `ExportStatusDatabaseManager`, `DevicesDatabaseManager`, `SportTypeDatabaseManager`, `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager`, `SegmentsDatabaseManager`, `WorkoutSamplesDatabaseManager`, `PebbleDatabaseManager`, `EquipmentDbHelper`, `ActiveDevicesDbHelper`, `ExportManager`, `BaseFileWriter`, and `GPXFileWriter` SHALL be wrapped in `try (Cursor cursor = ...)`.<br>• Trailing manual `cursor.close()` calls on try-with-resources cursors SHALL be eliminated.<br>• Public/protected factory/provider methods returning an open `Cursor` to external components (e.g. `getCursorForAllDevices()`, `getDeviceCursor(long)`) SHALL NOT close the cursor internally, but callers consuming them within internal methods SHALL use try-with-resources.<br>2. *Comprehensive Navigation Safety & Canonical Sentinel Mapping (`REQ-DAT-001.2`)*:<br>• All cursor navigation operations (`cursor.moveToFirst()`, `cursor.moveToLast()`, and iteration loops `while (cursor.moveToNext())`) SHALL be conditionally validated before reading column indices.<br>• If a query yields 0 rows (empty result set), query methods SHALL return deterministic, type-specific canonical empty-state sentinels:<br>  - Collection and List types (`List<T>`, `Set<T>`): SHALL return empty collection (`Collections.emptyList()`, `Collections.emptySet()`, or empty `new ArrayList<>()`).<br>  - Entity models, Objects, and Strings (`DeviceType`, `String`, custom POJO): SHALL return `null` (or empty string `""` where specified by method signature).<br>  - Database Identifiers (`long id`): SHALL return `-1L`.<br>  - Numeric counts and scalar metrics (`int`, `double`): SHALL return `0` / `0.0`.<br>  - Boolean state flags: SHALL return `false`.<br>• Zero `CursorIndexOutOfBoundsException` or `NullPointerException` crashes SHALL occur on empty or closed cursor states.<br>3. *Static Architectural Guard & Whitelist-Based CI/CD Contract (`REQ-DAT-001.3`)*:<br>• The codebase SHALL enforce try-with-resources and cursor safety via an automated JUnit architecture audit test (`TryWithResourcesCursorAuditTest.kt`) executed as part of `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`, verifying that all local cursor allocations in Java database managers use try-with-resources.<br>• The static audit test and standalone CLI linter `tools/lint_cursor_safety.py` SHALL utilize an explicit whitelist/method signature detection for provider methods returning `Cursor` (`public/protected Cursor get...`), preventing false positives on intentional cursor factory methods.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-DAT-001`. Fixes resource leak and empty cursor crash vectors in ATT-3550.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-42.4 (`ATT-3550`). Legacy code was written prior to Android API 19 try-with-resources support, relying on manual cursor closing and assuming non-empty query results.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Unchecked cursor navigation caused `CursorIndexOutOfBoundsException` when rows were missing, and unshielded cursors leaked on runtime exceptions.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Database schemas, table columns, query filters, and return values remain 100% backward compatible; cursors returning to external callers remain open.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* all Java database managers in `app/src/main`,<br>• *When* querying SQLite tables,<br>• *Then* all local cursors are enclosed in `try-with-resources`, ensuring automatic closure even if an exception occurs.<br>• *Given* any query method executed against an empty database table or non-existent record ID,<br>• *When* `cursor.moveToFirst()` returns `false`,<br>• *Then* the method returns safely with the specified sentinel value (`emptyList()`, `null`, `-1L`, `0`, or `false`) without throwing `CursorIndexOutOfBoundsException`.<br>• *Given* the test suite,<br>• *When* `TryWithResourcesCursorAuditTest` runs,<br>• *Then* zero unshielded local cursor allocations exist in Java database managers and zero false positives are reported on cursor provider methods.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero cursor leaks, zero `CursorIndexOutOfBoundsException`, deterministic sentinel return mapping, 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Deterministic resource management via try-with-resources and bounds checking on SQLite cursors across legacy database managers. | `ExportStatusDatabaseManager.java`, `DevicesDatabaseManager.java`, `SportTypeDatabaseManager.java`, `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager.java`, `PebbleDatabaseManager.java`, `BaseFileWriter.java` | `TST-DAT-001` | Verified |

workout summary record found to resume.")`), retain safe canonical sentinel defaults (`mWorkoutID = -1L`, `mBaseFileName = ""`, `mTimeTotal_s = 0`, `mTimeActive_s = 0`, `mDistanceTotal_m = 0.0`), and assigned to `mBaseFileName`, `mWorkoutID`, `mTimeTotal_s`, `mTimeActive_s`, `calories`, `lapNr`, and `mDistanceTotal_m`, as well as values passed to `BANALService.setInitialSensorValue(...)`, SHALL SHALL be rendered.<br>  - In the right column, below `timeOnSegment`: when `prDeltaFormatted != null`, render `stringResource(R.string.segment_status_pr_delta, liveSegmentData.prDeltaFormatted)` colored in `TTColor.Zone2` (green) when `(prDeltaSeconds ?: 1L) <= 0L` and `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant` when `> 0L`.<br>4. *9-Language Localization Parity (Rule 29)*:<br>• `segment_status_past_finish` and `segment_status_pr_delta` SHALL exist with non-empty translations and matching format specifiers (`%1$s`) across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br>• `segment_status_offset` SHALL be corrected in `values-ja` to "コースずれ: %1$s" and clarified in `es`, `fr`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt`.<br>5. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Virtual gate finish line crossing math, polyline orthogonal projection, bottom sheet layout height, and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate MUST NOT be broken.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-UI-379`). Complements `REQ-MAP-027` (*ClimbPro Cockpit Sheet*), `REQ-UI-196` (*Live Segment Bottom Sheet Design*), `REQ-UI-340` (*LiveSegmentSheet Type-Safe Numeric Metric Evaluation on Segment Finish*), and `REQ-UI-366` (*Harmonized Live Segment and Live Climb Tracking Bottom Sheet Architecture*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: `LiveSegmentData` and `SegmentLiveDetails` were introduced in Sprint 2026-40.1 (`ATT-1644` / `ATT-1735`, commits `50123512`, `7d488f51`) and refined in Sprint 2026-41.8 (`ATT-3108`, commit `91b12a9a`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: When segment tracking was first implemented, `segmentOffset` was the only secondary distance field on `LiveSegmentData`. To display how far the rider had traveled after crossing the finish line before auto-dismissal, `distanceToEnd` was shoved into `segmentOffset`. At the time, `SegmentLiveDetails` simply displayed all three lines statically without state-based visibility branches.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Active cross-track deviation warnings while on segment, along-track orthogonal projection, finish line virtual gate detection, and 100% full clean-room test suite pass rate are strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a live segment transitioning to `LiveSegmentStatus.FINISHED` with `distanceToEnd = 210.0`, `timeOnSegment = 219`, and `prTime_raw = 229`,<br>• *When* `SegmentLiveDetails` renders,<br>• *Then* it displays `distanceOnSegment`, "Nach Ziel: 210 m" / "Past finish: 210 m" in neutral `onSurfaceVariant`, and "-0:10 vs. PR" in green (`TTColor.Zone2`), with zero occurrences of "Ziel in: 0 m" or red "Daneben: 210 m".<br>• *Given* a live segment in `LiveSegmentStatus.APPROACHING` state,<br>• *When* `SegmentLiveDetails` renders,<br>• *Then* it displays `distanceToStart` and `remainingDistance`, and completely omits the lateral offset row ("Daneben: --").<br>• *Given* a live segment in `LiveSegmentStatus.ON_SEGMENT` with `distanceToSegment = 40.0`,<br>• *When* `SegmentLiveDetails` renders,<br>• *Then* it displays `distanceOnSegment`, `remainingDistance`, and `segmentOffset` ("Daneben: 40 m") styled with `TTColor.Zone4`.<br>• *Given* all 9 supported locale `strings.xml` resource files,<br>• *When* resolving `segment_status_past_finish`, `segment_status_pr_delta`, and `segment_status_offset`,<br>• *Then* all keys exist, are non-empty, and format strings compile cleanly.<br><br>**Invariants**: Pure UI presentation, zero changes to GPS projection math, and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | State-aware live segment lifecycle metrics, past-finish rollout & PR delta feedback in LiveSegmentSheet. | `LiveSegmentSheet.kt`, `SegmentLiveDetails.kt`, `LiveSegmentsRepository.kt`, `strings.xml` (all 9 locales) | `TST-UI-342` | Verified |
| **REQ-MAP-050** | **Calibrated Piecewise Linear-to-Logarithmic Follow-Me High-Speed Zoom and Autonomous Camera Control.** | The system SHALL calibrate Follow-Me camera zoom using a piecewise linear-to-logarithmic curve, raise minimum zoom to street-level resolution, and streamline Advanced Settings by removing manual camera tuning controls (ATT-3581, amending `REQ-MAP-042` and `REQ-MAP-049`):<br>1. *Piecewise Linear-to-Logarithmic Zoom Curve (`calculateFollowMeTargetZoom` in `MapBehaviors.kt`)*:<br>• For speeds $0.0 \le \text{speedKmh} \le 20.0\text{ km/h}$, target zoom SHALL interpolate linearly between `baseZoom` ($20.0f$ at $0\text{ km/h}$) and `cruisingZoom` ($18.0f$ at $20\text{ km/h}$): $\text{targetZoom} = \text{baseZoom} - \frac{\text{baseZoom} - \text{cruisingZoom}}{20.0} \times \text{speedKmh}$.<br>• For speeds $\text{speedKmh} > 20.0\text{ km/h}$, target zoom SHALL scale logarithmically with $\log_2(\text{speedKmh} / 20.0)$: $\text{rawZoom} = \text{cruisingZoom} - \frac{\text{baseZoom} - \text{cruisingZoom}}{2.0} \times \frac{\ln(\text{speedKmh} / 20.0)}{\ln(2.0)}$, returning $\text{rawZoom.coerceIn(minZoom, maxZoom)}$.<br>• When `speedZoomEnabled == false`, the camera SHALL lock firmly to $\text{baseZoom.coerceIn(minZoom, maxZoom)}$.<br>• Default `minZoom` SHALL equal `16.0f` (`DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_MIN_ZOOM = 16.0f` in `TuningPreferencesDefaults`).<br>2. *Autonomous Camera Parameter Wiring (`ATrainingTrackerMap.kt`)*:<br>• `followMeController(...)` SHALL be invoked using canonical defaults from `TuningPreferencesDefaults` for all camera tuning parameters (`baseZoom = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_INITIAL_ZOOM`, `speedZoomEnabled = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_SPEED_ZOOM_ENABLED`, `cruisingZoom = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_CRUISING_ZOOM`, `tiltAngle = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_TILT_ANGLE`, `lookaheadPaddingPercent = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_LOOKAHEAD_PADDING_PERCENT`, `speedSmoothingAlpha = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_SPEED_SMOOTHING_ALPHA`, `bearingSmoothingAlpha = DEFAULT_MAP_FOLLOW_ME_BEARING_SMOOTHING_ALPHA`).<br>• Legacy persisted DataStore tweaks SHALL NOT override calibrated physical camera behavior.<br>3. *Streamlined Navigation Advanced Settings UI (`NavigationSection.kt`, `AdvancedTuningScreen.kt`, `AdvancedTuningDialog.kt`)*:<br>• In `NavigationSection.kt`, the Follow-Me map camera sub-section divider, header (`tuning_map_camera_section_title`), and the 7 camera tuning items (`Initial Zoom`, `Speed-Dependent Zoom Enabled`, `Cruising Speed Zoom`, `Tilt Angle`, `Lookahead Bottom Padding`, `Speed Smoothing`, `Bearing Smoothing`) SHALL be removed.<br>• Unused Follow-Me parameters in `AdvancedTuningScreen.kt` and `AdvancedTuningDialog.kt` SHALL be removed.<br>• Remaining Navigation items (`routeSelectionRadiusKm`, `navigationCueDismissDurationSec`, `turnCueCountdownDistanceMeters`, `autoFollowUniqueRouteEnabled`) SHALL remain fully active and configurable.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants*:<br>• Low-speed linear progression ($\le 20\text{ km/h}$), exponential speed/bearing smoothing, hysteresis deadband ($0.10f$), forward lookahead projection, and 100% full clean-room unit test suite pass rate MUST NOT be broken.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-MAP-042` (*Speed-Dependent Map Zoom Calibration*, Sprint 2026-41.6, `ATT-2946`) and `REQ-MAP-049` (*Follow-Me Camera Speed Zoom Smoothing...*, Sprint 2026-42.0, `ATT-3227`). Formally tracked as `REQ-MAP-050`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: `REQ-MAP-042` introduced linear speed-dependent zoom and camera sliders in Sprint 2026-41.6 (commit `3c59a421`). `REQ-MAP-048` added forward lookahead projection in Sprint 2026-41.9 (commit `d97e201b`). `REQ-MAP-049` added exponential smoothing in Sprint 2026-42.0 (commit `c891ba32`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Early Compose prototyping used linear interpolation and exposed developer sliders for quick experimentation. Because Google Maps ground resolution scales as $2^{-\text{zoom}}$, continuing linear slope above $20\text{ km/h}$ caused exponential viewport blowout.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Low-speed behavior ($0\text{–}20\text{ km/h}$) remains identical. Smoothing filters, hysteresis deadband, forward projection, and 100% full clean-room unit test pass rate are preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* speeds between $0\text{ km/h}$ and $20\text{ km/h}$,<br>• *When* `calculateFollowMeTargetZoom` is evaluated with default parameters,<br>• *Then* zoom interpolates linearly from $20.0f$ ($0\text{ km/h}$) to $19.0f$ ($10\text{ km/h}$) and $18.0f$ ($20\text{ km/h}$).<br>• *Given* descent speeds of $30\text{ km/h}$, $40\text{ km/h}$, $50\text{ km/h}$, $60\text{ km/h}$, and $90\text{ km/h}$,<br>• *When* `calculateFollowMeTargetZoom` is evaluated,<br>• *Then* it returns $17.42f \pm 0.01f$ at $30\text{ km/h}$, $17.00f \pm 0.01f$ at $40\text{ km/h}$, $16.68f \pm 0.01f$ at $50\text{ km/h}$, $16.42f \pm 0.01f$ at $60\text{ km/h}$, and clamps at $16.0f$ at $90\text{ km/h}$.<br>• *Given* `speedZoomEnabled == false`,<br>• *When* `calculateFollowMeTargetZoom` is evaluated at any speed,<br>• *Then* it returns `baseZoom` ($20.0f$).<br>• *Given* the athlete opening Advanced Settings -> Navigation,<br>• *When* rendered,<br>• *Then* the obsolete Follow-Me camera tuning sliders are omitted, while Route Selection Radius, Cue Dismiss Duration, Turn Cue Countdown Distance, and Auto-Follow Unique Route remain present.<br><br>**Invariants**: Pure UI presentation and zoom curve calibration; GPS position tracking and 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Calibrated piecewise linear-to-logarithmic Follow-Me high-speed zoom and autonomous camera control. | `MapBehaviors.kt`, `TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `NavigationSection.kt`, `AdvancedTuningScreen.kt`, `AdvancedTuningDialog.kt`, `ATrainingTrackerMap.kt` | `TST-MAP-052` | Verified |

`android:foregroundServiceType="location|health"`.<br>• The string `connectedDevice` SHALL be completely purged from all service definitions.<br>3. *Runtime FGS Bitmask Simplification (`REQ-TRK-022.3`)*:<br>• In `TrackerService.java`, `determineForegroundServiceType()` SHALL start with `ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_LOCATION`.<br>• On Android 14+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE`), if `hasHealthPermission()` returns `true`, the bitmask SHALL add `ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_HEALTH`.<br>• `ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_CONNECTED_DEVICE` SHALL NEVER be included in the returned bitmask.<br>• The unused `hasBluetoothPermission()` helper in `TrackerService.java` SHALL be removed.<br>4. *Preservation of System Invariants (`REQ-TRK-022.4`)*:<br>• Uninterrupted workout session recording on Android 14+ (API 34+).<br>• Zero `SecurityException` during Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Amends `REQ-CON-019` (*Robust Bluetooth LE Sensor Discovery & Direct LE Transport Connection Architecture*, ATT-2773) and `REQ-TRK-015` Formally tracked as `REQ-TRK-022`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.4 (`ATT-2773`, commit `67451a9`): added `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE` and `connectedDevice` attribute. mMean4thPower) / (double) mCount4thPower`) and `mLastCalculatedNp = Math.pow(mMean4thPower, 0.25)` SHALL update on every valid tick starting at $k = 1$.<br>2. *Immediate Live Telemetry Emission From Second 1 (`REQ-TRK-023.2`)*:<br>• Starting from the first valid power sample (`k = 1`), `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` SHALL publish non-null live `NORMALIZED_POWER` (`mLastCalculatedNp`) and, when `ftp != null && ftp > 0`, non-null live `INTENSITY_FACTOR` (`NP / FTP`) and `TSS` (`(mActivePowerDurationSec * NP * IF) / (FTP * 36.0)`).<br>3. *Seamless Transition to Full 30s Window & Empty Guard (`REQ-TRK-023.3`)*:<br>• From second 30 onward (`mPowerWindow30s.size() == 30`), `pRolling` SHALL evaluate over the full 30-sample FIFO sliding window (`sum / 30.0`).<br>• Only when `mPowerWindow30s.isEmpty()` (or when instantaneous input `power` is `null`, `NaN`, infinite, or `< 0.0`) SHALL `NORMALIZED_POWER`, `INTENSITY_FACTOR`, and `TSS` emit `null`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TRK-023`, amending the initial 29-second warm-up behavior of `REQ-TRK-020` (`ATT-1290`) and `REQ-TRK-021` (`ATT-1291`). (`_mapState` and `_uiState`) in both `READY` (empty `currentTrack`) and `TRACKING` (non-empty `currentTrack`) modes without requiring a concurrent `currentTrack` emission, converting `null` | **REQ-TOOL-006** | **Variable-Interval TCX Telemetry Interpolation, Time-Based Playback Stepping & Workout-Relative ADB GPS Timestamp Synchronization in `tools/replay_workout.py`.** | The TCX workout replay tool (`tools/replay_workout.py`) SHALL preserve $1\text{ Hz}$ physiological telemetry across variable-interval GPS `<Trackpoint>` entries, compute fallback speed from distance/time deltas with zero-division / `NaN` / `Inf` guards when `<Speed>` extensions are absent, advance `ReplayEngine` by workout elapsed time (`time_sec`) rather than raw array index, and stamp ADB mock GPS fixes with Replay Session Epoch workout-relative timestamps so Android `SpeedAndLocationDevice.java` calculates accurate speed regardless of GPS recording interval or replay multiplier (ATT-3927, amending `REQ-TOOL-002`):<br>1. *Variable-Interval TCX Trackpoint Preservation, Linear Coordinate Interpolation & Safe Fallback Speed (`REQ-TOOL-006.1`)*:<br>• In `TcxParser.parse_file()`, whenever a `.tcx` file contains at least one valid `<Position>` (`<LatitudeDegrees>`, `<LongitudeDegrees>`), the parser SHALL retain intermediate `<Trackpoint>` elements that have a valid `<Time>` even when `<Position>` is omitted on those intermediate points, preserving their $1\text{ Hz}$ `hr_bpm`, `cadence_rpm`, `power_watts`, `ele`, and `distance_m` telemetry.<br>• For `<Trackpoint>` elements missing `<Position>`, `TcxParser.parse_file()` SHALL linearly interpolate `lat` and `lon` (and `ele` when `<AltitudeMeters>` is missing) with respect to workout elapsed time `time_sec` between the bounding known GPS fixes (and carry the first/last known fix at leading/trailing boundaries).<br>• After computing cumulative `distance_m` and `step_d`, for every point $i \ge 1$ where `<Speed>` was not provided in `<Extensions>` (or `speed_mps <= 0.0`): if $\Delta t = \text{points}[i].\text{time\_sec} - \text{points}[i-1].\text{time\_sec} \ge 0.001$, `TcxParser` SHALL compute `raw_speed = step_d / dt` and set `points[i].speed_mps = raw_speed if math.isfinite(raw_speed) else 0.0`; if $\Delta t < 0.001$ (duplicate or malformed timestamps), `points[i].speed_mps` SHALL be set to `0.0` (preventing `ZeroDivisionError`, `NaN`, or `Inf`). If `points[0].speed_mps <= 0.0` and `len(points) > 1`, `points[0].speed_mps` SHALL be initialized to the first subsequent finite non-zero `speed_mps` (or `0.0`).<br>2. *Elapsed-Time Playback Stepping in `ReplayEngine` (`REQ-TOOL-006.2`)*:<br>• `ReplayEngine` SHALL maintain `self.elapsed_time_sec: float` initialized to `self.points[0].time_sec` (or `0.0`) and synchronized with `self.points[self.current_index].time_sec` on `seek_ratio()`, `seek_time()`, and `stop()`.<br>• `ReplayEngine.step(dt_sec: float = 1.0)` SHALL advance `self.elapsed_time_sec += dt_sec * self.speed_multiplier` and advance `self.current_index` to the highest index $k \le \text{len(points)} - 1$ where `self.points[k].time_sec <= self.elapsed_time_sec`, cleanly clamping to `len(self.points) - 1` and transitioning to `PAUSED` at the final point without index-out-of-bounds errors.<br>• In `run_headless_cli`, the loop SHALL tick at a fixed $1.0\text{ s}$ base interval (`sleep_t = max(0.01, 1.0 - elapsed)`) so `speed_multiplier` is applied once in `engine.step()` rather than squared.<br>3. *Replay Session Epoch Workout-Relative ADB GPS Timestamps in `AdbGpsInjector` (`REQ-TOOL-006.3`)*:<br>• `AdbGpsInjector` SHALL maintain a Replay Session Epoch `self.base_epoch_ms: int = int(time.time() * 1000)` and expose `reset_epoch(self, time_sec: float = 0.0)` which sets `self.base_epoch_ms = int(time.time() * 1000) - int(round(time_sec * 1000.0))` (invoked on `stop()`, `load_file()`, or explicit seek so `base_epoch_ms` maintains the exact relative `time_sec` offset from the new current position without artificial `+1000ms` stuttering).<br>• `AdbGpsInjector.inject_location(self, lat: float, lon: float, ele: float = 0.0, speed_mps: float = 0.0, bearing_deg: float = 0.0, time_sec: Optional[float] = None)` SHALL compute `timestamp_ms = self.base_epoch_ms + int(round(time_sec * 1000.0))` when `time_sec is not None` (falling back to `int(time.time() * 1000)` when `time_sec is None`), preserving exact $\Delta t_{\text{workout}} = (t_i - t_{i-1}) \times 1000\text{ ms}$ across all playback multipliers.<br>• Both `ReplayGuiWindow._emit_telemetry` and `run_headless_cli` SHALL pass `time_sec=pt.time_sec` to `gps_injector.inject_location(...)`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TOOL-006`, amending `REQ-TOOL-002` (`ATT-2969`) Clauses 1, 2, and 4. Targets `tools/replay_workout.py` and `tools/test_replay_workout.py`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-41.6 (`ATT-2969`, commit `1523f683`), Sprint 2026-42.0 (`ATT-3178`, `ATT-3179`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation (Why was this fence built?)*: `tools/replay_workout.py` was originally built against synthetic $1\text{ Hz}$ TCX files where every `<Trackpoint>` contained `<Position>` and `<Speed>` at uniform $1.0\text{ s}$ intervals.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants (Why is it safe to modify now?)*: Interpolating missing `<Position>` coordinates by `time_sec`, deriving fallback speed from `step_d / dt` (guarded by `dt >= 0.001` and `math.isfinite`), advancing `ReplayEngine` by `elapsed_time_sec`, and stamping ADB `--time` with `base_epoch_ms + int(round(time_sec * 1000))` fixes speed inflation and timeline jumps on variable-interval TCX files while remaining 100% identical for uniform $1\text{ Hz}$ TCX files and leaving production Android code (`SpeedAndLocationDevice.java`) untouched.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a variable-interval `.tcx` file where `<Trackpoint>` elements appear at $t = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\text{ s}$ with HR/Power at every second, `<Position>` only at $t = 0\text{ s}$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$, and no `<Speed>` extension,<br>• *When* parsed by `TcxParser.parse_file()`,<br>• *Then* all 6 trackpoints ($t = 0..5\text{ s}$) are retained with their $1\text{ Hz}$ HR/Power values, intermediate `lat`/`lon` coordinates at $t = 1..4\text{ s}$ are linearly interpolated by time, and `speed_mps` is derived from `step_d / dt > 0` (with `dt < 0.001` safely yielding `0.0`).<br>• *Given* `ReplayEngine` loaded with trackpoints at $t = 0, 5, 10, 15\text{ s}$ at $1\times$ speed,<br>• *When* `engine.step()` ($1.0\text{ s}$) is invoked 4 times ($t_{\text{elapsed}} = 4.0\text{ s}$), 5 times ($t_{\text{elapsed}} = 5.0\text{ s}$), and up to $t_{\text{elapsed}} \ge 15.0\text{ s}$,<br>• *Then* `current_index` remains `0` at $4.0\text{ s}$, advances to `1` ($t = 5.0\text{ s}$) on the 5th step, and transitions to `PAUSED` at `current_index == len(points) - 1` without index-out-of-bounds errors.<br>• *Given* `AdbGpsInjector.inject_location(..., time_sec=t)` called at $t = 0.0\text{ s}$ and $t = 5.0\text{ s}$ regardless of replay speed multiplier ($1\times, 2\times, 5\times, 10\times$),<br>• *When* inspecting the queued timestamps,<br>• *Then* `timestamp_ms(5.0) - timestamp_ms(0.0) == 5000`, so Android's `SpeedAndLocationDevice.java` computes the exact workout speed without inflation.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero production code modifications in `app/src/main`; full backward compatibility with `REQ-TOOL-002`, `REQ-TOOL-003`, `REQ-TOOL-004`; 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Fix TCX replay speed inflation and timeline progression for variable-interval GPS tracks in `tools/replay_workout.py`. | `tools/replay_workout.py`, `tools/test_replay_workout.py` | `TST-TOOL-006` | Verified |

the 0-based priority index of `deviceType` for `sensorType` across all sensor types (`SPEED`, `ALTITUDE`, `LOCATION`, `CADENCE`, single-device sensors).<br>• If `deviceType` is not in the priority list, it SHALL return fallback rank `1000 + deviceType.ordinal()`. (`handle.cancel(true)`), `TrackerService` SHALL invoke `mScheduler.shutdownNow()` so the `ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor` worker thread is terminated and cannot enqueue further 1 Hz ticks onto `mDbExecutor` after `onDestroy()` begins.<br>• `TrackerService` SHALL expose `@VisibleForTesting boolean isSchedulerShutdownForTesting()` and `@VisibleForTesting boolean isDbExecutorShutdownForTesting()`.<br>2. *Non-Blocking Main-Thread `onDestroy()` & FIFO-Ordered `endWorkout()` on `mDbExecutor` (`REQ-TRK-033.2`)*:<br>• `TrackerService.onDestroy()` SHALL execute or `endWorkout()` on the main thread.<br>• `TrackerService.onDestroy()` SHALL create `CompletableFuture<Void> finalizationFuture = new CompletableFuture<>()` (stored in `volatile` `mFinalizationFuture`, exposed via `@VisibleForTesting public CompletableFuture<Void> getFinalizationFuture()`), enqueue a terminal `finalizationTask` onto the single-threaded FIFO `mDbExecutor` (`mDbExecutor.execute(finalizationTask)`), and immediately call `mDbExecutor.shutdown()`.<br>• Inside `finalizationTask` on `mDbExecutor`: `try { if (!interrupted) endWorkout(); } catch (Throwable t) { Log.e(TAG, ...); } finally { mBanalService = null; releaseWakeLock(); finalizationFuture.complete(null); }`, guaranteeing all prior queued sample writes complete before `endWorkout()` runs and `mBanalService` / `mWakeLock` remain valid throughout `endWorkout()`.<br>• If `mDbExecutor.execute(finalizationTask)` throws `RejectedExecutionException`, `onDestroy()` SHALL run resetting `cTrackingMode = TrackingMode.READY`, `cManualPauseLocked = false`, and `cAutoPaused = false`, plus `sendBroadcast(new Intent(TRACKING_STATE_CHANGED).setPackage(getPackageName()))`.<br>• `TrackerService` SHALL define `TRACKING_ABORTED_INTENT = "com.atrainingtracker.trainingtracker.tracker.TrackerService.TRACKING_ABORTED_INTENT"` and `handleTrackingAborted()` (dispatched via `runOnMainThread(this::handleTrackingAborted)` inside the `START_NORMAL` `mDbExecutor.submit(...)` `catch (Exception e)` block before `stopSelf()`), resetting `TrainingApplication` state and broadcasting `TRACKING_ABORTED_INTENT`.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TRK-033`, extending `REQ-TRK-015` (`ATT-2641`), `REQ-TRK-027` (`ATT-3981`), `REQ-TRK-028` (`ATT-3984`), `REQ-TRK-030` (`ATT-3986`), and `REQ-TRK-032` (`ATT-3988`). `endWorkout()` and `finalizeLiveSession()`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `mDbExecutor.awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` was originally added to ensure pending 1 Hz sample writes finished before `endWorkout()` ran on the main thread.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Queuing `finalizationTask` onto the single-threaded FIFO `mDbExecutor` before `mDbExecutor.shutdown()` runs on `mDbExecutor`.<br>• *Given* `TrainingApplication.getTrackingMode() == TrackingMode.TRACKING` and `START_NORMAL` database initialization throws an exception,<br>• *When* the `mDbExecutor` Targets `app/build.gradle`, `app/proguard-rules.pro`, and `ProGuardRulesContractTest.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `f1de722dd6d88a193444371fdd9e8f55de9820c5` (May 11, 2026) disabled `minifyEnabled` as an emergency precaution because comprehensive keep rules were not yet configured.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Emergency deactivation avoided potential reflection/SDK crashes, but resulted in 1% obfuscation, violating Google Play's mandatory 25% threshold.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Full reflection safety for SQLite enum resolution, ANT+/BLE hardware connectivity, Garmin FIT export, and 100% clean-room test pass rate strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* `app/build.gradle` and `app/proguard-rules.pro`,<br>• *When* `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease` is executed,<br>• *Then* the build succeeds, `mapping.txt` is generated at `app/build/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt`, and release DEX obfuscation is $\ge 25\%$.<br>• *Given* `app/proguard-rules.pro`,<br>• *When* inspected for Compose and keep rules in `ProGuardRulesContractTest`,<br>• *Then* blanket `-keep class androidx.compose.**` is absent, and domain enum, FIT, ANT+, Pebble, Dropbox, and serialization keep rules are present.<br>• *Given* the complete unit test suite,<br>• *When* executing `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`,<br>• *Then* 100% of tests pass without regression.<br><br>**Invariants**: Debug build speed preserved (`minifyEnabled false` in debug); SQLite enum persistence intact; 100% clean-room test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Enable R8 minification, resource shrinking, and DEX code obfuscation in release builds with safe ProGuard keep rules to satisfy Google Play threshold (>= 25%). | `app/build.gradle`, `app/proguard-rules.pro`, `ProGuardRulesContractTest.kt` | `TST-BLD-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-UI-411** | **Configurable Horizontal Section Dividers with Optional Mini-Titles in Cockpit Sensor Grid.** | The system SHALL support configurable horizontal section dividers with optional mini-titles between sensor rows in Cockpit tracking tabs (`TrackingViewsDbHelper`, `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager`, `TrackingViewsRepository`, `SensorGridScreen.kt`), persisting them in `FlexibleGenericView.db` with automated row shift tracking, prominent divider stroke contrast, horizontally centered mini-titles, unambiguous split iconography, minimal vertical height overhead, and 9-language localization parity (ATT-4055, refined by ATT-4286):<br>1. *Database Schema & Migration (`REQ-UI-411.1`)*:<br>• In `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager.TrackingViewsDbHelper`, `DB_VERSION` SHALL be incremented to `14` (verified as the next sequential schema version for `FlexibleGenericView.db`).<br>• A dedicated table `SectionDividersTable` SHALL be created with columns: `_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `ViewId INTEGER NOT NULL`, `RowNr INTEGER NOT NULL`, `Title TEXT`, and constraint `UNIQUE(ViewId, RowNr) ON CONFLICT REPLACE`.<br>• In `onUpgrade(SQLiteDatabase db, int oldVersion, int newVersion)`, when `oldVersion < 14`, table `SectionDividersTable` SHALL be created idempotently via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS SectionDividersTable (...)`.<br>2. *Data Access & Row Shift Invariants (`REQ-UI-411.2`)*:<br>• `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager` SHALL provide methods `getSectionDividers(long viewId)`, `setSectionDivider(long viewId, int rowNr, @Nullable String title)`, `deleteSectionDivider(long viewId, int rowNr)`, and `deleteSectionDividersForView(long viewId)`.<br>• When a new row is inserted at `rowNr` in `insertSensorFieldAt(long tabViewId, int rowNr, int colNr, ...)` with `colNr == -1`, any existing divider at `RowNr >= rowNr` for `tabViewId` SHALL shift up by 1 (`UPDATE SectionDividersTable SET RowNr = RowNr + 1 WHERE ViewId = ? AND RowNr >= ?`).<br>• When a row is removed or deleted, any divider at `RowNr > deletedRowNr` SHALL shift down by 1 (`UPDATE SectionDividersTable SET RowNr = RowNr - 1 WHERE ViewId = ? AND RowNr > ?`), while any divider attached to `deletedRowNr` SHALL be re-indexed during `normalizeGrid(tabViewId)` to the surviving row or removed if no rows remain.<br>• When `normalizeGrid(long tabViewId)` re-indexes distinct rows to contiguous `1..N`, existing section dividers for `tabViewId` SHALL be mapped to the matching new row indices, and any orphaned dividers SHALL be deleted.<br>• When a tab is deleted in `deleteTabView(long viewId)`, all dividers for `viewId` SHALL be deleted.<br>3. *Repository Flow & Screen State Synchronization (`REQ-UI-411.3`)*:<br>• `TrackingViewsRepository` SHALL expose `fun getSectionDividersFlow(tabViewId: Long): Flow<List<SectionDividerInfo>>` triggered by `configUpdateTrigger`.<br>• `TrackingScreenState` SHALL include `val sectionDividers: List<SectionDividerInfo> = emptyList()`.<br>• `TrackingViewModel` SHALL collect dividers from `TrackingViewsRepository` and update `TrackingScreenState.sectionDividers`.<br>4. *Glanceable Cockpit Rendering, Prominence & Centered Mini-Titles (`REQ-UI-411.4`)*:<br>• In `ScreenMode.TRACKING` and `ScreenMode.PREVIEW`, `SensorGridScreen.kt` SHALL render a section divider above any visible row that has a matching entry in `state.sectionDividers` (`divider.rowNr == fieldsInThisRow.first().rowNr`).<br>• When `divider.title` is null or blank, the divider SHALL render with a prominent high-contrast stroke (`HorizontalDivider`, `thickness = 2.5.dp`, `color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline`) across the grid with minimal vertical padding (`padding(vertical = 4.dp)`), ensuring clear demarcation against bordered sensor cells with total height $\le 10\text{ dp}$.<br>• When `divider.title` is present, the divider mini-title SHALL be horizontally centered across the full row width, flanked symmetrically by left and right `HorizontalDivider` segments with equal `Modifier.weight(1f)` and `thickness = 2.dp` (`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline`), styled with `MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall`, uppercase, bold, letter-spacing, and primary color, with total height overhead constrained to $\le 20\text{ dp}$.<br>• Mini-titles SHALL specify `maxLines = 1` and `overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis`, guaranteeing that long text strings gracefully truncate on narrow screen displays and never cause multi-line wrapping or breach the $\le 20\text{ dp}$ vertical height constraint.<br>5. *Configuration Mode WYSIWYG Controls & Unambiguous Split Iconography (`REQ-UI-411.5`)*:<br>• In `ScreenMode.CONFIGURATION`, an inter-row divider action/indicator SHALL be displayed next to `RowAdder` between rows.<br>• When `existingDivider == null`, the divider insertion action button SHALL render icon `Icons.Default.HorizontalSplit` with tint `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline` and contentDescription `stringResource(R.string.cockpit_section_divider_add)`, strictly prohibiting the use of `Icons.Default.HorizontalRule` (`—`) to eliminate any false visual affordance of a minus/row-delete button (`+ / -`) adjacent to `RowAdder` (`Icons.Default.Add`).<br>• When `existingDivider != null`, the action button SHALL render icon `Icons.Default.Title` with tint `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary` and contentDescription `stringResource(R.string.cockpit_section_divider_edit)`.<br>• Clicking the action SHALL launch `EditSectionDividerDialog` allowing the user to select from localized quick-pick preset chips (*Power*, *Heart Rate*, *Lap*, *Pacing*, *Navigation*, *Total*), enter custom free text, clear the title to make it an unlabeled divider line, or delete the divider entirely.<br>6. *9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-UI-411.6`)*:<br>• All UI strings for section divider controls, dialog actions, and preset chips SHALL exist across all 9 supported locales (`values`, `values-de`, `values-es`, `values-fr`, `values-it`, `values-ja`, `values-nl`, `values-pl`, `values-pt`).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-UI-411.4` (Glanceable Cockpit Rendering & Truncation Safety) and `REQ-UI-411.5` (Configuration Mode WYSIWYG Controls) within `REQ-UI-411` (*Configurable Horizontal Section Dividers with Optional Mini-Titles in Cockpit Sensor Grid*), refined by `ATT-4286`. Targets `SensorGridScreen.kt`, `SensorGridScreenLayoutTest.kt`, and `SensorGridLocalizationTest.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4055` (commit `6199b2a45fcfb81f13a31906b3e2b725ea6c4618`, Sprint `2026-42.10`), refined in `ATT-4286` (Sprint `2026-43.1`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `Icons.Default.HorizontalRule` was selected literally to represent a horizontal divider rule, but placed directly next to `RowAdder`'s `+` icon it misleadingly functioned as a minus/delete button (`-`). A faint `1.5.dp` stroke with `outlineVariant` visually blended with `1.dp` cell borders, and asymmetric weights (`0.12f`/`0.88f`) were an exploratory left-accent layout that appeared lopsided on device.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Replacing `HorizontalRule` with `HorizontalSplit` removes the deceptive minus affordance while preserving click handlers, accessibility descriptions, and active title indicators. Centering titles via symmetric `weight(1f)` flanking lines provides balanced layout across all screen sizes and orientations without mutating database schema (v14) or row-shift logic.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* the Cockpit in `ScreenMode.CONFIGURATION`,<br>• *When* viewing the inter-row controls between sensor rows,<br>• *Then* the section divider in `ScreenMode.TRACKING` or `ScreenMode.PREVIEW`,<br>• *When* rendered above a row,<br>• *Then* it renders with a prominent stroke (`thickness = 2.5.dp`, `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline`) distinguishable from adjacent cell borders with total height $\le 10\text{ dp}$.<br>• *Given* a titled section divider in `ScreenMode.TRACKING` or `ScreenMode.PREVIEW`,<br>• *When* rendered above a row,<br>• *Then* the title is horizontally centered with symmetric flanking divider lines (`weight(1f)`, `thickness = 2.dp`, `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline`), truncating with ellipsis (`maxLines = 1`) if long.<br>• *Given* the Cockpit in `ScreenMode.CONFIGURATION`,<br>• *When* the user taps the section divider action AND RowNr >= ?`).<br>• If a section divider's row coordinate is shifted, it SHALL retain its relative position between rows. Targets `TrackingViewsDatabaseManager.java`, `TrackingViewsRealSqliteMigrationTest.kt`, and `TrackingViewsDatabaseManagerTest.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4010`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, discovered during independent whole-app code review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`). `insertSensorFieldAt` was authored in March 2026 (commit `5a8d102e`) when the application supported only a single global layout view. samples).<br>• Centralized Constants: System constants SHALL be centralized (`ExportConfig` / `ExportStatusDatabaseManager`: `MAX_RETRIES = 3`, `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000L`,
