value : characteristic.getValue()).clone()`).<br>• A decoupled snapshot characteristic populated with the cloned byte buffer SHALL be dispatched to `mHandler`, guaranteeing that subsequent incoming BLE packets cannot mutate payload data before or during main-thread processing.<br>2. *Deterministic Search Timeout Lifecycle & Reconnect Backoff (`REQ-CON-020.2`)*:<br>• `MyBTLEDevice` SHALL maintain a single, reusable `mSearchTimeoutRunnable`.<br>• All pending search timeouts SHALL be explicitly cancelled via `mHandler.removeCallbacks(mSearchTimeoutRunnable)` upon: starting a new search (`startSearching()`), disconnecting from GATT (`disconnectFromGatt()`), explicit teardown (`shutDown()`), and successful service discovery (`notifyStopSearching(true)`).<br>• `MyBTLEDevice` SHALL maintain a volatile `mIsShutDown` guard; disconnections arriving during or after `shutDown()` SHALL be ignored.<br>• When an active connection drops unexpectedly (`STATE_DISCONNECTED`), `MyBTLEDevice` SHALL NOT reconnect immediately with 0 ms delay. It SHALL schedule `startSearching()` via `mReconnectRunnable` with exponential backoff: base delay 1,000 ms, doubling upon consecutive search failures up to 16,000 ms (`MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS`), and resetting to 1,000 ms upon successful service discovery.<br>3. *Search Queue Device Integrity in `DeviceManager` (`REQ-CON-020.3`)*:<br>• In `DeviceManager.mSearchingStoppedForOneReceiver`, advancing the search queue (`searchForNextRemoteDevice()`) and modifying retry counters SHALL strictly execute ONLY if the event's `deviceID` matches the active target `cMyRemoteDeviceCurrentlySearchingFor.getDeviceId()`.<br>• Before invoking `searchForNextRemoteDevice()`, `cMyRemoteDeviceCurrentlySearchingFor` SHALL be cleared to `null`.<br>• Any `SEARCHING_STOPPED_FOR_ONE_INTENT` from a device ID not currently matching `cMyRemoteDeviceCurrentlySearchingFor` SHALL be logged and discarded without modifying `mSearchQueue` or popping the next device.<br>4. *ANT+ Handle Hygiene & DEAD State Recovery (`REQ-CON-020.4`)*:<br>• In `MyANTDevice.startSearching()`, `releaseAccess()` SHALL be invoked before requesting new access (`requestAccess()`), ensuring any stale `pccReleaseHandle` is cleanly closed.<br>• In `MyANTDevice.onDeviceStateChangeHandler(DeviceState.DEAD)`, `releaseAccess()` SHALL be invoked, `pccReleaseHandle` SHALL be set to `null`, `notifyStopSearching(false)` SHALL be ensured, and sensors unregistered without leaving dangling channel allocations.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-CON-020`, extending `REQ-CON-019` (`ATT-2773`). Targets `MyBTLEDevice.java`, `DeviceManager.java`, `MyANTDevice.java`, and peripheral drivers under `com.atrainingtracker.banalservice.devices`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4007`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, discovered during whole-app code review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`). `DeviceManager` and `MyBTLEDevice` were part of initial BLE/ANT+ architecture and lacked concurrency/lifecycle hardening for modern Android 13+ APIs.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Early BLE APIs on Android (API 18–32) passed `BluetoothGattCharacteristic` directly without byte arrays, and single-threaded looper assumptions obscured race conditions. In `DeviceManager`, `searchForNextRemoteDevice()` was placed outside the check under the assumption that `SEARCHING_STOPPED` would only fire for the active device.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Existing peripheral drivers (`BTLEHeartRateDevice`, `BTLEBikePowerDevice`, `BTLEBikeDevice`, `BTLERunSpeedDevice`), service discovery sequences, and pairing flows must continue to function with 100% fidelity. Clean-room test suite must pass completely.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a `MyBTLEDevice` receiving rapid BLE notifications,<br>• *When* the Bluetooth callback thread receives consecutive packets where the underlying characteristic byte array is mutated in place,<br>• *Then* the main-thread handler receives independent immutable byte snapshots matching each exact packet payload without data corruption.<br>• *Given* a connected BLE sensor that disconnects unexpectedly,<br>• *When* `onConnectionStateChange` receives `STATE_DISCONNECTED`,<br>• *Then* it cancels any prior timeout, schedules reconnection with initial 1,000 ms backoff, doubles backoff on successive disconnects up to 16,000 ms, and cancels all pending timeouts when shut down.<br>• *Given* `DeviceManager` actively searching for Device A with Device B queued in `mSearchQueue`,<br>• *When* a `SEARCHING_STOPPED_FOR_ONE_INTENT` arrives with `deviceID = C` (alien device),<br>• *Then* the event is discarded, `cMyRemoteDeviceCurrentlySearchingFor` remains Device A, and Device B is NOT popped from `mSearchQueue`.<br>• *Given* an active or failing ANT+ device transition to `DeviceState.DEAD`,<br>• *When* `onDeviceStateChangeHandler(DEAD)` executes,<br>• *Then* `pccReleaseHandle` is closed and nulled, preventing `DEVICE_ALREADY_IN_USE` errors on subsequent search.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero regression in peripheral drivers; single-thread Looper contract on `mHandler` preserved; 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Resilient Bluetooth LE & ANT+ reconnection, immutable telemetry dispatch, and queue integrity architecture. | `MyBTLEDevice.java`, `DeviceManager.java`, `MyANTDevice.java` | `TST-CON-012` | Verified |

ADD COLUMN`, `CREATE INDEX`).<br>• Heavy cross-database Data Manipulation Language (DML) routines (`migrateExistingWorkouts`, `migrateExtremaPositions`, `migrateSpatialBounds`, and `backfillAltitudeExtrema`) SHALL be excised from synchronous execution inside `onUpgrade`, ensuring database opening completes in $< 10\text{ ms}$ on any thread without blocking the UI or causing ANRs.<br>3. *Idempotent Background Backfill Architecture (`REQ-MIG-046.3`)*:<br>• The application SHALL provide an asynchronous, off-UI-thread backfill mechanism (`DatabaseBackfillManager` / `DatabaseBackfillWorker`).<br>• Each backfill operation SHALL be strictly idempotent and self-healing: `migrateSpatialBounds` queries and populates strictly rows `WHERE boundMinLat IS NULL AND mapPolyline IS NOT NULL AND mapPolyline != ''`; `migrateExtremaPositions` queries and populates strictly rows `WHERE latitude IS NULL AND extremaType != 'AVG'`; `migrateExistingWorkouts` queries and populates strictly rows `WHERE mapPolyline = '' OR distanceStream = ''`; `backfillAltitudeExtrema` queries and populates strictly clusters `WHERE min_alt_lat IS NULL`.<br>• The SQLite row state itself SHALL serve as the atomic source of truth. | **REQ-DAT-030** | **Google Drive Query Escaping, Encapsulated Account Cache, Atomic Download Staging & Transparent Scan Results.** | The system SHALL ensure secure query construction, account-isolated folder caching with self-healing re-creation, atomic download streaming, and transparent directory scans during Google Drive cloud operations (ATT-4014, refining `REQ-DAT-022`):<br>1. *Centralized Query Construction & Escaping (`GoogleDriveQueryBuilder`, `REQ-DAT-030.1`)*:<br>• `GoogleDriveQueryBuilder` SHALL provide `escapeQueryValue(value: String): String`, escaping backslashes (`\\`) and single quotes (`\'`) in strict accordance with Google Drive API v3 query syntax.<br>• `GoogleDriveQueryBuilder` SHALL construct search queries for folders (`buildFolderQuery`), files (`buildFileQuery`), and child entries (`buildChildrenQuery`).<br>• `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL route all search query generation exclusively through `GoogleDriveQueryBuilder`, eliminating raw string query assembly.<br>2. *Encapsulated, Thread-Safe, Account-Scoped Folder Cache (`GoogleDriveFolderCache`, `REQ-DAT-030.2`)*:<br>• `GoogleDriveFolderCache` SHALL encapsulate internal map storage and concurrency synchronization under a dedicated monitor lock.<br>• In production, `accountProvider` SHALL bind to `TrainingApplication.getGoogleDriveAccountEmail()`, ensuring the cache key remains stable across OAuth token refreshes. In headless test harnesses where `accountProvider` is omitted, the cache key SHALL derive from a token fingerprint; on token rotation, the cache for the client instance SHALL be cleanly cleared to prevent duplicate or stale entries.<br>• `GoogleDriveFolderCache` SHALL provide atomic eviction methods: `evictFolder(folderId: String)` (atomically removing all entries resolving to that folder ID) and `invalidateHierarchy(accountKey: String, folderNames: List<String>)`.<br>• `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL expose `evictFolder(folderId: String)` and `invalidateFolderHierarchy(folderNames: List<String>)` delegating to the encapsulated cache.<br>3. *Bounded Self-Healing Folder Re-Creation (`REQ-DAT-030.3`)*:<br>• In `GoogleDriveUploader.doExport()` and `GoogleDriveBackupManager`, if a file upload fails with HTTP 404 Not Found, the system SHALL evict the stale folder ID via `client.evictFolder(folderId)`.<br>• The upload process SHALL invoke `ensureFolderHierarchy` to recreate the remote folder and retry the upload exactly once (`maxAttempts = 1`), preventing infinite loops if permissions are missing. If the second attempt fails, the uploader SHALL return failure immediately.<br>4. *Atomic Download Staging, Durability Flush & Bounded 24h Orphan Cleanup (`REQ-DAT-030.4`)*:<br>• In `GoogleDriveClient.downloadFileById(fileId: String, destinationFile: File)`, download streams SHALL write to a temporary staging file (`.part_<timestamp>_<uuid>`) co-located in `destinationFile.parentFile` (guaranteeing same filesystem inode mount point).<br>• Before closing the output stream, the system SHALL invoke `FileOutputStream.fd.sync()` to durably flush file contents and inode metadata to non-volatile storage. If `fd.sync()` fails with `SyncFailedException` or `IOException`, the staging file SHALL be discarded and the download marked as failed.<br>• If `contentLength > 0`, the client SHALL verify that the temporary file length matches `contentLength`; mismatches SHALL trigger immediate abort and file deletion.<br>• Upon successful verification, the client SHALL atomically move the temporary file to `destinationFile` using `java.nio.file.Files.move` with `StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE` and `StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING`.<br>• If `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` or filesystem move failure occurs (e.g. non-POSIX external mount), the client SHALL fall back to `copyTo(destinationFile, overwrite = true)` followed by deleting the temporary file.<br>• If an exception or stream interruption occurs, the temporary file SHALL be deleted in a `finally` block, leaving `destinationFile` completely untouched.<br>• On download invocation, `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL lazily scan `destinationFile.parentFile` (bounded to at most 50 matching files to prevent I/O latency) and delete orphaned `.part_*` files older than 24 hours (`86_400_000L`).<br>5. *Transparent Recursive Directory Traversal (`RecursiveScanResult`, `REQ-DAT-030.5`)*:<br>• `GoogleDriveClient` SHALL provide `listFilesRecursivelyResult(folderId: String, extensions: List<String>): RecursiveScanResult`, where `RecursiveScanResult` exposes `val entries: List<DriveFileEntry>`, `val isComplete: Boolean`, and `val error: Exception? = null`.<br>• If an HTTP error or exception occurs on any page or subfolder, `isComplete` SHALL be false and `error` SHALL contain the failure exception, while accumulated entries remain available for diagnostic inspection.<br>• `listFilesRecursively` SHALL maintain backward compatibility by delegating to `listFilesRecursivelyResult`.<br>• `LegacyImportEngine` SHALL inspect `RecursiveScanResult.isComplete`; if false, it SHALL log a descriptive warning and update listener status without silently treating the directory as completely processed.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-DAT-030`, refining and extending `REQ-DAT-022` (*Google Drive Background Token Refresh, 401 Re-Authentication, Folder Hierarchy Resolution Resilience & Concurrency Synchronization*). Targets `GoogleDriveClient.kt`, `GoogleDriveUploader.kt`, `GoogleDriveBackupManager.kt`, and `LegacyImportEngine.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4014`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, discovered during independent whole-app architecture review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `globalFolderIdCache` and `hierarchyLock` were created in `REQ-DAT-022` (`ATT-2631`) to prevent concurrent WorkManager workers from creating duplicate folders. However, the cache key was account-agnostic and un-evictable, causing 404 errors on remote deletions or account switches. Query literals lacked escaping for quotes and backslashes, downloads were non-atomic, and directory scans swallowed errors.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Concurrency deduplication across workers under the same account is strictly preserved. In addition, queries with special characters execute reliably, cross-account leaks are eliminated, deleted folders recover self-healingly, file downloads are atomic with durability sync and 24h cleanup, and folder scans report errors transparently.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a folder or file name containing single quotes or backslashes (e.g. `"Runner's Track"`, `"Workouts\\2026"`),<br>• *When* `findFolderIdByName` or `findFileIdByName` executes,<br>• *Then* the generated query escapes quotes as `\'` and backslashes as `\\`, and the request succeeds with HTTP 200 without HTTP 400 Bad Request parse errors.<br>• *Given* Account A has resolved `"aTrainingTracker/Workouts"` to folder ID `"folder_a"`,<br>• *When* the user switches to Account B,<br>• *Then* `ensureFolderHierarchy` resolves a separate folder ID `"folder_b"` without returning `"folder_a"`.<br>• *Given* a previously cached Google Drive folder was deleted remotely,<br>• *When* `GoogleDriveUploader.doExport()` executes an upload and receives HTTP 404,<br>• *Then* the client evicts the stale folder ID, recreates the folder via `ensureFolderHierarchy`, and successfully uploads the file on the single retry.<br>• *Given* an active file download via `downloadFileById`,<br>• *When* the network connection drops or throws an `IOException` mid-stream,<br>• *Then* the partially written `.part_*` file is deleted, and `destinationFile` is never corrupted or left in a truncated state.<br>• *Given* a recursive folder scan encountering an HTTP error on page 2,<br>• *When* `listFilesRecursivelyResult` executes,<br>• *Then* `isComplete` is false, `error` contains the HTTP failure details, and `LegacyImportEngine` surfaces the incomplete status rather than masking it.<br><br>**Invariants**: Least-privilege `drive.file` scope, canonical v3 root folder creation (`parents` omitted), account-level concurrency deduplication, and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Ensure Google Drive query escaping, account-isolated cache with bounded 404 self-healing, atomic download staging with durability flush, and transparent recursive listing error reporting. | `GoogleDriveClient.kt`, `GoogleDriveUploader.kt`, `GoogleDriveBackupManager.kt`, `LegacyImportEngine.kt` | `TST-DAT-025` | Verified |
| **REQ-DAT-031** | **Atomic Concurrent-Safe Database Backup Snapshots, Storage Verification, and Singleton Helper Lifecycle.** | `BackupManager` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/migration/BackupManager.kt`), `DatabaseConnectionManager` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/migration/DatabaseConnectionManager.kt`), `StravaUploadDbHelper` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/exporter/db/StravaUploadDbHelper.java`), `EquipmentDbHelper` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/database/EquipmentDbHelper.java`), and `ActiveDevicesDbHelper` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/database/ActiveDevicesDbHelper.java`) SHALL guarantee that backup bundle creation generates atomic, consistent database snapshots without torn page reads or omitted WAL frames under active concurrent tracking writes, pre-verifies available filesystem storage before staging, executes SQLite `VACUUM INTO` on API 30+ without blocking concurrent writers, provides a writer-synchronized fallback checkpoint and retry mechanism on API 26–29, manages all SQLite open helpers as thread-safe singletons without connection or file descriptor leakage, verifies snapshot integrity prior to packaging, and cleans up staging directories on all exit paths (ATT-4011, extending `REQ-MIG-040`, `REQ-MIG-041`, and `REQ-MIG-043`):<br>1. *Storage Space Pre-Verification (`REQ-DAT-031.1`)*:<br>• Before snapshotting databases or initiating backup bundling, `BackupManager` SHALL calculate the sum of sizes of all active `.db` and `-wal` files.<br>• `BackupManager` SHALL assert that available filesystem storage in `context.filesDir.usableSpace` is at least 1.5 times the total database size (`totalDbSize * 1.5`).<br>• If usable space is insufficient, `createBackup()` SHALL log a warning, notify `ProgressListener` of the error, and abort cleanly returning `null` without partially allocating disk space or exhausting device storage.<br>2. *API 30+ Primary Snapshot Pipeline via `VACUUM INTO` (`REQ-DAT-031.2`)*:<br>• On Android 11+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R`), for each active database registered in `DatabaseConnectionManager`, `BackupManager` SHALL create an atomic standalone snapshot into an isolated temporary staging directory (`backups/temp_db_snapshot/`) using the SQLite statement `VACUUM INTO '<snapshot_file_path>'`.<br>• `VACUUM INTO` SHALL execute concurrently without holding exclusive application writer locks, guaranteeing that concurrent writer threads (`TrackerService`, `ExportWorker`) are not blocked.<br>• The produced snapshot file SHALL be an atomic, self-contained, defragmented, non-WAL SQLite database incorporating all committed transactions up to the snapshot instant.<br>3. *API 26–29 Fallback Snapshot Pipeline & Checkpoint Retry (`REQ-DAT-031.3`)*:<br>• On Android 8.0–10 (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.R`) or when storage is insufficient for `VACUUM INTO`, `BackupManager` SHALL execute a writer-synchronized checkpoint and copy pipeline: acquire `DatabaseConnectionManager.databaseLock` to prevent new write transactions from starting; execute `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)` on all active databases (retrying up to 3 times with exponential backoff if `BUSY` is returned); copy clean `.db` files and non-empty `-wal` files into staging; and release `DatabaseConnectionManager.databaseLock`.<br>4. *Thread-Safe Singleton Helper Lifecycle & Zero Leakage (`REQ-DAT-031.4`)*:<br>• `StravaUploadDbHelper`, `EquipmentDbHelper`, and `ActiveDevicesDbHelper` SHALL provide a thread-safe singleton accessor `getInstance(Context context)` using double-checked locking and binding to `context.getApplicationContext()`.<br>• All ad-hoc constructor instantiations across the codebase (`DatabaseConnectionManager.getActiveDatabases`, `LegacyImportEngine`, `WorkoutDeletionHelper`, `StravaUploader`, `TrackerService`, `StravaDataPurgeManager`) SHALL be eliminated and replaced with `getInstance(context)`.<br>• `DatabaseConnectionManager.getActiveDatabases` SHALL exclusively reference the singleton instances.<br>• Database helper singletons SHALL expose `@VisibleForTesting fun resetForTesting()` to ensure clean test isolation across unit test suites.<br>• Zero unmanaged or unclosed `SQLiteOpenHelper` instances SHALL be leaked during application lifecycle or backup execution.<br>5. *Snapshot Integrity Verification, Atomic Packaging & Cleanup (`REQ-DAT-031.5`)*:<br>• Before packaging, `BackupManager` SHALL verify each snapshot file in the staging directory using `PRAGMA integrity_check`, ensuring no corrupted or torn database files enter the backup archive.<br>• `BackupManager` SHALL archive the verified snapshot directory as the `databases/` tree inside `aTrainingTracker_backup.attbackup.tmp` alongside `shared_prefs` and `datastore`.<br>• The temporary backup file SHALL be atomically renamed to canonical `aTrainingTracker_backup.attbackup` using `Files.move(..., ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`.<br>• The temporary staging directory (`temp_db_snapshot/`) SHALL be strictly purged in a `finally` block on all execution paths (success, failure, or cancellation).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-DAT-031`, extending `REQ-MIG-040` (`ATT-3982`), `REQ-MIG-041` (`ATT-3989`), and `REQ-MIG-043` (`ATT-3992`). Targets `BackupManager.kt`, `DatabaseConnectionManager.kt`, `StravaUploadDbHelper.java`, `EquipmentDbHelper.java`, and `ActiveDevicesDbHelper.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4011`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, discovered during independent whole-app architecture review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`). `BackupManager.kt` was originally authored to zip the live `databases/` directory while excluding `-wal` files. Commit `f320b92b` (`ATT-3989`) introduced `quiesceAllDatabases`, but ignored `wal_checkpoint` return codes.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Direct zipping was written before WAL mode was pervasive across all databases. Filtering `-wal` files was intended to prevent copying ephemeral lock files (`-shm`), but did not account for uncheckpointed WAL frames or tearing from concurrent writers. `StravaUploadDbHelper`, `EquipmentDbHelper`, and `ActiveDevicesDbHelper` lacked singletons because early versions only accessed them infrequently from single threads.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: The `.attbackup` archive structure (`databases/`, `shared_prefs/`, `datastore/`) remains 100% backward and forward compatible. Full restore (`RestoreManager`) and incremental import (`AttachDatabaseHelper`) operate unchanged. Passive `onOpen()` behavior and 100% clean-room test pass rate are strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* available disk space in `filesDir` less than 1.5x total active database size,<br>• *When* `BackupManager.createBackup(context)` is called,<br>• *Then* backup generation aborts immediately, logs a warning, returns `null`, and allocates zero staging files.<br>• *Given* Android 11+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 30`) and active concurrent write transactions in progress on `WorkoutSamples.db`,<br>• *When* `createBackup(context)` executes,<br>• *Then* are blocked.<br>• *Given* Android 8.0–10 (`SDK_INT < 30`) and a database returning `BUSY` on the initial `wal_checkpoint(FULL)`,<br>• *When* `createBackup(context)` executes,<br>• *Then* it acquires `databaseLock`, retries the checkpoint with backoff, copies clean database files to staging, and releases `databaseLock`.<br>• *Given* multiple components accessing `StravaUploadDbHelper`, `EquipmentDbHelper`, and `ActiveDevicesDbHelper`,<br>• *When* calling `getInstance(context)` repeatedly across threads,<br>• *Then* exactly one shared instance is returned per helper class, and `DatabaseConnectionManager.getActiveDatabases(context)` creates zero new helper instances, eliminating SQLite connection leaks.<br>• *Given* a completed or aborted backup run,<br>• *When* `createBackup()` returns,<br>• *Then* `temp_db_snapshot/` is completely purged from disk on all execution paths.<br><br>**Invariants**: Archive format compatibility, API 26-35+ compatibility, passive onOpen(), and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Atomic concurrent-safe database backup snapshots via VACUUM INTO on API 30+, storage pre-verification, writer-synchronized fallback on API 26-29, = null` SHALL be exposed with a default parameter, preserving in-memory backward compatibility.<br>• In `SensorFieldView.kt`, `WPrimeBatteryGaugeBar` SHALL be rendered directly beneath the primary value and unit for `SensorType.W_PRIME_BAL` fields when `wPrimeBatteryState != null`.<br>• When `isWarning == true` ($W' < 20\%$), the tile's outline border SHALL switch to high-visibility Warning Red (`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error` / `TTColor.Zone5`), providing immediate biofeedback without touch interaction.<br>• In `TrackingViewModel.kt`, `wPrimeBatteryState` SHALL be computed in `applySensorData` using an immutable snapshot of `totalWPrimeKj` per 1-Hz frame, stamped with the frame timestamp.<br>• Progressive disclosure gating (`REQ-UI-409.3`) SHALL be strictly preserved: when `enableCriticalPowerModel == false`, the entire `W_PRIME_BAL` tile is excluded from `visibleFields` and row height collapses to 0.<br>5. *9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-UI-416.5`)*:<br>• All new UI strings (`w_prime_battery_pct` with format `%1$d%%`, `w_prime_warning_low_battery` e.g. `W\' Battery Low (<20%)`) SHALL exist across all 9 application locales (`values`, `values-de`, `values-es`, `values-fr`, `values-it`, `values-ja`, `values-nl`, `values-pl`, `values-pt`).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-UI-416`, extending `REQ-UI-399` (ATT-3862) and `REQ-UI-409` (ATT-3921). Targets `WPrimeBatteryState.kt`, `WPrimeBatteryMath.kt`, `WPrimeBatteryGaugeBar.kt`, `SensorFieldState.kt`, `SensorFieldView.kt`, `TrackingViewModel.kt`, `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SettingsDataStore.kt`, and `values*/strings.xml`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: `ATT-3862` (`61ccb801dc18`), `ATT-3921` (`a6289096638b`), `ATT-3106` (`REQ-UI-376`), and `ATT-3107` (`REQ-UI-377`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: While ATT-3862 introduced Skiba mathematical modeling and scalar Aftermath telemetry, the live cockpit tile only rendered scalar kJ numbers without an intuitive visual battery gauge, without percentage capacity, and without a low-battery color-coded warning alert.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Preservation of Skiba math formulas, 44-sensor catalog partition, `DB_VERSION = 13`, progressive disclosure gating (`REQ-UI-409.3`), True-Black AMOLED compliance, and 100% clean-room test pass rate.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active ride with power telemetry above Critical Power ($P > CP$),<br>• *When* 1-Hz metrics are computed in `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice`,<br>• *Then* $W'_{\text{bal}}$ depletes according to $(P - CP) \cdot 1\text{s}$, and the battery gauge fill fraction decreases accordingly.<br>• *Given* an active ride where power drops below Critical Power or during a pause,<br>• *When* 1-Hz metrics are computed,<br>• *Then* $W'_{\text{bal}}$ reconstitutes exponentially toward full capacity $W'$.<br>• *Given* remaining $W'$ dropping below $20\%$,<br>• *When* rendered in `SensorFieldView`,<br>• *Then* the battery gauge bar turns Red (`TTColor.Zone5`), and the card's border switches to Warning Red.<br>• *Given* telemetry sensor disconnection or missing power samples,<br>• *When* `WPrimeBatteryGaugeBar` is rendered,<br>• *Then* it maintains its fixed 14.dp height slot with dimmed track opacity (0.35 alpha) and empty fill, with zero layout jumping, transitioning to stale within $\le 3000\text{ ms}$.<br>• *Given* mid-session baseline parameter change of $CP$ or $W'$,<br>• *When* recalculating W' battery state,<br>• *Then* remaining balance is safely clamped to $[0.0, W'_{\text{new}}]$ and normalized without discontinuous exceptions.<br>• *Given* `enableCriticalPowerModel == false`,<br>• *When* `SensorGridScreen` evaluates visible fields,<br>• *Then* the `W_PRIME_BAL` tile is completely hidden and row height collapses to 0.<br><br>**Invariants**: Skiba differential math formulas, 44-sensor catalog partition, `DB_VERSION = 13`, progressive disclosure gating (`REQ-UI-409.3`), True-Black AMOLED compliance, and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Real-time W' Balance (W-Prime Battery) expenditure and recovery tracking, battery gauge bar with anti-clipping padding and fixed-height slot, and color-coded warning alert. | `WPrimeBatteryState.kt`, `WPrimeBatteryMath.kt`, `WPrimeBatteryGaugeBar.kt`, `SensorFieldState.kt`, `SensorFieldView.kt`, `TrackingViewModel.kt`, `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `SettingsDataStore.kt` | `TST-UI-379` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-037** | **Speed Sensor Standstill vs. In-Motion Signal Loss (Tunnel / Dropout) Discrimination in AutoPauseManager and Static Coupling Decoupling.** | `AutoPauseManager` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/tracker/AutoPauseManager.kt`) and `TrackerService` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/trainingtracker/tracker/TrackerService.java`) SHALL distinguish physical standstill from in-motion sensor loss based on the last recorded valid speed (`lastValidSpeedMps`), transitioning in-motion dropouts to `SENSOR_LOST` without pausing while debouncing decelerated standstill to `AUTO_PAUSED`, resetting `lastValidSpeedMps` on dynamic unpairing, and decoupling manual resume from static application state (ATT-4094, extending `REQ-TRK-018` and `REQ-TRK-028`):<br>1. *Stale Packet Speed Classification (`REQ-TRK-037.1`)*:<br>• In `AutoPauseManager.evaluateTick(...)`, when a speed source is registered (`hasSpeedSource == true`) and packet updates become stale (`isPacketStale == true`, delta > `STALE_PACKET_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000L`):<br>  - The system SHALL inspect the last recorded valid speed (`lastValidSpeedMps`).<br>  - If `lastValidSpeedMps != null && lastValidSpeedMps > resumeThresholdMps`: the athlete was in motion at high speed before packets ceased (e.g. tunnel entry, GPS multipath shadow, BLE wheel sensor dropout). `AutoPauseManager` SHALL transition to `AutoPauseState.SENSOR_LOST` (from `TRACKING` or `PAUSE_DEBOUNCE_PENDING`), log `auditLogEvent = "SENSOR_LOST_IN_MOTION_DROPOUT"`, and reset `debounceCounter = 0`. It SHALL NOT evaluate effective speed as `0.0 m/s` and SHALL NOT transition to `AUTO_PAUSED`.<br>  - If `lastValidSpeedMps == null || lastValidSpeedMps <= resumeThresholdMps`: the athlete decelerated to standstill or was already stationary before packet silence (e.g. traffic light stop). `AutoPauseManager` SHALL evaluate effective speed as `0.0 m/s`, advancing `debounceCounter` toward `AUTO_PAUSED` after `pauseDebounceSeconds`.<br>2. *Dynamic Sensor Unpairing & Disconnection Reset (`REQ-TRK-037.2`)*:<br>• When a speed sensor is dynamically unpaired, powered off, or disconnected mid-session such that `hasSpeedSource == false`: `AutoPauseManager` SHALL immediately transition to `SENSOR_LOST` (`auditLogEvent = "SENSOR_LOST_STALE_TTL_EXCEEDED"`).<br>• In addition, `AutoPauseManager` SHALL explicitly reset `lastValidSpeedMps = null` upon `!hasSpeedSource` or when reset via `setState(TRACKING)` / `setState(MANUAL_PAUSED)`, guaranteeing that stale historic speed values cannot linger across sensor unpairing or distinct workout sessions.<br>3. *Sensor Recovery Invariant (`REQ-TRK-037.3`)*:<br>• When in `SENSOR_LOST`, the engine SHALL require 2 consecutive fresh valid readings (`hasFreshValidReading == true`) to recover back to `TRACKING` (`auditLogEvent = "SENSOR_RECOVERED"`).<br>4. *Decoupled Manual Resume Method Signature (`REQ-TRK-037.4`)*:<br>• `AutoPauseManager.onManualResume(manualPauseLocked: Boolean = false)` SHALL accept `manualPauseLocked: Boolean` with `@JvmOverloads` defaulting to `false`, eliminating static access to `TrainingApplication.isManualPauseLocked()`.<br>• Callers in `TrackerService.java` (`notifyManualResume()`, `onStartCommand()` for `RESUME_BY_USER`, and `evaluateAutoPauseTick(...)`) SHALL explicitly pass `TrainingApplication.isManualPauseLocked()` to `onManualResume(...)`.<br>• When `manualPauseLocked == true` or `currentState == AutoPauseState.MANUAL_PAUSED`, `onManualResume` SHALL return immediately without modifying state.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-TRK-037`, extending `REQ-TRK-018` (`ATT-2642`) and `REQ-TRK-028` (`ATT-3984`). Targets `AutoPauseManager.kt`, `TrackerService.java`, and `AutoPauseManagerTest.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-4094`, Sprint `2026-42.10`, following Sprint `2026-42.9` code review of `ATT-3984` (commit `69e984f1`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ATT-3984` fixed the bug where auto-pause failed to trigger due to zero timestamps in `ProxySensor`, but unconditionally evaluated stale packets as `0.0 m/s`. This worked for standstill red lights, but caused false auto-pauses when cruising athletes entered tunnels or suffered temporary RF dropouts.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Standstill auto-pause debounce, 2-tick `SENSOR_LOST` recovery hysteresis, manual pause lock precedence, and 100% clean-room test pass rate strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete cruising at 8.0 m/s with `resumeThresholdMps = 1.0 m/s`,<br>• *When* speed packets stop arriving for > 5000 ms (e.g. entering a tunnel),<br>• *Then* `AutoPauseManager` transitions to `SENSOR_LOST` with audit event `"SENSOR_LOST_IN_MOTION_DROPOUT"` and does NOT enter `AUTO_PAUSED`.<br>• *Given* an athlete slowing down to 0.5 m/s ($\le resumeThresholdMps$),<br>• *When* speed packets stop arriving for > 5000 ms,<br>• *Then* `AutoPauseManager` evaluates effective speed as `0.0 m/s`, increments debounce counter, and transitions to `AUTO_PAUSED` after debounce expires.<br>• *Given* an active speed sensor mid-session,<br>• *When* the sensor is unpaired or powered off (`hasSpeedSource == false`),<br>• *Then* `AutoPauseManager` transitions to `SENSOR_LOST` and resets `lastValidSpeedMps` to `null`.<br>• *Given* `AutoPauseManager` in `AUTO_PAUSED` state,<br>• *When* `onManualResume(manualPauseLocked = true)` is invoked,<br>• *Then* the state remains `AUTO_PAUSED` without clearing debounce or recovery counters.<br>• *Given* `AutoPauseManager` in `AUTO_PAUSED` state,<br>• *When* `onManualResume(manualPauseLocked = false)` is invoked,<br>• *Then* the state transitions to `TRACKING` and debounce counters are reset.<br><br>**Invariants**: Standstill auto-pause debounce, 2-tick recovery hysteresis, thread synchronization, static decoupling, and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Distinguish speed sensor standstill from in-motion signal loss (tunnel/dropout) in AutoPauseManager based on last valid speed and decouple static pause lock check. | `AutoPauseManager.kt`, `TrackerService.java`, `AutoPauseManagerTest.kt` | `TST-TRK-030` | Verified |

| **REQ-UI-417** | **Distance Interval Filtering (Min/Max Range and Preset Intervals) in Routes and Favorite Routes.** | The system SHALL support bounded distance interval filtering ($[D_{\text{min}}, D_{\text{max}}]$ in meters) across Routes (`RouteFilterCriteria`, `RouteFilterBottomSheet`) and Favorite Routes / Workout Clusters (`ClusterFilterCriteria`, `ClusterFilterBottomSheet`), harmonizing filter mechanics with Workout filtering (`REQ-UI-157`):<br>1. *Immutable Criteria Domain Models (`RouteFilterCriteria.kt`, `ClusterFilterCriteria.kt`)*:<br>• `RouteFilterCriteria` and `ClusterFilterCriteria` SHALL declare property `val maxDistanceMeters: Double? = null` with default `null`.<br>• `activeFilterCount` in both models SHALL treat distance as a single active filter dimension if and only if `minDistanceMeters != null || maxDistanceMeters != null`. Setting both bounds SHALL NOT increment `activeFilterCount` by more than 1.<br>• In `RouteFilterCriteria.matches(route: RouteWithPath)`: The system SHALL evaluate `if (minDistanceMeters != null && route.summary.distance < minDistanceMeters) return false` and `if (maxDistanceMeters != null && route.summary.distance > maxDistanceMeters) return false`.<br>• In `ClusterFilterCriteria.matches(cluster: WorkoutCluster, linkedEquipment: Set<String>)`: The system SHALL evaluate `if (minDistanceMeters != null && cluster.refDistance < minDistanceMeters) return false` and `if (maxDistanceMeters != null && cluster.refDistance > maxDistanceMeters) return false`.<br>• Persistence & Backward Compatibility: `toJson()` in both models SHALL serialize `maxDistanceMeters` as a JSON number when non-null. `fromJson()` SHALL deserialize `maxDistanceMeters` safely if present in JSON. power spikes in Cycling Power frequency histograms into an aggregated rightmost overflow bar by default, provide interactive zoom navigation into a dedicated Sprint Tail view with independent local Y-axis scaling, provide a symmetric 2-segment header range toggle with consistent active segment highlighting and navigation affordances restoring the Main View, and snap the tail cutoff to an enclosing upper Power Zone boundary, while preserving linear binning for non-skewed rides and Heart Rate histograms (ATT-4293, ATT-4370, complementing `REQ-UI-372`, `REQ-UI-388`, and `REQ-UI-420`):<br>1. *Power Zone Boundary Snapping Tail Cutoff ($P_{99}$) in `TelemetryHistogramCalculator.kt` (`REQ-UI-419.1`)*:<br>• In `TelemetryHistogramCalculator.calculatePowerHistogram`, the system SHALL compute the cumulative active duration across frequency bins to locate the 99th percentile duration threshold ($P_{99}$): $P_{99} = \text{bin.rangeMax where } \sum_{i=0}^{k} d_i \ge 0.985 \times T_{\text{total}}$.<br>• The cutoff candidate SHALL be floored at the athlete's Zone 4 upper boundary (`thresholds.z4Max`) to guarantee that the full aerobic and threshold spectrum (Zones 1–4) remains permanently in the Main View: $\text{candidate} = \max(P_{99}, \text{thresholds.z4Max})$.<br>• The system SHALL snap the candidate cutoff upward to the enclosing upper Power Zone boundary (`thresholds.z4Max`, `thresholds.z5Max`, or `thresholds.z6Max`):<br>  - If $\text{candidate} \le \text{thresholds.z4Max}$: snap to `thresholds.z4Max`.<br>  - If $\text{thresholds.z4Max} < \text{candidate} \le \text{thresholds.z5Max}$: snap to `thresholds.z5Max`.<br>  - If $\text{thresholds.z5Max} < \text{candidate} \le \text{thresholds.z6Max}$: snap to `thresholds.z6Max`.<br>  - If $\text{candidate} > \text{thresholds.z6Max}$ (above Zone 6, into Zone 7) or if zone thresholds are unconfigured: fall back to rounding up to the nearest 50 W boundary: $\lceil \text{candidate} / 50 \rceil \times 50$.<br>• The snapped cutoff candidate SHALL be aligned to the histogram bin width: $\text{tailCutoff} = \lceil \text{rawCutoff} / \text{binWidth} \rceil \times \text{binWidth}$.<br>• Tail folding SHALL be gated and enabled if and only if: (a) $\text{dataMax} - \text{tailCutoff} \ge 10 \times \text{binWidth}$ ($\ge 100\text{ W}$ in the tail); (b) $\text{dataMax} \ge \text{tailCutoff} \times 1.25$; and (c) active duration above `tailCutoff` is strictly $> 0$.<br>• When gating conditions are not met or when calculating Heart Rate histograms (`calculateHeartRateHistogram`), the system SHALL return standard linear dataset (`tailCutoff = null`, `sprintTail = null`).<br>2. *Domain Model Extensions in `ZoneDistributionModels.kt` (`REQ-UI-419.2`)*:<br>• `TelemetryHistogramBin` SHALL declare `val isOverflow: Boolean = false` and `val isReturn: Boolean = false` with backward-compatible defaults.<br>• `TelemetryHistogramData` contain regular bins from `dataMin` to `tailCutoff` plus a single rightmost overflow bin (`isOverflow = true`, `rangeMin = tailCutoff`, `rangeMax = dataMax`, `durationSec = \sum_{P_i > \text{tailCutoff}} d_i`, `percentage = (\text{duration} / T_{\text{total}}) \times 100\%`, `zoneIndex = 5` or highest zone, `color = TTColor.Zone5`).<br>• The `sprintTail` dataset SHALL contain a single leftmost return bin (`isReturn = true`, `binIndex = 0`, `rangeMin = dataMin`, `rangeMax = tailCutoff`, `durationSec = \sum_{P_i \le \text{tailCutoff}} d_i`, `percentage = (\text{duration} / T_{\text{total}}) \times 100\%`, `color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outlineVariant`) plus all individual 10 W sprint bins from `tailCutoff` to `dataMax`.<br>3. *Symmetrical Two-Segment Header Range Toggle Navigation in `TelemetryHistogramChart.kt` (`REQ-UI-419.3`)*:<br>• `TelemetryHistogramChart` SHALL maintain reactive view state `var isSprintTailView by remember(histogram) { mutableStateOf(false) }`.<br>• The resting header readout SHALL render a symmetrical 2-segment range toggle alongside the resolution indicator (`Δ ${histogram.binWidth} $unit`), where the currently active range segment is consistently highlighted and the inactive range segment serves as the clickable view switch action:<br>  - In Main View (`!isSprintTailView`), Segment 1 (Main Range `${histogram.dataMin}–${histogram.tailCutoff} $unit`) SHALL be highlighted with `primaryContainer` (e.g. `primaryContainer.copy(alpha = 0.7f)`), bold text in `onPrimaryContainer`, and non-clickable; Segment 2 (Sprint Tail Range) SHALL be rendered as an unhighlighted clickable chip with `surfaceVariant` (e.g. `surfaceVariant.copy(alpha = 0.6f)`), text in `onSurfaceVariant`, and trailing forward Tapping Segment 2 or the rightmost overflow bar on the canvas SHALL set `isSprintTailView = true` and clear `selectedBinIndex`.<br>  - In Sprint Tail View (`isSprintTailView`), Segment 1 (Main Range) SHALL be rendered as an unhighlighted clickable chip with `surfaceVariant` (e.g. `surfaceVariant.copy(alpha = 0.6f)`), text in `onSurfaceVariant`, and leading back arrow icon (`Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack`), displaying localized string `power_histogram_return_label` (`${histogram.dataMin}–${histogram.tailCutoff} $unit`). Tapping Segment 1 or the leftmost return bar on the canvas SHALL set `isSprintTailView = false` and clear `selectedBinIndex`; Segment 2 (Sprint Tail Range `${histogram.tailCutoff}–${histogram.dataMax} $unit`) SHALL be highlighted with `primaryContainer` (e.g. `primaryContainer.copy(alpha = 0.7f)`), bold text in `onPrimaryContainer`, and non-clickable.<br>4. *Independent Y-Axis Scaling in Sprint Tail View (`REQ-UI-419.4`)*:<br>• In Sprint Tail View, vertical Y-axis scaling `maxDuration` SHALL be computed strictly across sprint bins (`filter { !it.isReturn }`), excluding the bulk duration of the return bar, elevating 3–15 second sprint efforts to full canvas height ($96\text{ dp}$).<br>• In Main View, `maxDuration` is computed across all visible bins (`bins.maxOfOrNull { it.durationSec }`), with the overflow bar rendered with a minimum visible height ($\ge 6\text{ dp}$).<br>5. *Bin Inspection & Drag Scrubbing Parity (`REQ-UI-419.5`)*:<br>• Tapping or dragging across regular bins in either view SHALL update `selectedBinIndex` and display that bin's exact wattage range, duration, percentage, and zone badge (`Z1`–`Z7`) in the header readout.<br>• Touching the overflow bar in Main View or return bar in Sprint Tail View immediately triggers the respective view transition without sticking in selected mode.<br>6. *9-Language Localization & Format Parity (`REQ-UI-419.6`)*:<br>• All `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` (`app/src/main/java/com/atrainingtracker/banalservice/devices/CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`) SHALL seed initial anaerobic capacity ($W'_{\text{bal}}$ in kJ) upon constructor instantiation to guarantee constructor state parity with `resetSession()` (Rule 51), while strictly gating $W'_{\text{bal}}$ sensor emissions (`mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue`) on the presence State Seeding Parity & Sensor-Presence Gating (`REQ-TRK-038.1` — Rule 51 & Rule 52)*:<br>• `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` constructors SHALL invoke `resetSession()` (or seed baseline capacity identically) upon instantiation, ensuring internal capacity state parity (Rule 51).<br>• When `resolveEffectiveCpWatts() > 0 && mWPrimeKjProvider.getWPrimeKj(mContext) > 0.0f`, internal accumulator null`. If and only if a power sensor is present, `mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue((double) wPrimeKj)` SHALL be published immediately on device creation (Rule 51). If no power sensor is present, `mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue(null)` SHALL be published (Rule 52), preventing `TrackerService` from recording phantom `W_PRIME_BAL` extrema.<br>• When $CP \le 0$ or $W' \le 0.0\text{f}$, `mCurrentWPrimeBalJoules` SHALL be initialized to `null` and `mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue(null)` emitted.<br>2. *Stationary & Paused W/kg Alignment (`REQ-TRK-038.2`)*:<br>• In `calculateMetrics()`, when `isSuspended == true` (Auto-Pause or Manual Pause), the engine SHALL retrieve instantaneous power (falling back to raw sensor data) and athlete weight `athleteWeightKg`.<br>• When `athleteWeightKg > 0.0f`: if `power != null && power >= 0.0`, the system SHALL publish `mPowerToWeightSensor.newValue(power / athleteWeightKg)`; if `power == null` and a power sensor is present, it SHALL publish `0.0`.<br>• When `athleteWeightKg <= 0.0f` (unconfigured), `mPowerToWeightSensor.newValue(null)` SHALL be published.<br>• Continuously updating `mPowerToWeightSensor` during pause prevents `TimedMovingAverageFilter` (3-second window) from starving and purging all samples, ensuring `W/kg (3 sec Ø)` displays `0.0 W/kg` (or `0,0 W/kg`) alongside `0 W` instead of expiring to `-- W/kg`.<br>3. *Transient Dropout Resilience for W'bal & Cumulative Metrics (`REQ-TRK-038.3`)*:<br>• In `calculateMetrics()`, when `power == null || Double.isNaN(power) || Double.isInfinite(power) || power < 0.0` during an active non-suspended session, the engine SHALL NOT publish `null` to `mWPrimeBalSensor`, `mNormalizedPowerSensor`, `mIntensityFactorSensor`, or `mTssSensor`.<br>• The engine SHALL preserve the existing session values and return early before integrating mechanical work or pushing into `mPowerWindow30s`.<br>• During transient RF/BLE packet dropouts ($\le 3\text{ seconds}$), $W'_{\text{bal}}$ and cumulative metrics remain preserved, allowing `TrackingViewModel`'s `wPrimeStaleJob` (`STALE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000L`) to govern UI staleness gracefully without visual flickering or instantaneous gauge collapse.<br>4. *Cumulative Metric Pause Invariant & Suspended W'bal Reconstitution Gating (`REQ-TRK-038.4` — Rule 52)*:<br>• While `isSuspended == true`, Normalized Power (NP), Mechanical Work (kJ), Intensity Factor (IF), and Training Stress Score (TSS) SHALL remain strictly gated and SHALL NOT accumulate, integrate work, or advance FIFO samples.<br>• $W'_{\text{bal}}$ exponential reconstitution at $P = 0.0\text{ W}$ during pause SHALL execute and publish to `mWPrimeBalSensor` if and only if `mCurrentWPrimeBalJoules != null` AND `mMySensorManager != null && mMySensorManager.getSensor(SensorType.POWER) != null` (Rule 52).<br>5. *Aftermath Presentation Defense & DTO Mapping Symmetry (`REQ-TRK-038.5` — Rule 20 & Rule 52)*:<br>• In `WorkoutDataMapper.kt`, `resolveWPrimeBalSummary()` SHALL accept `hasPowerData: Boolean` and evaluate `if (!hasPowerData) return Triple(null, null, false)`.<br>• `hasPowerData` SHALL be evaluated as `(avgPowerWatts != null && avgPowerWatts > 0.0) || (maxPowerWatts != null && maxPowerWatts > 0.0)`.<br>• Both single-row `fromCursor()` and batch `fromSnapshot()` mapping pathways SHALL resolve `hasPowerData` identically, enforcing Rule 20 DTO symmetry.<br>• In `WorkoutDetails.kt`, `AnaerobicBatteryRow` SHALL be rendered if and only if `data.minWPrimeBalKj != null && data.minWPrimeBalPct != null`, ensuring non-power workouts omit the row and preceding divider completely, while preserving the modularity budget of `WorkoutDetails.kt` strictly below 500 lines.<br>6. *9-Language Localization & Format Parity (`REQ-TRK-038.6`)*:<br>• Existing telemetry strings (`power_to_weight`, `power_to_weight_short`, `units_power_to_weight`, `w_prime_battery_pct`, `w_prime_warning_low_battery`, `workout_w_prime_min_kj_label`, `workout_w_prime_min_pct_label`) across all 9 application locales (`values/`, `values-de/`, `values-es/`, `values-fr/`, `values-it/`, `values-ja/`, `values-nl/`, `values-pl/`, `values-pt/`) SHALL remain 100% defined and uncorrupted, with zero new string resources required.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines `REQ-TRK-038.1` (*Constructor State Seeding Parity (Rule 51)*, introduced in `ATT-4283`). Targets `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice.java`, `CyclingPowerMetricsDeviceTest.kt`, `WorkoutDataMapper.kt`, `WorkoutDataMappingSymmetryTest.kt`, and `WorkoutDetails.kt`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Introduced in Sprint 2026-43.1 via commit `a4e878f5` (`fix(ATT-4283): Seed initial W'bal capacity on startup and align W/kg & W'bal behavior when stationary or paused`). Refined in Sprint 2026-43.2 (`ATT-4368`) after physical device verification revealed phantom W'bal rows on non-power workouts.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: In `ATT-4283`, `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` was updated because unit tests had been masking an uninitialized `mCurrentWPrimeBalJoules = null` state on device startup. When instantiated in production for a power ride, the live cockpit battery gauge rendered empty (`--%` / `-- kJ`) until the first power packet arrived. `REQ-TRK-038.1` mandated calling `resetSession()` and publishing `mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue((double) wPrimeKj)` immediately on device creation so that the cockpit gauge renders full 100% capacity from second zero. However, `BANALService` instantiates `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` across all sports, and fallback CP (200W) and fallback W' (20.0 kJ) are always non-zero, causing `mWPrimeBalSensor.newValue(...)` to be published unconditionally without checking for a power meter, which injected phantom `20.0 kJ` extrema into `TrackerService`'s database for every workout.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Rule 51 internal seeding parity preserved (internal accumulator `mCurrentWPrimeBalJoules` is seeded so initial capacity is ready immediately upon power meter connection); Rule 52 sensor-presence gating enforced (virtual sensor `mWPrimeBalSensor` only publishes non-null when `SensorType.POWER` is registered); Rule 20 DTO mapping symmetry preserved across `fromCursor` and `fromSnapshot`; legacy `CyclingPowerMetricsDevice` instantiated when `SensorType.POWER` IS registered in `MySensorManager`, with effective $CP = 280\text{ W}$ and $W' = 20.0\text{ kJ}$,<br>• *When* the constructor completes,<br>• *Then* `wPrimeBalSensor.sensorData.value` immediately emits `20.0` (kJ) and the internal balance is seeded with `20000.0` Joules (Rule 51).<br>• *Given* an active ride entering Auto-Pause (`isSuspended == true`) with an athlete weighing $75.0\text{ kg}$ and power sensor reporting $0\text{ W}$,<br>• *When* `calculateMetrics()` executes,<br>• *Then* `powerToWeightSensor` emits `0.0` W/kg, preventing `TimedMovingAverageFilter` from expiring to `null` (`"-- W/kg"`).<br>• *Given* an active ride where power temporarily drops to `null` for 1 second (e.g. transient BLE packet loss),<br>• *When* `calculateMetrics()` executes,<br>• *Then* `wPrimeBalSensor`, `normalizedPowerSensor`, `intensityFactorSensor`, and `tssSensor` retain their current session values and do NOT publish `null`.<br>• *Given* a workout without recorded power data (`avgPower == null && maxPower == null`), even if legacy `W_PRIME_BAL` extrema exists in SQLite,<br>• *When* mapped via `WorkoutDataMapper.fromCursor` or `WorkoutDataMapper.fromSnapshot`,<br>• *Then* `minWPrimeBalKj` and `minWPrimeBalPct` evaluate to `null` symmetrically (Rule 20).<br>• *Given* a workout without recorded power data rendered in `WorkoutDetails`,<br>• *When* sections are constructed,<br>• *Then* `AnaerobicBatteryRow` is omitted and no duplicate or stray dividers are rendered.<br>• *Given* a workout with recorded power data (`avgPower > 0.0`),<br>• *When* mapped and rendered in `WorkoutDetails`,<br>• *Then* `AnaerobicBatteryRow` is rendered normally displaying `Min X kJ (Y%)`.<br><br>**Invariants**: Rule 51 constructor parity, Rule 52 sensor-presence gating, Rule 20 DTO mapping symmetry, Skiba differential equation preservation, pause accumulation gating, engine (`BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java`) SHALL declare `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` bounded to Android 8.0 through Android 11 (API 26–30), verify `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` permission alongside `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` application crashes (ATT-3997, extending `REQ-CON-019`):<br>1. *Manifest Permission Declaration (`REQ-CON-021.1`)*:<br>• In `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, the system SHALL declare `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.BLUETOOTH_ADMIN" android:maxSdkVersion="30" />`.<br>• The declaration SHALL be active (not commented out), ensuring that devices running Android 8.0 through Android 11 obtain install-time Bluetooth admin authorization required by the framework Bluetooth service for BLE discovery, while modern devices running Android 12+ (API 31+) ignore it in favor of runtime `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` without triggering Google Play Store policy warnings.<br>2. *Legacy Permission Guard in Search Engine (`REQ-CON-021.2`)*:<br>• In `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.startAsyncSearch()`, when executing on Android versions below API 31 (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.S`), the engine SHALL explicitly verify both `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` and `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` via `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission`.<br>• If either `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` or `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` is not granted (`!= PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED`), the engine SHALL log a descriptive warning (`Log.w`), abort execution before calling `scanner.startScan(...)`, and ensure `scanning` remains `false`.<br>3. *Defensive Scan Execution & Lifecycle State Restoration (`REQ-CON-021.3`)*:<br>• In `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.startAsyncSearch()`, the call to `scanner.startScan(filters, settings, mScanCallback)` SHALL be wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (SecurityException | IllegalStateException e)` block.<br>• In the event of a `SecurityException` or `IllegalStateException`, the engine SHALL log an error with the exception details, restore `scanning = false`, and return cleanly without crashing the caller thread or permanently locking the engine out of subsequent scan attempts.<br>4. *Defensive Scan Teardown (`REQ-CON-021.4`)*:<br>• In `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.stopAsyncSearch()`, the call to `scanner.stopScan(mScanCallback)` SHALL be wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (SecurityException | IllegalStateException e)` block.<br>• If the platform throws an exception during teardown (e.g., Bluetooth adapter disabled or permissions revoked mid-scan), the engine SHALL log a warning, ensure `scanning = false` is maintained, and proceed to invoke `resetTrackingState()` cleanly.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement `REQ-CON-021`, extending and refining `REQ-CON-019` (`ATT-2773`). Targets `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` and `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-3997`, Sprint `2026-43.1`. Discovered during independent whole-app code review of `feature/ATT-3921` (`0234bfc0`). `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` was present in Initial Commit (`845818c2`, 2019) and was commented out in commit `f2f55e11cf48` ("feat: Android permissions", July 26, 2024). Ticket `ATT-2773` (`REQ-CON-019`) introduced Android 12 permissions and `TRANSPORT_LE` but omitted legacy `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` verification and scan exception guards.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Commit `f2f55e11cf48` commented out `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` under the erroneous assumption that modern `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` superseded it globally across all Android versions. On API $\le 30$, `BluetoothLeScanner.startScan` strictly enforces `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` at the framework Binder boundary. Furthermore, `startScan()` and `stopScan()` omitted defensive exception handling under the assumption that pre-flight permission checks would prevent all platform runtime exceptions.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Android 12+ runtime permission model (`BLUETOOTH_SCAN`, `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`) remains strictly intact (`REQ-CON-019`); existing BLE peripheral drivers (`BTLEHeartRateDevice`, `BTLEBikePowerDevice`, `BTLEBikeDevice`, `BTLERunSpeedDevice`) remain 100% untouched; search engine lifecycle state consistency (`scanning` flag) is preserved; and clean-room full test suite pass rate remains 100%.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an Android 8.0–11 device (API 26–30) with `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` declared with `maxSdkVersion="30"` in `AndroidManifest.xml`,<br>• *When* the application is installed and executed,<br>• *Then* `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` is granted at install time without runtime prompt and without triggering Google Play Store policy warnings on API 31+.<br>• *Given* an Android 8.0–11 device where `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` is not granted,<br>• *When* `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.startAsyncSearch()` executes,<br>• *Then* the method logs a warning, aborts cleanly before calling `scanner.startScan()`, and leaves `scanning = false`.<br>• *Given* an Android 8.0–11 device where `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` is not granted,<br>• *When* `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.startAsyncSearch()` executes,<br>• *Then* the method logs a warning, aborts cleanly before calling `scanner.startScan()`, and leaves `scanning = false`.<br>• *Given* a running `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine` where `scanner.startScan(...)` throws `SecurityException` or `IllegalStateException`,<br>• *When* `startAsyncSearch()` executes,<br>• *Then* the exception is caught and logged, `scanning` is restored to `false`, and subsequent calls to `startAsyncSearch()` are not blocked by the `already searching` guard.<br>• *Given* an active scan where `scanner.stopScan(...)` throws `SecurityException` or `IllegalStateException`,<br>• *When* `stopAsyncSearch()` executes,<br>• *Then* the exception is caught and logged, `scanning` is set to `false`, and `resetTrackingState()` executes cleanly.<br>• *Given* an Android 12+ device (API 31+) with `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` granted,<br>• *When* `startAsyncSearch()` executes,<br>• *Then* scanning proceeds using low-latency aggressive scan settings without requiring `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN`.<br><br>**Invariants**: Android 8–11 compatibility (API 26–30), Android 12+ permission boundaries (`REQ-CON-019`), search engine lifecycle state consistency (`scanning` flag), zero regression in existing BLE peripheral drivers, and 100% clean-room test pass rate. | Restore BLUETOOTH_ADMIN with maxSdkVersion="30" in AndroidManifest.xml for Android 8–11 compatibility, verify BLUETOOTH_ADMIN before scan on API < 31, and wrap startScan/stopScan in defensive exception handling to prevent search lockups. | `AndroidManifest.xml`, `BTSearchForNewDevicesEngine.java` | `TST-CON-021` | Verified |

| **REQ-PRI-006** | **Decoupled Multi-Permission Cascade, Contextual Bluetooth & Notification Gating, Sensor Discovery Permission Handling, and Legacy Code Retirement.** | The system SHALL decouple runtime permission evaluation so that fine location (`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`), notification (`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` on API 33+), and Bluetooth connect (`BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` on API 31+) are checked independently via dedicated predicates (`checkHasLocation()`, `checkHasNotification()`, `checkHasBluetoothConnect()`), rather than gating the entire rationale flow strictly on `!checkHasLocation()`, SHALL contextually prompt for missing notification or Bluetooth permissions when location is already granted, SHALL gate sensor search and scanning on Bluetooth permissions just-in-time, SHALL retire dead legacy permission methods from `MainActivityWithNavigation.kt`, and SHALL maintain 100% 9-language localization parity (ATT-3998, refining `REQ-PRI-003`):<br>1. *Decoupled Permission Check Predicates (`ControlTrackingScreen.kt`, `REQ-PRI-006.1`)*:<br>• `ControlTrackingScreen.kt` SHALL define granular, decoupled permission check lambdas: `checkHasLocation`, `checkHasNotification` (API 33+), `checkHasBluetoothConnect` (API 31+), and `checkHasBluetoothScan` (API 31+).<br>• Missing notifications or Bluetooth permissions SHALL NOT be shadowed or bypassed by location permission being already granted.<br>2. *Decoupled Multi-Step Cascade for Workout Start (`REQ-PRI-006.2`)*:<br>• When the athlete taps Start (`handleStartClick`):<br>  - If `!checkHasLocation()`: the system SHALL present `RationaleStep.FOREGROUND` (requesting Location, Notifications on API 33+, and Bluetooth on API 31+).<br>  - If `checkHasLocation()` is `true`: the system SHALL evaluate `proceedAfterPermissions()`:<br>    a. If `!checkHasNotification()` (Android 13+) and notification permission has not yet been requested or dismissed in the current session: the system SHALL present `RationaleStep.NOTIFICATION` (or request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`).<br>    b. If paired Bluetooth sensors are registered (`hasPairedBluetoothSensors == true`) and `!checkHasBluetoothConnect()` (Android 12+): the system SHALL present `RationaleStep.BLUETOOTH` (or request `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`).<br>    c. If the athlete declines or dismisses notification or Bluetooth prompts ("Not Now"), the system SHALL gracefully advance to the next step without blocking workout tracking.<br>    d. If `!checkHasBackgroundLocation()` (Android 11+): the system SHALL present `RationaleStep.BACKGROUND_LOCATION`.<br>    e. If `!checkIsIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()`: the system SHALL present `RationaleStep.BATTERY_OPTIMIZATION`.<br>    f. When all required/un-dismissed steps are satisfied: the system SHALL execute `onStart()`.<br>3. *Just-in-Time Bluetooth Permissions for Sensor Discovery (`REQ-PRI-006.3`)*:<br>• In `ControlTrackingScreen.kt` (`ResearchButton` / `onSearch`): when tapped, the system SHALL check whether Bluetooth permissions are granted (`BLUETOOTH_SCAN` and `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` on API 31+; `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` and `BLUETOOTH_ADMIN` on API < 31); if missing, it SHALL launch the permission request launcher rather than dispatching search blindly.<br>• In `DevicesTabbedScreen.kt`: before initiating BLE scanning or pairing scans for `Protocol.BLUETOOTH_LE`, the system SHALL verify Bluetooth scan permission; if missing, it SHALL request permission contextually, and if denied, display `bluetooth_permission_scan_required` with action `grant_permission` rather than running a silent dead search.<br>4. *Start Button Warning Badge Synchronization (`REQ-PRI-006.4`)*:<br>• The warning indicator on `ControlTrackingButton` SHALL evaluate to `true` whenever: Precise Location is missing (`!hasLocationPermission`), OR battery optimization exemption is missing (`!isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations`), OR paired Bluetooth sensors exist but Bluetooth connect permission is missing (`hasPairedBluetoothSensors && !hasBluetoothPermission`).<br>5. *Legacy Permission Dead Code Retirement (`REQ-PRI-006.5`)*:<br>• Obsolete methods `getPermissions()`, `getPermissions(popup: Boolean)`, `onRequestPermissionsResult`, and `showBackgroundLocationDialog()` in `MainActivityWithNavigation.kt` SHALL be completely removed, and `MainActivityStartupPermissionContractTest.kt` SHALL retire the reflection assertion while preserving cold-start freedom and location safety.<br>6. *Full 9-Language Localization Parity (`REQ-PRI-006.6`)*:<br>• All new string resources (`bluetooth_permission_scan_required`, `grant_permission`, `permission_rationale_notification_subtitle`, `permission_rationale_bluetooth_subtitle`) SHALL be localized with 100% parity across EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Refines and supersedes `REQ-PRI-003` (*Contextual Just-in-Time Permission Flow, Zero-Friction Cold Start, Background Location Escalation, Battery Optimization Exemption & Graceful Settings Return Handling*) and test specification `TST-PRI-002`. permission integration and `MainActivityWithNavigation` kept dead legacy methods.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Zero cold-start popups (`REQ-PRI-003`), strict fine location requirement (`REQ-PRI-004`), Android 11+ two-step background location cascade, fail-safe OEM battery optimization handling (`REQ-PRI-005`), Android 8–11 BLE compatibility (`REQ-CON-021`, ATT-3997), and 100% full test suite pass rate remain strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete on Android 13+ with location already granted but notifications missing,<br>• *When* tapping Start on `ControlTrackingScreen`,<br>• *Then* `checkHasNotification() == false` is detected and notification rationale/prompt is presented.<br>• *Given* an athlete on Android 12+ with location granted and paired BLE sensors but Bluetooth missing,<br>• *When* tapping Start,<br>• *Then* `checkHasBluetoothConnect() == false` is detected and Bluetooth rationale/prompt is presented.<br>• *Given* an athlete dismissing notification or Bluetooth rationale with "Not Now",<br>• *When* dismissed,<br>• *Then* the cascade proceeds to background location / battery optimization / tracking start without blocking.<br>• *Given* an athlete lacking fine location,<br>• *When* tapping Start,<br>• *Then* `RationaleStep.FOREGROUND` is presented with the full onboarding permission permission is requested and, if denied, `bluetooth_permission_scan_required` is displayed with `grant_permission` action.<br>• *Given* `MainActivityWithNavigation`,<br>• *When* inspected,<br>• *Then* eagerly updated from `dataStore.data`.<br>• `SettingsDataStore` SHALL expose non-blocking $O(1)$ synchronous getters `getZoneMaxSync(zoneType: ZoneType, zoneIndex: Int): Int`, `getFtpSync(): Int?`, `getAthleteWeightKgSync(): Float`, `getCpWattsSync(): Int?`, and `getWPrimeKjSync(): Float?`.<br>• Unused dead code `SettingsDataStore.getSummary(zoneType)` calling `runBlocking` SHALL be completely `getZoneDisplayOptions`, `getTuningConfig`, `getGpsAccuracyThreshold`, `getAltitudeFilterWindow`, `getSlopeMinSpeed`, `getFtp`, `isAutoPauseEnabled`, `getAutoPauseSpeedThresholdKmh`, `getAutoPauseDebounceSec`, `getAutoPauseConfig`, `getAthleteWeightKg`, `getCpWatts`, `getEffectiveCpWatts`, `getWPrimeKj`, `getEffectiveWPrimeKj`) SHALL read directly from the singleton in-memory caches of `SettingsDataStore` and `TuningPreferencesDataStore` without calling `runBlocking` or `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO)`.<br>• `SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper.setAthleteWeightKg(context, weightKg)` SHALL dispatch asynchronously onto `appScope.launch` instead of parking the caller thread via `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO)`.<br>• All public static method signatures in `SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper` SHALL remain 100% backward-compatible, ensuring that existing unit tests utilizing `mockkStatic(SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper::class)` (`TelemetryZoneMathTest`, `SpeedAndLocationDeviceDecayTest`,
